rule: Features are only ever added, or have passes flipped to true with evidence recorded in PROGRESS.md. Never delete, reword or weaken a feature once this file is committed.

features.title: Handle rules: one shared normalize-and-validate function
acceptance: Vitest (pnpm test): normalizeHandle lowercases and drops every character outside a-z, 0-9 and '-': 'Mara_Studio!' -> 'marastudio', 'MARA' -> 'mara', ' ma ra ' -> 'mara', 'mará' -> 'mar', 'a.b' -> 'ab'. It never truncates.
validateHandle returns 'short' for 0-2 characters ('', 'ab', 'a-') and this check runs before every other rule.

validateHandle returns 'ok' for exactly 30 characters ('a' x 30) and for 3-character values ('abc', 'a-b', '123'), and 'too_long' for 31 characters. The 30-character cap is a build assumption (the docs set no maximum; a DNS label allows 63), so it is asserted explicitly here.

validateHandle returns 'invalid' for a leading or trailing dash ('-mara', 'mara-') and for any value starting 'xn--' ('xn--pple-43d'), because punycode labels render as lookalike Unicode names (phishing risk on open signup). 'ma-ra' is 'ok'.

The module has no server-only imports: a Vitest test imports it in a jsdom environment (as the client signup form will) and in a node environment (as server actions will) with no error. Reserved and taken are not decided here, because the browser cannot read reserved_handles; the availability endpoint feature covers them.

features.title: Handle availability endpoint (available, reserved, taken, short, too long, invalid)
acceptance: GET http://app.localhost:3000/api/handles/check?handle=mara returns 200 with JSON {handle: 'mara', status: 'taken'} (mara is the seeded tenant).

?handle=www, ?handle=app, ?handle=api and ?handle=ADMIN return status 'reserved' (the value is normalized first, so ADMIN comes back as handle 'admin'); the reserved set comes from the reserved_handles table, not a hard-coded list.

?handle=ab, ?handle= and a missing handle param return 'short'; 31 'a' characters return 'too_long'; ?handle=-mara and ?handle=xn--pple-43d return 'invalid'; ?handle=zq-avail-1 returns 'available'. Precedence is short, too_long, invalid, reserved, taken.
Live data: after a pages row with handle 'zq-avail-1' is inserted with the secret key, the same request returns 'taken'; after that row is deleted it returns 'available' again.
Response contains only the keys handle and status, has Cache-Control: no-store, and POST returns 405.

Abuse case (direct PostgREST, publishable key): GET {SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/reserved_handles?select=* with no JWT and again as a signed-in authenticated user returns 401/403 or an empty array; GET /rest/v1/pages?select=handle returns only the caller's own rows (empty for no JWT and for a user with no page). The endpoint is the only route to availability and leaks nothing beyond the status.
Host scoping: http://mara.localhost:3000/api/handles/check?handle=zz and http://localhost:3000/api/handles/check?handle=zz both return 404.

features.title: Log in page and email sign-in link request (no password)
acceptance: Signed out, http://app.localhost:3000/login uses the Signup layout (charcoal brand panel plus form column) with h1 'Log in', an Email field, primary button 'Email me a sign-in link', divider 'or', secondary 'Continue with Google', and 'New here? Create your page' linking to /signup. There is no handle field and no password field anywhere on /login or /signup. The page has no mockup of its own; derive it from Signup.dc.html.

Submitting e2e-login-1@example.com replaces the form with a sent state: heading 'Check your email', text 'We emailed a sign-in link to e2e-login-1@example.com.', a 'Use a different email' button (returns to the form, field cleared and focused) and a 'Resend link' button that is disabled with a countdown ('Resend in 60s', verified with page.clock) and enabled at 0. Exactly one message reaches the local Supabase mail inbox (address from `supabase status`) within 10 s.

The email: subject 'Your HYDLNK sign-in link'; HTML and plain-text parts; one primary link labelled 'Sign in to HYDLNK' whose href starts with http://app.localhost:3000/auth/callback and is not a supabase.co verify URL; body says the link works once and expires in 1 hour, plus 'If you didn’t ask for this, ignore this email.'; no exclamation marks; the HTML has no fixed width above 600px and the link button is at least 44px tall.

The committed magic-link template is referenced from supabase/config.toml. The cross-browser callback feature depends on this template, so the template change is part of this work. Production needs the same template applied by Gary through the release step; until then production links only work in the browser that requested them.
No account enumeration: an address with no account ('never-seen-1@example.com') gets the identical sent state and copy, and also receives an email, same as an existing address.

Invalid input ('' and 'not-an-email') shows 'Enter a valid email address.' under the field (role='alert'), sends no request to the server action, and returns focus to the field. Vitest: the shared email Zod schema rejects 'a@b', 'a b@c.com' and any string over 254 characters.

Rate limits: a second request for the same address within 60 s shows 'You can request another link in a minute.' (not the raw Supabase error text). Local supabase/config.toml [auth.rate_limit] email_sent is raised so 20 requests to 20 different addresses within an hour all deliver, letting the e2e suite run repeatedly.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/login: document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= 390, every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide), the brand panel is a slim charcoal bar with only the logo, inputs compute to font-size >= 16px, and the sent state fits without horizontal scroll.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: two columns with the charcoal panel left and a form column of max-width 400px, primary button 48px tall, and the sent state replaces the form in the same column.

features.title: Auth callback signs in from the emailed link in any browser
acceptance: Opening the emailed link in the same Playwright context ends on http://app.localhost:3000/ (default landing; routed onward by the auth gate feature) with a session cookie set; GET {SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/user with that cookie's access token returns the signed-in email, and a reload keeps the session.

Opening a second fresh link in a brand-new browser context (no cookies, simulating a phone mail app that opens a different browser than the one that requested the link) also signs in. This requires the token-hash style link from the login feature's template verified by the callback, not a PKCE code-verifier cookie.

A link that was already used and a link with one character of its token altered both end on http://app.localhost:3000/login?error=link_invalid showing 'That sign-in link expired or was already used. Request a new one.' above the email form: HTTP 200, no session cookie set, no 500. Vitest: the callback maps the verify errors otp_expired and invalid token to that same redirect.
GET http://app.localhost:3000/auth/callback with no parameters redirects to /login.

Open-redirect abuse: a valid callback URL with an added next=https://evil.example, next=//evil.example, next=/\evil.example, next=javascript:alert(1) or redirect_to=https://evil.example always ends on http://app.localhost:3000/. No request parameter ever controls the destination.
/auth/callback is served on the app host only; http://localhost:3000/auth/callback and http://mara.localhost:3000/auth/callback return 404.

Test helper for every later signed-in spec: a Playwright fixture signInAs(email) creates the user if needed, generates a sign-in link with the secret key (Supabase auth admin generateLink), opens it through /auth/callback and saves storageState, so later specs sign in without reading the inbox. A smoke spec proves it yields a signed-in session for the seeded user mara in both Playwright projects.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/login?error=link_invalid: document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= 390, every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide), and the error text sits above the form in #B23A2B without overflow.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the error notice appears inside the form column above the Email field.

features.title: Account row is created server-side on first sign-in
acceptance: After a brand-new address (e2e-acct-1@example.com) completes the callback, exactly one accounts row exists with id equal to that auth user's id, plan 'free', stripe_customer_id null and suspended_at null (read with the secret-key client).

Idempotent: sign out, request and open another link for the same address and there is still exactly one row with unchanged values (a plan set to 'pro' with the secret key is not reset). Two concurrent calls of the ensure-account function for one user produce one row and no error (Vitest integration).
Self-healing: delete that row with the secret key, then load any signed-in app page; the row is recreated with plan 'free'.
The row is written only by server-only code using the secret key, and the user id comes from the verified session, never from request input.

Abuse case (direct PostgREST, publishable key plus the user's JWT, role authenticated): POST /rest/v1/accounts with {id: <own id>, plan: 'studio'} is rejected (401/403, code 42501) and creates no row; PATCH /rest/v1/accounts?id=eq.<own id> with {plan: 'studio'}, {stripe_customer_id: 'cus_x'} and {suspended_at: null} each is rejected or updates 0 rows, with values unchanged when re-read using the secret key; DELETE /rest/v1/accounts?id=eq.<own id> is rejected or deletes 0 rows.
Read isolation: GET /rest/v1/accounts?select=* returns exactly the caller's own row, and ?id=eq.<another user's id> returns an empty array. A pgTAP file run by pnpm test:db covers the same cases.

features.title: Session cookies are host-only on the app host; auth routes exist on the app host only
acceptance: After signing in on http://app.localhost:3000, context.cookies() shows the Supabase auth cookie(s) (sb-...-auth-token...) for host app.localhost with no Domain attribute (host-only), Path=/ and SameSite=Lax.
Requests the same context makes to http://mara.localhost:3000/ and http://localhost:3000/ carry no sb- cookie in their request headers, and their responses contain no Set-Cookie header.

On http://mara.localhost:3000, /login, /signup, /claim, /auth/callback, /editor, /design, /analytics, /domains, /settings and /api/handles/check all return 404. On http://localhost:3000 the same paths return 404, except /login and /signup, which redirect (308) to the same path on http://app.localhost:3000 with the query string preserved.
Loading http://mara.localhost:3000/ and http://localhost:3000/ triggers zero requests to the Supabase auth URL: session refresh runs only for app-host requests.

Vitest on the proxy's session helper: an expired access token with a valid refresh token yields a response carrying refreshed cookies and the request proceeds as signed in; an invalid refresh token clears the cookies and the request is treated as signed out.
Persistence: a context restored from saved storageState keeps the user signed in when it loads http://app.localhost:3000/.

Abuse case: replaying a valid sb-...-auth-token value as a Cookie header on requests to http://mara.localhost:3000/ and http://localhost:3000/ changes nothing in the response (same HTML, no personalisation, no Set-Cookie), and the tenant host never accepts it as a session.

Production smoke after deploy: on https://app.hydlnk.com the auth cookie has Secure, host app.hydlnk.com and no Domain attribute, and https://hydlnk.com and https://<any handle>.hydlnk.com neither receive nor set it.

features.title: Auth gate and landing redirects for app routes
acceptance: Signed out, GET http://app.localhost:3000/, /editor, /design, /analytics, /domains, /settings and /claim each return a redirect to /login (assert status and Location header; destination pages may not exist yet); /login and /signup render.
Signed in with an account that has no page: / and each of /editor, /design, /analytics, /domains, /settings redirect to /claim; /claim renders.
Signed in with an account that has a page: / redirects to /editor; /login, /signup and /claim redirect to /editor.
Abuse case: the gate trusts verified claims, not cookie presence: a request carrying a forged sb-...-auth-token cookie that holds a garbage JWT is treated as signed out and redirected to /login.
Signed-in app responses send Cache-Control: no-store; after signing out, page.goBack() onto an app page shows /login and no cached app content.
No redirect or link ever carries a return-URL parameter: /login and /signup ignore ?next=, ?redirect_to= and ?return_to= entirely.

features.title: Continue with Google on the log in page
acceptance: On http://app.localhost:3000/login, clicking 'Continue with Google' navigates (intercept the request with page.route; do not try to finish Google's login in Playwright) to the local Supabase auth endpoint: host 127.0.0.1:54321, path /auth/v1/authorize, query provider=google, a PKCE code_challenge with code_challenge_method, and redirect_to exactly http://app.localhost:3000/auth/callback with no query string (production's allow-list holds the bare path). That URL is listed in supabase/config.toml [auth] additional_redirect_urls.
The same assertion against production with no login completed: https://app.hydlnk.com/login produces an authorize request whose redirect_to is exactly https://app.hydlnk.com/auth/callback.

Callback (Vitest, Supabase client mocked to accept a code for a user whose provider is google): creates the accounts row exactly as the email path does and redirects to http://app.localhost:3000/. A callback with ?error=access_denied&error_description=... redirects to /login?error=google_cancelled, which shows 'Google sign-in didn’t finish. Try again or use an email link.' and sets no session cookie.

Manual, because the Google OAuth client is in Testing and cannot be automated: Gary signs in at https://app.hydlnk.com/login with a Google account on the test-user list and lands signed in on /claim or /editor; using a Google address that already has an email-link account lands on that same account (one auth.users row, one accounts row). An account outside the test-user list gets Google's blocked screen, which is expected until the OAuth app is published (see the M5 Google OAuth feature).

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/login: document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= 390, every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide), and the Google button is full width, 48px tall, labelled 'Continue with Google' with a 1px #C9C5BE border.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the Google button sits below the 'or' divider inside the 400px-max form column, same 48px height.

features.title: Server-only handle claim creates the first page (reserved, taken, plan limit, race-safe)
acceptance: claimHandle (server-only, secret key) for a signed-in account with no page inserts one pages row: owner_id equals the session user, handle is the normalized value, draft is an empty page document (blocks: [], no token overrides), published and published_at are null; it returns the handle.

Each rejection returns a typed error and writes nothing: 'short', 'too_long', 'invalid', 'reserved' (including 'WWW', 'Admin' and any value in reserved_handles), 'taken' (a pages row already has it), 'page_limit' (account already has its plan's maximum, 1 on free, even for a different handle), 'no_account', and 'suspended' (accounts.suspended_at is set). The limit follows accounts.plan: with plan 'pro' set via the secret key a second claim succeeds and a fourth is rejected; 'studio' allows 15.

Race safety: 10 parallel claims of 'zq-race-1' by 10 different accounts leave exactly one pages row, 9 'taken' results and no 500; 2 parallel claims by one free account for 'zq-r-a' and 'zq-r-b' leave exactly one row, so the page limit is enforced by the database (lock or constraint), not only an app-level count.
Case safety: with the secret key, inserting handle 'MARA' while 'mara' exists fails with a unique violation, so differently-cased duplicates cannot coexist.
The owner always comes from the verified session: a claim request whose body contains another user's owner_id ignores it; an unauthenticated call returns 401 and writes no row.

Abuse case (direct PostgREST, publishable key plus the user's JWT, role authenticated; pgTAP via pnpm test:db): POST /rest/v1/pages with {handle: 'zq-direct-1', owner_id: <own id>} is rejected (401/403, code 42501) and creates no row; the same with handle 'www' is rejected; a second page for an account that already has one is rejected; PATCH /rest/v1/pages?id=eq.<own page id> with {handle: 'zq-other'}, with {published: {}} and with {published_at: 'now'} each is rejected or updates 0 rows, values unchanged when re-read with the secret key; DELETE /rest/v1/pages?id=eq.<own page id> is rejected or deletes 0 rows; GET /rest/v1/pages?select=handle as a different user returns an empty array.

features.title: Signup page layout with brand panel and form
acceptance: Signed out, http://app.localhost:3000/signup has <title> 'HYDLNK — Sign up'. Charcoal (#1C1B1A) brand panel: logo link (brass 9px diamond plus 'HYDLNK' 15px/700 with 0.14em tracking) to http://localhost:3000/; 'Claim your name.' at 44px/700; a bordered pill with a lock icon and 'yourname.hydlnk.com' in Geist Mono (handle part #D9B877, suffix #A9A49B); three check bullets 'Every block and the full theme system', 'Per-link analytics from day one', 'Bring your own domain whenever you’re ready'; footer note 'Free forever. At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/signup: document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= 390, every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide; inline Terms and Privacy links in the sentence are exempt), the brand panel is a slim charcoal bar at most 80px tall holding only the logo (heading, pill, bullets and note hidden), and the form starts directly beneath it with 20px side padding (see SignupPhone.dc.html).

features.title: Signup handle field: live availability and ?handle= prefill
acceptance: The Handle field normalizes as you type: entering 'Zq_Test 9!' leaves 'zqtest9' in the input; the brand-panel pill mirrors it ('zqtest9.hydlnk.com') and shows 'yourname' while the field is empty.
Empty or under 3 characters: neutral text 'At least 3 characters — letters, numbers and dashes.' in #5E5A54, field border #D9D6D0, and no request to /api/handles/check is sent.

After a debounce of at most 400 ms: 'mara' shows red text 'That one’s taken. Try another.' with border #B23A2B; 'www', 'app' and 'api' show red 'That name is reserved. Try another.'; '-mara' and 'xn--abc' show red 'Handles can’t start or end with a dash or start with xn--.'; 31 characters shows red 'Handles can be up to 30 characters.' (no maxlength attribute, so the state is reachable); 'zq-live-1' shows green (#2F7D4F) with a check icon and 'zq-live-1.hydlnk.com is available'.

While a check is in flight the status line shows neutral 'Checking…' and never the previous handle's result. Stale responses are discarded: with the 'mara' response delayed 1 s via page.route, typing 'mara' then 'zq-live-2' ends on 'zq-live-2.hydlnk.com is available' and never shows taken.
If the endpoint returns 500 the status line shows 'Couldn’t check that handle. Try again.' in neutral text and the submit button stays enabled (the server validates anyway).
Accessibility: the status container is aria-live='polite' with an id referenced by the input's aria-describedby, and has min-height 20px so the layout does not jump between states.

Prefill: http://app.localhost:3000/signup?handle=zq-pre-1 loads with the field already holding 'zq-pre-1' and the check already run (green 'zq-pre-1.hydlnk.com is available') with no interaction; ?handle=Mara loads 'mara' with the red taken message. The server-rendered HTML already contains the normalized value in the input (works before JS runs).

Hostile and long input: ?handle=<script>alert(1)</script> loads 'scriptalert1script', fires no dialog, and the initial HTML response contains no unescaped <script>alert(1) text; a 40-character value is kept in full and shows the 'Handles can be up to 30 characters.' state (not silently truncated); no handle param gives an empty field and other query parameters are ignored.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/signup?handle=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa (30 a's): document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= 390, every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide), the long value scrolls inside the input instead of widening the page, and the longest status message ('Handles can’t start or end with a dash or start with xn--.') wraps inside the column.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the status line sits under the Handle field, and the value shows in the brand-panel pill, wrapping inside it (overflow-wrap: anywhere).

features.title: Signup with email sign-in link claims the chosen handle
acceptance: On /signup?handle=zq-su-1, entering e2e-su-1@example.com and clicking 'Email me a sign-in link' replaces the form with 'Check your email' and 'We emailed a sign-in link to e2e-su-1@example.com. Open it to claim zq-su-1.hydlnk.com.'; exactly one message arrives in the local mail inbox, using the same email as the login feature.

Opening that link in a brand-new browser context (different device) ends signed in on http://app.localhost:3000/ and a pages row exists with handle 'zq-su-1' and owner_id equal to the new user (the handle travels with the sign-in request, not browser-local state), plus one accounts row.

Server-side enforcement before any email: with 'mara' (taken), 'www' (reserved), 'ab' (short) and '-x1' (invalid) the page shows the same status message as the live availability feature, focuses the Handle field, and the inbox message count is unchanged. Abuse case: a direct POST of the signup server action with handle=www returns a validation error, sends no email and creates no auth.users row.

An account that already has a page signing up again with a new handle gets the sent state; opening the link signs in without creating a second page (free limit 1): pages rows for that user stay 1 and the handle is unchanged.
Invalid email shows 'Enter a valid email address.' inline and sends nothing; the provider rate-limit message matches the login feature ('You can request another link in a minute.').

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/signup (sent state showing): document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= 390, every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide), and the 'Use a different email' and 'Resend link' buttons are full width.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the sent state replaces the form inside the 400px column, with the brand panel pill still showing 'zq-su-1.hydlnk.com'.

features.title: Continue with Google on signup carries the chosen handle
acceptance: On /signup?handle=zq-gs-1, clicking 'Continue with Google' navigates to http://127.0.0.1:54321/auth/v1/authorize with provider=google and redirect_to exactly http://app.localhost:3000/auth/callback (no handle in the URL). The response that starts the redirect sets a short-lived pending-handle cookie: HttpOnly, host app.localhost with no Domain attribute, Max-Age at most 900, SameSite=Lax.

The handle must be valid first: with 'mara', 'www', 'ab' or an empty field, the browser does not leave for Google, the same status messages as the live availability feature appear, and focus moves to the Handle field. Abuse case: a direct POST of the Google-start server action with handle=www is rejected and sets no cookie.

Callback with the pending-handle cookie (Vitest, mocked code exchange): the page is created through the server-only claim, the cookie is cleared, and the user lands on http://app.localhost:3000/. A cookie holding a handle that has since become taken, or a missing, tampered or over-long cookie, creates no page and lands on /claim. The cookie is also cleared when the account already has a page (no second page is created).

Manual on production (Google OAuth app is in Testing): Gary signs up with a test-user Google account and a fresh handle; afterwards a pages row exists and https://<handle>.hydlnk.com returns 200 showing the placeholder.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/signup?handle=zq-gs-1: document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= 390, every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide), and 'Continue with Google' is full width at 48px.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the Google button sits below the 'or' divider in the form column.

features.title: Tenant host serves a placeholder when the handle is claimed and a 404 when it is not
acceptance: For a claimed handle whose published column is null ('zq-ph-1', claimed through the server-only claim), GET http://zq-ph-1.localhost:3000/ returns 200 HTML with <title> 'zq-ph-1.hydlnk.com', exactly one h1 'zq-ph-1', the line 'Nothing published here yet.', and <meta name='robots' content='noindex'>. (Milestone 2 swaps in the real renderer for non-null published; this milestone never renders a page document.)

It is a tenant page, not HYDLNK UI: the page root sets the tenant token CSS variables resolved from the system-default theme by the Milestone 0 token resolver, and the response contains no --hl-* custom properties, no app-shell markup (no sidebar, top bar or tab bar) and no #1C1B1A charcoal bar; the placeholder uses system fonts and makes no network request to any host other than zq-ph-1.localhost:3000 (the Google Fonts link arrives in Milestone 3 and applies only to pages rendered from a published document).

Published-only: set the page's draft to a document containing the text 'DRAFT-MARKER-7f3a' with the secret key; the response body never contains it (public render reads only published and published_at).

Abuse case, no cookies: the response has no Set-Cookie, and sending an sb-...-auth-token cookie header to this host does not change the response. /login, /signup, /claim, /editor, /settings and /auth/callback on this host all return 404. A request whose Host header is ZQ-PH-1.localhost:3000 (upper case) returns the same page.

GET http://zq-none-1.localhost:3000/ (no pages row) returns status 404 with Cache-Control: no-store and <meta name='robots' content='noindex'>. The page uses HYDLNK UI styling (background #F4F3F0, ink text), says 'This address isn’t claimed.' with a primary link 'Claim zq-none-1' to http://app.localhost:3000/signup?handle=zq-none-1 and a secondary link 'Go to hydlnk.com' to http://localhost:3000/.

Claim then reload (distinguishes this from the routing stub): claim 'zq-none-1' with the secret-key claim function, then reload the same URL; it returns 200 with the placeholder immediately, with no stale 404 and no waiting. After the owner's account is deleted the host returns 404 again immediately (covered end to end in the delete account feature).

This can’t be undone.', a field 'Type your handle to confirm', a danger button 'Delete account' that stays disabled until the field equals 'zq-del-1', and 'Cancel'. Escape and Cancel close it with nothing changed; focus is trapped inside and returns to the trigger on close.

Confirming ends on http://app.localhost:3000/login with a notice 'Your account was deleted.' (role='status'). The session is gone: the refresh token captured earlier cannot be exchanged, and /editor redirects to /login.

Data is gone: no rows remain for that user in auth.users, accounts, pages, themes (owned), domains (via the page), daily_stats and events for the page. A pgTAP test (pnpm test:db) fails if any foreign key that references auth.users, accounts or pages has no explicit ON DELETE CASCADE or SET NULL action (NO ACTION and RESTRICT fail; SET NULL is for rows that must outlive the page, such as reports), so no row can block deletion and tables added in later milestones cannot leave orphans.

Handle released: /api/handles/check?handle=zq-del-1 returns 'available', a different new user can claim it, and http://zq-del-1.localhost:3000/ returns 404 immediately after deletion (cache tag invalidated, not a stale placeholder). Storage objects, Stripe subscriptions and custom domains are removed by the Milestone 4 account-deletion feature.

Abuse case, server action: the action deletes only the session user; with two users, user A's request carrying B's id in the payload leaves B's rows intact; a call without a session returns 401 or a redirect to /login and deletes nothing; a call whose confirmation text does not equal the handle is rejected server-side and deletes nothing.

Abuse case, direct API (publishable key plus the user's JWT): DELETE /rest/v1/accounts?id=eq.<own id> and DELETE /rest/v1/pages?id=eq.<own page id> are rejected or delete 0 rows; DELETE {SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/admin/users/<own id> returns 401/403; all rows are still present when re-read with the secret key.

features.title: Google sign-in on the log in page through a Google ID token
acceptance: With NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID set and Google's script stubbed (page.route on https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client; Google's real login is never driven), http://app.localhost:3000/login calls google.accounts.id.initialize once with the configured client_id, ux_mode 'popup', auto_select false and a 64-hex nonce, then renderButton with type standard, theme outline, size large, text continue_with and a width of at most 400. The nonce handed to Google equals sha256 of the value in the hl-google-nonce cookie, which is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, has no Domain (host app.localhost) and lives at most 900 seconds; the raw value appears nowhere in the page (document.cookie, the initialize config).

A stubbed credential with the right nonce and audience reaches the signInWithGoogle Server Action: the local Supabase refuses it, the page shows 'Google sign-in didn’t work. Try again or use an email link.', stays on /login and no sb-...-auth-token cookie is set. The attempt spent the nonce: a new hl-google-nonce is issued, initialize is called again with sha256 of it, and a second attempt reaches Supabase again (the same message, not the 'expired' one).

Abuse cases, each refused with no session cookie and the nonce spent, and with Supabase never called (Playwright for the first group, Vitest for all): a token whose nonce claim is another page's nonce or the raw cookie value, or a cleared or expired nonce cookie ('Google sign-in expired. Try again.'); a token for another Google client id; a credential that is not a JWT or is over 6000 characters; a nonce cookie that is not 43 base64url characters; and a missing or foreign Origin header, which is refused without touching the visitor's nonce.

Vitest, Supabase mocked: a valid token calls signInWithIdToken({provider:'google', token, nonce}) with the RAW nonce read from the cookie (never from the request), makes the accounts row exactly as the email path does (a failure there does not undo the sign-in), clears the nonce cookie and returns ok; the page then loads / and the auth gate routes to /claim or /editor. A Supabase error gives the friendly message (429 gives 'Too many attempts. Try again in a minute.'), only its code is logged, and nothing is set. A stale hl-pending-handle cookie is dropped when the account already has a page.

Without NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID the Google button, the 'or' rule and Google's script are absent from the server-rendered /login and /signup and email sign-in works alone. When Google's script cannot load the page says 'Google sign-in couldn’t load. Use an email link instead.' and the email form still works.

Headers: only app-host responses are affected; the app-host CSP still forbids framing and sets no script-src, frame-src, connect-src or style-src, so Google's script, iframe and requests are not blocked, and any such directive added later automatically lists Google's documented origin (https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client, /gsi/, /gsi/style); Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin is never sent (it blanks Google's popup).

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/login: document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= 390, every other button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall, and Google's button spans the form column below the 'or' rule inside a row at least 48px tall. Google draws its button 40px tall inside its own iframe and does not allow resizing, so the 44px floor does not apply inside it. Narrowing the viewport draws the button again at the new width. At 1440x900 it sits below the 'or' rule inside the 400px-max form column.

Manual on production, after the Google Cloud, Supabase and Vercel steps: Gary signs in at https://app.hydlnk.com/login with a Google account, Google's popup names hydlnk.com, and he lands on /claim (new account) or /editor (existing account); a Google address that already has an email-link account lands on that same account (one auth.users row, one accounts row).

features.title: Page document schema and limits in Zod
acceptance: Vitest unit: one shared module (extending the Milestone 0 page and block schemas) exports `draftDocSchema` and `publishDocSchema` for the page document `{version, rev, profile:{name, bio, photo}, theme:{ref, overrides}, blocks[]}`. The editor, the Publish action and the public-page query all import from it (static import check). `theme` reuses the Milestone 0 token types.

`draftDocSchema` is lenient about completeness so half-typed blocks can autosave (empty strings and empty URLs allowed); `publishDocSchema` is strict. Fixture: a link block with label '' and url '' passes the draft schema and fails the publish schema; a doc with an empty display name does the same.

The block union has exactly nine types: link, card, header, text, image, social, embed, grid, divider. Each block has `id` (nanoid, 8-24 chars of A-Za-z0-9_-) and `visible` (boolean, defaults true). An unknown `type` fails both schemas; unknown keys are stripped on parse so published JSON carries only known fields.

Limit table, each tested at the limit (passes) and limit+1 (fails both schemas), counted in Unicode code points with the same helper the editor counters use: display name 60, bio 160, blocks 50, link label 80, card title 60, card caption 100, header text 80, text 600, image alt 140, embed caption 80, social icons 1 to 8, grid cells 2 to 6, cell title 40, cell subtitle 60.

Ids are unique across the whole document, including social-icon ids and grid-cell ids (so Milestone 4 click tracking can resolve any link by id); a duplicate id fails both schemas. Moving, editing or re-saving a block never changes its id (round-trip test).

Text fields are trimmed. Control characters (U+0000-U+001F except newline inside text blocks, U+007F-U+009F) and bidi override or isolate characters (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069) fail `publishDocSchema`.

Image references are `{path, width, height}` and `path` must match `^[0-9a-f-]{36}/[a-z0-9-]{8,64}[.](jpg|png|webp)$` (owner folder, then a file name; this one scheme covers the pass-through names of this milestone and the hashed WebP names of Milestone 5); an external URL, a path containing `..` or a data: URI fails both schemas, so a tenant cannot point the renderer at a third-party image.

Block `overrides` keep only the color, buttonStyle and radius keys the Milestone 0 resolver allows: any other key (for example `fontHeading`) is stripped on parse and never reaches `published`, while an invalid value for an allowed key (radius -5, color 'red') fails `publishDocSchema`.

Direct-API abuse (Vitest): a 60-block document and a document containing a block with `type: 'script'` both fail `publishDocSchema`. RLS lets an owner write any JSON to `draft` with the publishable key, so these writes land in the draft and are stopped at Publish (see the Publish gate feature).

features.title: Link URL validation rule (http and https only)
acceptance: Vitest table with at least 30 cases for `httpUrl`. Accepts `https://maraokafor.com/portraits`, `http://example.com/a?b=c#d`, an internationalised host and a URL of exactly 2048 chars. Rejects `javascript:alert(1)`, `JaVaScRiPt:alert(1)`, `data:text/html,<script>`, `vbscript:`, `file:///etc/passwd`, `//evil.example`, `https://user:pw@example.com` (userinfo), `https://` (no host), `mailto:a@b.co`, `ftp://example.com`, a URL containing a tab or newline, and a 2049-char URL.

`normalizeUrl('maraokafor.com/portraits')` returns `https://maraokafor.com/portraits`; inputs that already start with http:// or https:// are unchanged; `javascript:alert(1)` is never prefixed into a valid-looking URL and stays invalid.
`safeHref(url)` returns the normalized URL for valid input and `undefined` for anything else. It is the only function renderer code may use to obtain an href.
Table-driven test over every URL-bearing field in `publishDocSchema` (link.url, card.url, image.url, embed.url, social icon url, grid cell url): each rejects `javascript:alert(1)` and `data:` URLs.

Email addresses are not URLs: the social email icon stores an address validated by a separate `emailAddress` rule (one `@`, no whitespace, at most 254 chars); the renderer builds the `mailto:` href from it. `mailto:` is rejected by `httpUrl` everywhere else.

Direct-API abuse: a PostgREST update of `pages.draft` with a `javascript:` link URL succeeds (drafts are untrusted under RLS) but `publishDocSchema` rejects it, so the URL can never reach `published` or the public page (end-to-end proof lives in the Publish gate feature).

features.title: Editor opens the current page's draft
acceptance: Signed in as the seeded user mara, `http://app.localhost:3000/editor` renders mara's current page (chosen by the `hl-page` cookie rule from the page switcher feature, oldest page by default) with the draft loaded using the user's Supabase session and publishable key; a Vitest static check confirms no editor route module imports the server-only secret-key client. The sidebar Editor link keeps aria-current='page'.
Unauthenticated GET `http://app.localhost:3000/editor` returns 302 to the Milestone 1 sign-in route and the response body contains none of any page's draft text.

Cross-tenant: signed in as a second e2e user (jonas), set the cookie `hl-page` to mara's page id and GET `http://app.localhost:3000/editor`: the editor shows jonas's own page and none of mara's draft text appears in the body. Direct API: `GET /rest/v1/pages?id=eq.{mara's pageId}` with jonas's access token and the publishable key returns `[]`.

Header bar: mono 12px breadcrumb `mara.hydlnk.com / main` in #5E5A54 (the address is always shown as `{handle}.hydlnk.com`), h1 'Main page' at 22px/700, and on the right a secondary 'Preview' link (opens `http://mara.localhost:3000` in a new tab with `target='_blank'` and `rel='noopener'`, hidden below 760px) and a charcoal 'Publish' button (wired in the Publish gate feature). The seeded page's draft renders: name, bio and the seeded blocks.

A page whose draft has no profile or blocks yet (what signup creates) opens with defaults: display name equal to the handle (`mara`), empty bio, zero blocks. The Blocks section shows the empty state 'No blocks yet. Add your first block above.' and the route returns 200 without an error boundary.

Corrupted draft: with the publishable key PATCH mara's `draft` to `{}` and then to `{"blocks": 5}` (RLS allows it); the editor still loads, repairs what it can to defaults, shows a notice 'Some content couldn’t be read and was reset in the editor. Nothing is saved until you edit.' and does not write to the database until the user edits.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor the header wraps (title block first, then status chip and Publish), Publish is at least 44px tall (the mockup's 40px loses to DESIGN.md), every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide) and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: breadcrumb and title sit left; status chip, Preview and Publish sit right on one row.

features.title: Autosave draft, with a database integrity check on drafts
acceptance: Playwright at `http://app.localhost:3000/editor` as mara: typing 10 characters into Display name in under 500 ms produces exactly one PATCH to `/rest/v1/pages?id=eq.{pageId}` about 800 ms after the last keystroke (count with `page.on('request')`). The body contains only the `draft` key, and the draft's `rev` has increased by 1.

A mono 12px save indicator next to the status chip (`aria-live='polite'`) reads 'Saving...' while the request is in flight, 'Saved' after a 2xx and 'Not saved' after a failure. After a full reload the edit is still there (loaded from Postgres).
Flush: after an edit, firing `visibilitychange` to hidden sends the PATCH immediately without waiting for the debounce. A `beforeunload` prompt appears only while unsaved edits are pending.

Failure: with the context offline (`context.setOffline(true)`) an edit shows 'Not saved' and the message 'Couldn’t save. Your changes stay here and will retry.', retries with backoff, and saves once back online (indicator returns to 'Saved'). This is the one wording of the save-failure state used by the Editor and Design screens.
The client validates with `draftDocSchema` before sending. A draft over 256 KB is not sent and the indicator reads 'This page is too large to save. Remove some content.'

Stale tab guard: open the editor in two browser contexts as mara; context A edits the name and saves; context B (loaded earlier) edits the bio and its save is refused (the update filtered on the stored `rev` matches 0 rows). Context B shows 'This page changed in another tab. Reload to keep editing.' with a Reload button, the database keeps A's name and the old bio, and Reload shows A's name.
Autosave never touches `published` or `published_at` (asserted by a DB read after each save), and the public page `http://mara.localhost:3000` is unchanged after autosave.

Database integrity (new migration plus pgTAP in `pnpm test:db`): a CHECK on `pages.draft` requires a JSON object with `octet_length(draft::text) <= 262144`. Direct-API abuse, as mara with the publishable key through PostgREST: PATCH draft to `[]`, to `"x"` and to a 300 KB object are each rejected (HTTP 400, check violation); a 200 KB object is accepted; a PATCH against jonas's page matches 0 rows. Existing Milestone 0 policies still pass.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor the indicator and chip wrap inside the header without horizontal scroll or overlap with the title, and every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide); at 1440x900 they sit on the right of the header row.

features.title: Shared page renderer for preview and public page
acceptance: Exactly one component, `PageRenderer`, renders profile and block markup. Both the editor's preview and the public page import it (Vitest static check: no other module outputs block markup; the preview wrapper and the public page component pass the same props shape).

The root element `[data-page-root]` carries the resolved tenant tokens as CSS variables prefixed `--t-` (all eight color tokens plus the type, shape, space and background groups from PLAN.md). Vitest static scan of the renderer directory finds no hex or rgb color literals and no `--hl-*` references, so blocks only read variables and the two token systems never mix.

Sizing uses container queries only: the root has `container-type: inline-size`, and a static scan of the renderer styles finds no `@media` width queries and no `vw` units (the editor preview is narrower than the viewport). The content column is capped by the `maxWidth` token (default 480px) and positioned by the `align` token; the `--t-bg` background fills the full viewport, not just the column.

Profile: a circular avatar that is either the photo (``, object-fit cover, `alt` equal to the display name) or an initials fallback (first letter of the first and last word, uppercased: 'Mara Okafor' gives 'MO', 'Prince' gives 'P', 'jean claude van damme' gives 'JD', empty name gives '?'), then an `

` with the display name and a `

` with the bio. An empty name or bio renders no empty element.

Blocks render in array order inside `<main>`. Every block root carries `data-block-id` and `data-block-type`; nested social icons and grid cells carry `data-item-id`. Blocks with `visible === false` are skipped (defense in depth; Publish also strips them) and an unknown `type` renders nothing without throwing. The renderer accepts a footer slot that the badge and report-link features fill.

Every outbound anchor gets its `href` from one `outboundHref()` helper that wraps `safeHref` and sets `rel='nofollow noopener'`; in Milestone 2 it returns the validated destination (Milestone 4 swaps it for the `/r/[pageId]/[blockId]` redirect). Static scan finds no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in the renderer; a name of `` renders as visible text and no dialog event fires.

Markup is identical wherever it is mounted. The editor's preview wrapper, not the renderer, intercepts clicks on anchors so they do not navigate (Playwright: clicking a link in the editor preview leaves the URL unchanged).

Dev-only fixture route `http://localhost:3000/dev/renderer` (404 when NODE_ENV is production). At 390x844 with a 60-character unbroken display name and long bio: `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, avatar 96px, name wraps via `overflow-wrap`, and every anchor, button and social icon is at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the same fixture route: column no wider than 480px and centered, background color covers the whole viewport.

features.title: Page media bucket and server-only image upload
acceptance: New migration creates a public Storage bucket `page-media` (the single bucket for every tenant image from here on) with `file_size_limit` 4 MB (below Vercel's 4.5 MB request-body cap; the 10 MB figure in PLAN is the Free plan's total upload quota, enforced in Milestone 4) and `allowed_mime_types` image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp. No insert, update, delete or select policy for `anon` or `authenticated` exists on its objects, so files are readable by public URL but cannot be listed or written by clients. pgTAP covers the policies.

The one upload route is `POST http://app.localhost:3000/api/media` (multipart field `file`, plus an optional field `kind` with value avatar, background or content, default content, which Milestone 5's pipeline uses to pick an output size; any other `kind` value returns 400). It requires a session, rejects bodies over 4 MB with 413 before decoding, sniffs magic bytes (JPEG FF D8 FF, PNG 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A, WebP RIFF....WEBP) and ignores the client-declared type and file name. It stores the file as-is at `{uid}/{uuid}.{jpg|png|webp}` (uid always from the session; any owner or folder field in the form is ignored) with a one-year cache-control, and returns `{path, width, height, url}` with width and height read from the image header, valid per the image-reference schema (an 800x600 fixture returns width 800, height 600). Images wider or taller than 8000px are rejected with 422.
The public URL `{SUPABASE_URL}/storage/v1/object/public/page-media/{path}` returns 200 with the correct content-type and a long `cache-control`.

Rejected with a clear error and no object created (verified by listing with the secret key): no session (401), a PNG-named SVG or HTML file declared as image/png (415), a GIF (415), a 0-byte file (422), and a file of 4 MB + 1 byte (413).

Direct-API abuse with mara's access token and the publishable key: `POST /storage/v1/object/page-media/{mara uid}/x.png` is rejected (no client insert policy); uploading into jonas's folder is rejected; overwriting an existing object with upsert is rejected; deleting another user's object is rejected; `POST /storage/v1/object/list/page-media` as anon and as authenticated returns no objects; a 5 MB direct upload is refused by the bucket limit.

Replacing or removing an image in the editor changes only the draft reference: the client makes no Storage delete call, and an object the published copy still references stays readable at its public URL. Garbage collection of unreferenced objects is the Milestone 5 cleanup feature; resizing, WebP conversion and per-account quotas are Milestones 5 and 4.

features.title: Link button block with shared URL field

The embed `src` is always rebuilt from the parsed id, never copied from the input.

Renderer, YouTube: a click-to-play facade, a 16:9 `<button aria-label='Play video: {caption}'>` on a dark poster (#050505) with a play glyph and the caption '{caption} · YouTube' below. features.title: Public page renders published content only, with safe response headers
acceptance: Precondition: the seeded `mara` page has a `published` document (seed.sql or a fixture written with the secret key, since Publish is built later), for example name 'Mara Okafor' with a link block 'Portrait sessions - fall dates'. GET `http://mara.localhost:3000/` returns 200, `<title>Mara Okafor - links</title>`, a meta description equal to the bio, `<html lang='en'>`, and the page rendered by `PageRenderer` from `published` with its frozen tokens.

Draft isolation: set `draft.profile.name` to `DRAFT-ONLY-7f3a` and add a block 'DRAFT-BLOCK-7f3a' (through the editor or PostgREST). GET `http://mara.localhost:3000/` and the same URL with header `RSC: 1` contain neither string nor a `draft` key.

The public query is server-only and selects `published`, `published_at` and fields of the owner's accounts row (the plan in this milestone; suspended_at joins in Milestone 5) (Vitest static check: it never selects `draft` or `*`). After `pnpm build`, a grep of `.next/static` finds no `sb_secret_` and no `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`.

Direct-API abuse: `GET {SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/pages?select=published,draft&handle=eq.mara` with the publishable key and no JWT returns `[]`, and as signed-in jonas also returns `[]` (no public select), so the page cannot be read around the server query.

A handle whose `published` is null (for example a freshly signed-up page) still shows the Milestone 1 placeholder, never draft content. An unknown handle, `http://nobody.localhost:3000/`, returns 404 per Milestone 1.
Host-only cookies: after signing in at `http://app.localhost:3000`, `context.cookies('http://mara.localhost:3000')` contains no `sb-` cookie, and the public response has no `Set-Cookie`.

Response headers on the public page: `Content-Security-Policy` with `frame-src https://www.youtube-nocookie.com https://open.spotify.com; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'` (no script-src nonce, so the page stays static and cacheable), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`; a Playwright run with a YouTube and a Spotify embed shows no CSP violation in the console, and an injected iframe to `https://evil.example` is blocked.
At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/: `scrollWidth <= innerWidth` and every anchor, button and social icon is rendered at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the column is no wider than 480px, centered, and the page background covers the viewport.

features.title: Publish gate: server-only, validated, resolved
acceptance: Server Action `publishPage(pageId)` is `'use server'` and imports the secret-key client under `server-only`. Its signature takes only a page id and no document (type test); it reads the draft from Postgres itself. Playwright: type ' X' into Bio and click Publish within 100 ms; the live page `http://mara.localhost:3000` contains the final text (the client flushes autosave first, and the server reads the saved draft).

Auth (Vitest integration against local Supabase): no session is rejected as unauthorized; jonas calling it for mara's page id is rejected as forbidden; in both cases `pages.published` and `published_at` are unchanged.

Validation gate: the draft is parsed with `publishDocSchema` plus the URL rule and embed allowlist, every image `path` must start with the owner's uid and exist in `page-media`, and required fields must be filled. Any failure returns `{ok:false, errors:[{blockId, field, message}]}` and writes nothing. Direct-API abuse: as mara with the publishable key, PATCH `pages.draft` through PostgREST to include a link URL `javascript:alert(1)`, a `data:` URL, an embed of `https://evil.example/x`, a photo path in jonas's folder, 51 blocks and a display name with U+202E. Each Publish attempt is refused with the offending block id named, `published` stays as before and the live HTML never contains those strings.
Escaping: a display name of `<script>alert(1)</script>` is valid, publishes, and renders as escaped text (live HTML contains `<script>`, no dialog event).

Success writes `pages.published` as the publish form of the draft: the profile, only blocks with `visible !== false` (hidden blocks are removed, not just flagged), the frozen resolved tokens (see the freeze feature) and `published_at = now()`, and returns `{ok:true, publishedAt}`. Unknown draft keys are stripped.

Direct-API abuse: with mara's access token and the publishable key, PATCH `/rest/v1/pages?id=eq.{id}` with `{published: {...}}` and with `{published_at: '2026-01-01'}` are each rejected (HTTP 403 or 401, permission denied) and `published` is unchanged.

UI: the 'Publish' button shows 'Publishing...' and is disabled while running (double-click sends one request); on success a toast 'Published.' with a 'View live page' link to `http://mara.localhost:3000` appears and the status chip reads 'Published' (chip states are in the Unpublished changes feature).

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor the Publish button is at least 44px tall, the toast does not overlap the bottom tab bar, every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide) and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the button sits right-aligned in the header after the Preview link.

features.title: Publish errors shown on the blocks that failed
acceptance: When Publish returns errors, an alert (`role='alert'`) above the block list reads 'Fix {n} blocks before publishing.' (or 'Fix 1 block before publishing.') and lists each failure by block title. Failing rows get a #B23A2B-accented border (#E8C4BD fill) and an inline message under the field in #B23A2B text. Nothing is published (`published` and `published_at` unchanged in the DB).

The first failing block expands, scrolls into view and focuses its first invalid input. Copy is sentence case and says what to do: 'Add a link label.', 'Enter a full web address, like https://example.com.', 'Paste a link to a YouTube video or a Spotify track, album, playlist or episode.', 'Add a short description of this image.', 'Upload an image.', 'Add a display name.'
Profile errors highlight the Display name field. Social icon and grid cell failures highlight the specific icon row or cell by id.
Fixing a field clears its error as soon as it validates (client-side check with `publishDocSchema` on blur) and the status chip stays 'Unpublished changes' throughout.

Playwright: seed a draft (through PostgREST) with a link with an empty URL, an embed to a non-allowlisted host and an image block without alt text; Publish shows 'Fix 3 blocks before publishing.' and the three rows are marked.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor with the Preview tab active, clicking Publish on an invalid draft switches to the Blocks tab and shows the alert; alert and inline messages wrap with `scrollWidth <= innerWidth` and every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide).
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the alert spans the block column (max 720px) and the preview stays visible.

features.title: Publish freezes resolved tokens into the live page
acceptance: Fixture: with the secret key insert a theme row owned by mara (name 'Freeze fixture', tokens differing from the system default) and point mara's draft at it with a page override `accent: '#C46A4F'` and a block override `buttonStyle: 'pill'` on one link block. After Publish, `pages.published.tokens` contains every token from the PLAN.md table fully resolved (system default, then theme, then page overrides) with no nulls, and the overridden block carries its resolved override values.
Rendering the live page reads only `published`: a Vitest check with a mocked Supabase client shows `PageRenderer` and the public query make zero calls to `themes`.

Using the secret key, update the fixture row's `tokens` (different bg and accent). `http://mara.localhost:3000` still serves identical CSS variable values, and after deleting the fixture row the page still renders identically.
The editor for mara's draft now resolves the new theme values (preview changes) and the status chip shows 'Unpublished changes', because the draft's resolved tokens differ from the frozen ones.
After Publish again, `http://mara.localhost:3000` shows the new theme values.

Direct-API abuse: with mara's publishable-key JWT, PATCH `/rest/v1/pages` writing `published.tokens` directly is rejected, and applying or editing a theme never changes a live page by itself (there is no code path from a theme write to `published` or the page cache).

features.title: Publish invalidates the page cache with updateTag
acceptance: Against a production build (`pnpm build && pnpm start`): two consecutive GETs of `http://mara.localhost:3000/` return the second with `x-nextjs-cache: HIT`, and a call counter on the public query (enabled by a test env flag) reads 1 after both requests.

Publish calls `updateTag` with a per-page tag inside the Server Action. Changing the bio, clicking Publish and immediately GETting `http://mara.localhost:3000/` (no waiting, no second request) returns the new bio; the OG image and metadata refresh too.
Autosave does not invalidate: after a draft autosave, a GET of `http://mara.localhost:3000/` is still `HIT` and its body is byte-identical.
Tags are per page: publishing mara's page leaves jonas's page response (`http://jonas.localhost:3000/`) as `HIT` with its query counter unchanged.
A Publish that fails validation does not call `updateTag`; mara's page stays `HIT`.

First publish: a handle that served the Milestone 1 placeholder switches to the real page on the first successful Publish. Direct-API abuse: a PostgREST write to `draft` does not change the live page, and a PostgREST write to `published` is rejected, so a client cannot alter or poison the cached page.

features.title: Unpublished changes state in the editor header
acceptance: The status chip in the header (4px radius, 12px/500, 6px dot, `aria-live='polite'`) has three states: 'Not published' (page whose `published` is null; neutral #EFEDE9 background, #5E5A54 text), 'Unpublished changes' (#F6EEDF background, #6B5226 text) and 'Published' (#E7F3EC background, #2F7D4F text).

State is computed from the data, not a client flag: the draft's publish form (visible blocks only, resolved tokens, `rev` ignored) is deep-compared with `pages.published`. A seeded mara page whose draft equals published shows 'Published' after a hard reload.
Editing the bio flips the chip to 'Unpublished changes' immediately (before the autosave PATCH completes) and it persists across reload; typing the original bio back returns it to 'Published'.
Reordering and toggling a block's visibility change the state. Editing the label of a block that is hidden in both draft and published does not.

A new page with `published` null shows 'Not published'; after Publish the chip becomes 'Published' without a reload and a 'View live page' link to `http://mara.localhost:3000` is available in the header.
A change to the draft's theme row (secret-key update) flips the chip to 'Unpublished changes' on reload even though no draft field was edited.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor the chip wraps within the header (`scrollWidth <= innerWidth`), the 'View live page' link is at least 44px tall and every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide).
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the chip sits left of the Preview and Publish buttons.

features.title: Made with HYDLNK footer badge on Free pages
acceptance: The public query reads the owner's `accounts.plan` server-side (secret key, with the page) and the renderer shows the footer link 'Made with HYDLNK' if and only if the plan is 'free'. The decision is made at render time from the account row, never from the draft or published JSON, so a plan change does not need a republish (the webhook feature in Milestone 4 triggers the cache refresh). Seeded free mara: `http://mara.localhost:3000` shows the link pointing to the HYDLNK marketing origin (`https://hydlnk.com`; locally `http://localhost:3000`) with `rel='noopener'`, rendered in the renderer's footer slot.

Fixtures: a page whose owner has plan 'pro' and another with 'studio' (set with the secret key before the first render) show no badge; Vitest renders the footer for plan values free, pro and studio and for an unknown plan value (fails closed to showing the badge).

One helper, `invalidateAccountPages(accountId)`, calls `revalidateTag` for every page tag of that account (Vitest with the cache API mocked asserts one call per page); it is the single function the Stripe webhook (Milestone 4) and admin suspend (Milestone 5) call.
The editor's live preview shows the same footer, following the account's current plan.

The badge uses `--t-text-muted` on `--t-bg` and keeps readable contrast in the Noir, Ivory and Smoke system themes (WCAG AA check on computed colors).
At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/ the badge's tap area is at least 44px tall, it sits after the last block without overlapping the report link and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: it is centered under the 480px column.

features.title: Report link on every public page
acceptance: Every published tenant page's footer has a link 'Report this page' on `http://mara.localhost:3000` whose `href` is the HYDLNK marketing origin plus `/report?page={pageId}` (locally `http://localhost:3000/report?page=<mara's page id>`), built by one `reportUrl(pageId)` helper. The report form and admin review are Milestone 5; this milestone only ships the link, whose destination may 404 until then.
The link is present in the static HTML (curl without JavaScript), on a page with zero blocks, on a Pro page with the badge removed, and in the editor preview (clicks do not navigate there).

Direct-API abuse: writing `draft.settings={hideReport:true}` or any other field through PostgREST cannot remove the link, since Publish strips unknown keys and the footer is rendered by the renderer, not by tenant data. A page whose published JSON contains such a key still renders the link (Vitest).

The link text is escaped and the href carries only the page id (a hostile handle or display name never reaches it; Vitest with hostile fixtures). The footer is not a block: it has no block id and, from Milestone 4, no click event.
At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/ the link has a tap area of at least 44px, does not overlap the badge and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: it is centered under the column.

features.title: OG image and social metadata per page
acceptance: `http://mara.localhost:3000/` includes `og:title` (display name), `og:description` (bio), `og:type=website`, `og:url` (absolute URL on the host the page is served from), `og:image` (absolute URL on the same host) and `twitter:card=summary_large_image`.

Fetching the `og:image` URL returns 200 with `content-type: image/png` and a PNG IHDR of 1200x630 (parsed in the test) with a non-trivial body. The image shows the display name, the bio truncated with an ellipsis, the avatar (photo or initials), the host in mono type, and the page's frozen background, text and accent colors.

Rendering uses bundled fonts only: a mocked `fetch` shows no request to fonts.googleapis.com or fonts.gstatic.com during generation. Parity at 1440x900: the nine `[data-block-id]` elements in the editor's preview pane and on `http://mara.localhost:3000` have the same ids, the same `data-block-type` order, equal `textContent` and equal `href` and `src` attributes. The hidden Text block appears in neither and its text is absent from the live HTML source; the avatar shows the photo in both. (Pixel equality is not required because the preview bezel is narrower than the live page.)

features.title: Google Fonts allowlist and safe stylesheet URL builder
acceptance: Vitest: the allowlist module exports at least 12 families, each with a family name, a category (sans, serif, display or mono) and a non-empty list of supported weights; it includes Instrument Serif, Fraunces and Geist (the tenant fonts used in Design.dc.html), at least 3 sans and at least 3 serif families.

Vitest: the stylesheet URL builder given ['Instrument Serif','Geist'] returns one https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2 URL with exactly those two family params (URL-encoded, e.g. family=Instrument+Serif) plus display=swap; the same family passed twice is emitted once.
Vitest: given 'Comic Sans MS', '', 'Geist;}body{x:y', 'Geist, sans-serif' or a 200-character string, the builder throws or returns null, and no returned URL ever contains the raw input.

Vitest: the fontHeading and fontBody Zod schemas accept every allowlisted family and reject each invalid string above. End-to-end abuse cases (a direct draft write of a hostile font name) are asserted in the tenant fonts and Publish validation features.

features.title: Token values: strict schema and injection-safe CSS variables
acceptance: Vitest: the 8 colour tokens (bg, surface, text, textMuted, accent, buttonBg, buttonText, border) accept #RGB, #RRGGBB and #RRGGBBAA and reject 'red', 'rgb(0,0,0)', '#GGGGGG', 'url(x)', '#fff;}body{display:none' and any string longer than 9 characters.

Vitest: enum tokens accept only their documented values (buttonStyle fill|outline|soft|shadow|pill, density compact|regular|airy, bgType solid|gradient|image, align left|center, letterCase normal|uppercase|lowercase) and reject any other string.

Vitest: numeric tokens enforce ranges and reject NaN, negatives and numeric strings: radius 0-32, borderWidth 0-4, scale 0.8-1.3, weightHeading one of 400/500/600/700, maxWidth 360-720, overlayOpacity 0-1, blur 0-24.

Vitest: bgImage accepts only an https (or the local http://127.0.0.1:54321) URL under this project's Storage public path for the `page-media` bucket and rejects javascript:, data:, http: on production hosts, https://evil.example/x.png and any URL containing quotes or parentheses. The page-level overrides schema accepts any subset of token keys and rejects unknown keys such as 'fontHeadingg' or 'customCss'.

Vitest: the CSS variable serializer (extending the Milestone 2 renderer root) emits one --t-* custom property per token, and drops any value that fails the token schema, using the system default value for that token instead; values are never concatenated into a style string without validation.

Playwright 1440x900: on http://mara.localhost:3000 the tenant root element has --t-bg, --t-accent and --t-text equal to the published values (Noir bg #16120E, accent #C9A86A, text #EFE8DC), and getComputedStyle(root).getPropertyValue('--hl-ink') is empty, so the two token systems never mix.

Direct-API abuse: with mara's session and the publishable key, PATCH http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1/pages?id=eq.<mara page id> setting draft overrides bg to 'red;}</style><script>window.__x=1</script>' (RLS allows draft writes); opening http://app.localhost:3000/editor shows a preview root that contains no script element, window.__x is undefined, and the bg falls back to the resolved default.

features.title: More system themes: 6 to 8 shipped, read-only
acceptance: Milestone 0 already ships Noir, Ivory and Smoke. pgTAP after supabase db reset: select count(*) from themes where owner_id is null is between 6 and 8; the rows include Noir, Ivory and Smoke with the values in Design.dc.html (Noir bg #16120E, surface #221B13, text #EFE8DC, accent #C9A86A, Instrument Serif, Outline, radius 12, regular, solid; Ivory bg #F3EEE4, Fraunces, Fill, radius 4, airy; Smoke bg #1C2023, Geist, Pill, radius 20, gradient); names are unique and at most 40 characters; the added rows come from a new migration, not seed.sql and not an edit of an already committed migration.

Direct-API abuse: with a user JWT and the publishable key at http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1/themes, PATCH and DELETE on a row with owner_id is null change nothing (zero rows affected, row unchanged on re-read), and an INSERT with owner_id null is rejected.

Direct-API abuse: with the Free user's JWT and the publishable key POST http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1/themes {name, tokens} as a 4th row is rejected; 6 concurrent inserts starting from 2 saved themes leave exactly 3 rows; an insert with owner_id of another user or null is rejected.
At 390x844 the limit message is fully visible with `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, and its dismiss control is at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 the message sits above the saved themes grid.

features.title: Update and rename a saved theme
acceptance: Playwright 1440x900 as a Pro fixture user with pages mara and maraprints both on saved theme 'Shared look': on mara change the accent to Sage and the tag reads 'Edited'; an 'Update Shared look' button then writes the page's resolved tokens into that themes row through the user's own session, clears mara's overrides, returns the tag to 'Applied', and leaves the preview unchanged. The button is not offered when the applied theme is a system theme (only 'Save as theme' is).

After Update, maraprints' draft preview at http://app.localhost:3000/design shows the new accent and its editor chip reads 'Unpublished changes' (resolved tokens differ from the frozen ones), while http://mara.localhost:3000 and http://maraprints.localhost:3000 remain byte-identical.

After renaming to 'Night Market' the card, the header ('Theme · Night Market') and every other page using the theme show the new name, the row's tokens are unchanged (deep-equal), and no page shows 'Unpublished changes' because of the rename.

Direct-API abuse: with user B's JWT and the publishable key PATCH http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1/themes?id=eq.<Shared look id> (rename or tokens) changes nothing (row unchanged on re-read), the same on any system theme, and a PATCH setting a 41-character name on one's own theme is rejected by a database constraint.
At 390x844 (DesignPhone.dc.html) the Update button, the rename trigger and the rename input are at least 44px tall and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.

features.title: Delete a saved theme and fall back to the default
acceptance: Playwright 1440x900 as a Pro fixture user with pages mara and maraprints on saved theme 'Shared look': Delete opens a dialog 'Delete Shared look? Drafts using it fall back to the default theme. Live pages keep their look until you republish.' with danger 'Delete theme' and 'Cancel'; Escape closes it and focus is trapped inside.
