After one real beacon (valid user agent and Origin) is recorded for the page, reloading removes the chip and shows real data (Views 1, Clicks 0, the empty states from the other cards); the chip stays gone even for a range with no activity.
For a page with published = null the chip is shown with the line 'Publish your page to start counting views.'
At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/analytics the chip wraps under the date label without overflow and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: it sits on the same line as the date label.

features.title: Free plan analytics limits enforced on read
acceptance: Free account on /analytics: 7d and 30d work; the 90d and 1y buttons carry a 'Pro' chip (brass-soft) and choosing them, or loading ?range=90 or ?range=365, shows a card 'Longer ranges come with Pro' with an 'Upgrade to Pro' link to /settings#plans instead of data; KPIs and clicks by link stay available for 7d and 30d.

Free account: the referrers, devices and countries cards are replaced by locked cards (title, 'Included with Pro', a 'See plans' link) and the footnote adds 'On Free, this page shows 30 days of per-link clicks; referrers, devices and countries come with Pro.'; Pro and Studio never show the lock or that sentence.

Server enforcement: the stats query called for a Free account with range 90 or 365 returns plan_required and runs no query for rows older than 30 days (Vitest query spy), so editing the URL cannot bypass it.

RLS enforcement (pgTAP): for a Free owner, select on daily_stats returns only rows from the last 30 UTC days and select on daily_dim_stats returns no rows; for a Pro owner both return everything; a plan flip through the webhook takes effect immediately.
Abuse case: with a Free user's JWT and the publishable key, GET /rest/v1/daily_stats?page_id=eq.<mine>&day=lt.<today minus 30 days> and GET /rest/v1/daily_dim_stats?page_id=eq.<mine> both return [].
At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/analytics the locked cards and upgrade card are full width with buttons at least 44px tall and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: they occupy the same grid cells as the unlocked cards.

features.title: Upload quota enforced on write (Free 10 MB, Pro 100 MB, Studio 1 GB)
acceptance: The upload route `POST /api/media` (profile photo, image blocks, card images and backgrounds) sums the account's stored bytes under its folder `{uid}/` in the `page-media` bucket and rejects an upload that would push the total past 10 MiB (Free), 100 MiB (Pro) or 1 GiB (Studio) with 413 upload_quota and 'Uploads are limited to 10 MB on Free. Delete an image or upgrade.' (100 MB on Pro, 1 GB on Studio), storing nothing. The plan is read server-side from accounts.plan.
Vitest or integration table: a Free account with 9 MiB used uploading 2 MiB gets 413, uploading 1 MiB is accepted (exactly at the limit is allowed); Pro with 99 MiB plus 2 MiB gets 413.

Accounting counts the bytes actually stored in the bucket under the account's folder, so an accepted upload adds its bytes (bytes freed by the Milestone 5 cleanup lower the total); a secret-key-only function account_upload_bytes(uid) returns the sum and the usage meter reads it.
Concurrency: two simultaneous uploads that together exceed the cap result in at most one accepted.

Abuse case: with the user's session and the publishable key, a direct Supabase Storage upload (POST /storage/v1/object/page-media/<uid>/big.webp) is rejected, as is an upload into another user's folder (uploads happen only through the server route; the authenticated role has no insert policy on the bucket), so the cap cannot be bypassed.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor the upload control shows the 413 message inline (role alert) with a retry control at least 44px tall, every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide) and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the message sits under the Profile photo buttons and the same limit applies to the Design background upload.

features.title: Usage meters on the billing screen
acceptance: The Usage card on /settings shows four meters in an auto-fit grid (min 190px): Pages 'n / limit', Custom domains 'n / limit', Uploads 'X / Y MB' (Y shown as 10 MB, 100 MB or 1 GB) and Saved themes ('n / 3' on Free, 'n · no limit' with a dashed empty track on Pro and Studio); the track is 6px #EFEDE9 with a brass fill of width min(100%, used / limit); numbers are mono 13px.
Free account shows Custom domains as 'Not included' with a dashed track instead of '0 / 0'.

Counts come from a server-only account_usage(uid) computed from pages, domains (through the owner's pages), saved themes and storage bytes; Vitest seeds 2 pages, 1 domain, 18 MiB and 5 themes for a Pro account and asserts '2 / 3', '1 / 1', '18 / 100 MB' and '5 · no limit'. Abuse case: POST /rest/v1/rpc/account_usage with a user JWT and the publishable key is rejected (execute revoked from anon and authenticated).
Upload formatting: under 1 MiB shows '<1 MB', up to 999 MiB shows whole MB, beyond that GB with one decimal.
Over limit (after a downgrade) the fill stays at 100% and a helper line under the meter reads 'Over your plan’s limit. What you have stays; you can’t add more.'

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/settings the meters stack in one column with no sidebar, every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide) and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the meters wrap in the grid inside the 920px column.

features.title: Downgrade keeps existing data and blocks only new writes
acceptance: Setup: a Pro account with 3 pages, 1 verified custom domain, 4 saved themes and 50 MiB uploaded receives a signed customer.subscription.deleted, so accounts.plan becomes 'free'.

Nothing is deleted or unpublished: the 3 pages, the domain row, the 4 themes and the stored objects are unchanged, all three published pages and the custom host still answer 200, and the pages can still be edited and published (what happens to over-limit custom domains is deliberately not changed in this milestone).

New writes are rejected with the messages from the limit features: creating a page, adding a domain and uploading a file all fail; deleting a page, a domain or an object is allowed and the usage meter drops accordingly. Abuse case: with the publishable key a direct INSERT into pages, domains or themes past the Free limit is rejected by the database as well.

The billing meters show the over-limit state ('3 / 1' with a full bar and the helper line), analytics gating applies immediately (90d locked, 30-day RLS window) and the Made with HYDLNK badge returns on the published pages.
A later signed customer.subscription.created for Pro restores add rights with no data loss and the meters return to normal; no row was altered by the downgrade except accounts.
At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/settings the over-limit meter row and helper text wrap with `scrollWidth <= innerWidth` and every button at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the over-limit meters render in the 920px grid without overflow.

features.title: Account deletion cancels billing, removes custom domains and uploaded images
acceptance: Extends the Milestone 1 Delete account flow at http://app.localhost:3000/settings. For an account with an active subscription the modal adds a line 'Your Pro subscription will be canceled.' (Studio for Studio). Confirming first cancels each active subscription of the account's customer through the Stripe stub (exactly one cancel request per subscription), then removes each custom domain from the project through the Vercel stub, then deletes the user's objects under `{uid}/` in the `page-media` bucket, and only then deletes the auth user (cascade removes pages, themes, domains, events and stats).

If the Stripe or Vercel stub fails, nothing is deleted and the dialog shows 'We couldn’t cancel your subscription. Try again.' or 'We couldn’t remove your custom domain. Try again.'; the account, pages, domains and files are intact and a retry succeeds once the stub recovers (so a failed delete never leaves a paying zombie account or a domain stuck on the project).

After deletion: the stub log shows the cancel and remove requests, the `page-media` listing for the uid is empty, accounts.plan changes by webhook are ignored for the deleted customer (200, no write), http://<handle>.localhost:3000/ and any custom host return 404 immediately, and the handle is free again.

Abuse case: the action deletes only the session user; a request carrying another user's id or customer id cancels nothing for them; an unauthenticated call returns 401 and calls no stub; a wrong confirmation text is rejected server-side before any stub call.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/settings with the dialog open: the extra line wraps, buttons are full width, stacked and at least 44px tall, every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide) and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the dialog stays centered at max-width 440px with the subscription line above the confirmation field.

features.title: Done when: upgrading to Pro unlocks a custom domain that serves over SSL, and its clicks show in the dashboard next day
acceptance: Local automated run (Playwright in both the 390x844 and 1440x900 projects, Vercel stub, signed Stripe webhook fixtures): a Free account's /domains shows 'Custom domains start on Pro.' and no domain input; a signed customer.subscription.created for the Pro monthly price flips the plan; /domains now shows the add form and the usage line '0 of 1 used on Pro'.

Add links.example.test serving the account's published page; flip the stub to verified; the chip shows 'Live · SSL issued'; a browser at http://links.example.test:3000/ (host-resolver mapping) shows the same page as the subdomain.
On that host click a link: the browser follows /r/<pageId>/<blockId> to the destination; the events table holds one view and one click for the page, with no Set-Cookie on any response.

Run rollup_daily_stats for that UTC day (the manual stand-in for the nightly job); /analytics for that page shows Views of at least 1, Clicks 1 and the link in 'Clicks by link' under its label, with no 'Sample data' chip, at 390x844 and 1440x900 without horizontal scroll (`scrollWidth <= innerWidth`) and with every button and link at least 44px tall at 390x844.

Production sandbox run (performed by Gary as part of release; unattended sessions never touch production): upgrade a test account through real Stripe Checkout with the test card 4242 4242 4242 4242 and confirm the webhook flips the plan to Pro on https://app.hydlnk.com/settings; add a hostname Gary controls (recorded in PROGRESS.md), create the DNS record the Domains screen shows, and wait for or press 'Check DNS now' until 'Live · SSL issued'.

Production: curl -sI https://<that host>/ returns HTTP 200 with a certificate that verifies without -k, and the page renders at 390x844 and 1440x900; clicking a link on that host redirects through /r/<pageId>/<blockId> and an events row is visible via SQL.

Production, next UTC day after the nightly pg_cron job has run: https://app.hydlnk.com/analytics shows that click and view for the page; screenshots at both viewports and the cron.job_run_details row are saved as evidence in PROGRESS.md.

Cleanup: remove the test domain with 'Remove domain' (the Vercel project no longer lists it) and return the test account to Free through the portal; no live Stripe account or other business's data is touched.

features.title: Per-IP rate limit on the view beacon /api/e, and the rate-limit mechanism decision
acceptance: Decision recorded in docs/PLAN.md (the Open item moves to Decided) naming the mechanism behind one rateLimit(key, limit, windowSeconds) function used by /api/e, /r, uploads and reports, with the reason for the choice; the mechanism must work in local dev and in Playwright, and any platform rule (e.g. a Vercel Firewall rule) is only a coarse backstop in front of it.

Vitest on rateLimit with limit 120 per 60 s: calls 1-120 for IP 203.0.113.7 are allowed, call 121 is blocked with retryAfter between 1 and 60, a call for 198.51.100.9 in the same window is allowed, and after the window rolls over 203.0.113.7 is allowed again.

Playwright API test: POST http://mara.localhost:3000/api/e with a valid view-beacon body for the seed mara page and header x-forwarded-for: 203.0.113.7, 121 times inside one minute. Requests 1-120 return 204; request 121 returns 429 with a Retry-After header and does not add an events row; the same body from 198.51.100.9 immediately afterwards returns 204.

Every request counts toward the limit, including malformed JSON bodies and bot or HEAD requests, and the limit check runs before any events insert (Vitest asserts the insert function is never called for a blocked request).

Direct-curl abuse: a request with no client-IP header is counted in one shared 'unknown' bucket instead of skipping the limit, and the key is the platform-supplied client IP, never a value taken from the beacon body. If the limiter is backed by the database, its RPC and counter table are rejected for anon and authenticated with the publishable key.
If the counter store throws, the beacon still returns 204 and the error is logged (fail open), so a limiter outage never breaks page views.

features.title: Per-IP rate limit on the click redirect /r
acceptance: Using the same rateLimit function, GET http://mara.localhost:3000/r/{pageId}/{blockId} allows 60 requests per minute per IP: requests 1-60 from 203.0.113.7 return 302 with Location equal to the block's published URL (and one click row each, bots excluded as before); request 61 returns 429 with a Retry-After header, no Location header and no new events row; the same request from 198.51.100.9 returns 302.
The limit is per IP across all pages and blocks: 30 requests to block A plus 31 to block B from one IP trip on request 61, so rotating blockIds or pageIds does not dodge it.
The 429 body is a small HYDLNK-styled page reading 'Too many clicks from your network. Try again in a minute.'. A blocked request performs no pages lookup and no events insert (Vitest spies on both).

Direct-curl abuse: GET /r/{pageId}/{blockId}?to=https://evil.example never redirects to evil.example, and a request with no client-IP header lands in the shared 'unknown' bucket rather than bypassing the limit.
If the counter store throws, the redirect still returns 302 and the error is logged (fail open): a limiter outage must never break a visitor's click.
At 390x844 on the 429 page: document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= 390, it has no horizontal scroll and any link on it measures at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the 429 page: it is centered and uses HYDLNK UI tokens (not tenant tokens).

features.title: Link blocklist: rejected when a draft is saved and again at Publish
acceptance: A new migration creates blocked_domains (domain text primary key, reason text, created_at) with RLS on and no policies for anon or authenticated, and seeds it from a reviewed starter list in the migration (not seed.sql). Later entries are added through new migrations (db-change skill) in v1. pgTAP proves anon and authenticated get permission denied or zero rows for select, insert, update and delete on it.

A trigger on pages (insert, and update of draft) calls a SQL function that extracts every URL-valued field in the draft document (link, card, embed, image link, social row items, 2-column grid children) and raises an exception with message blocked_link and the offending host in detail when the host matches blocked_domains or a built-in rule (IP-literal hosts and single-label hosts such as localhost).

pgTAP as an authenticated page owner with blocked.example in the blocklist: UPDATE pages SET draft containing https://blocked.example/x throws blocked_link, the same draft with https://ok.example succeeds, and the stored draft is unchanged after the failed update.

Matching table test, shared as one JSON fixture file that Vitest also loads. Rejected: https://BLOCKED.example, https://blocked.example. (trailing dot), https://www.blocked.example/a?b=1, https://a.b.blocked.example, https://good.example@blocked.example/, https://blocked.example:8443/, https://blocked%2Eexample/, and a blocked URL inside a grid child. Allowed: https://notblocked.example, https://xblocked.example and https://blocked.example.evil.test.

Direct-API abuse: with the publishable key and the owner's JWT, PATCH {SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/pages?id=eq.{id} with a draft containing a blocklisted URL returns a 4xx whose message contains blocked_link and the stored draft is unchanged.

Editor at http://app.localhost:3000/editor: typing https://blocked.example into a link block's URL field shows the inline error 'That site is blocked. Use a different link.' under that field, the autosave status shows 'Not saved' (without the retry message, because the error is permanent), and Publish is disabled; changing the URL to https://ok.example clears the error and the status returns to 'Saved'.

Publish re-checks: the publish Server Action takes only a page id, reads the saved draft and runs the same function again. With blocked.example added to blocked_domains after the draft was saved, publish returns blocked_link with the offending hosts; pages.published and published_at are unchanged and updateTag is never called. The editor shows 'Can’t publish. 1 link points to a blocked site: blocked.example. Remove or change it.', expands the first affected block, and http://mara.localhost:3000 still serves the previously published content. After the link is removed, Publish succeeds and the chip changes to 'Published'.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor the field error and the publish banner are visible without horizontal scroll (`scrollWidth <= innerWidth`), the banner sits above the bottom tab bar, the URL input uses 16px text and every tappable target measures at least 44px.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the layout matches Editor.dc.html and DESIGN.md.

features.title: Admin area at /admin, admins only
acceptance: ADMIN_USER_IDS (comma-separated auth user UUIDs, optional, empty means nobody is admin) is added to .env.example and the Zod env schema; Gary sets the production value. Admin identity comes from the verified Supabase session (getClaims), never from a request field.

Unauthenticated GET http://app.localhost:3000/admin redirects to sign-in. A signed-in non-admin gets a 404 (identical to an unknown route) for /admin, /admin/reports, /admin/pages and /admin/traffic. A signed-in admin gets 200. The same paths on http://mara.localhost:3000 return the tenant 404.

Direct-API abuse: a signed-in non-admin POSTing the exact Server Action request captured from the admin UI (the suspend action) gets 403 and the target row is unchanged; an unauthenticated POST gets 401; both cases are covered for every admin mutation.

Every admin mutation (Server Actions and any /api/admin routes) calls one shared requireAdmin(). A Vitest suite iterates a registry of admin actions, calls each with a non-admin session and expects 403 with no database write, so adding an unguarded action fails the test.
Admin shell follows DESIGN.md (>= 760px: 240px charcoal sidebar; < 760px: top bar) with sections Reports, Pages and Traffic; an Admin link appears in the sidebar user area for admins only.
At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/admin the section nav wraps in a segmented control with `scrollWidth <= innerWidth` and every tappable target measures at least 44px.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the shell matches Analytics.dc.html (header bar with mono breadcrumb and 22px title).

features.title: Report a page: form, submission and the public-page link target
acceptance: A new migration creates reports (id, page_id nullable with on delete set null, reason, details, reporter_email nullable, reporter_hash, status open/dismissed/actioned default open, created_at, resolved_at) with RLS on and no client policies. pgTAP: anon and authenticated get permission denied or zero rows for select, insert, update and delete.

Direct-API abuse: POST {SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/reports with the publishable key, both anonymous and with a user JWT, is rejected and no row is written. The reporter IP is stored only as a salted hash with a daily-rotating salt, never as a raw IP.

http://localhost:3000/report?page={pageId} shows 'Report a page' with the page's address read server-side (handle only, no page content), a reason select (Phishing or scam, Malware, Impersonation, Illegal content, Spam, Something else), a details textarea (max 1000 characters, required for Something else), an optional email and a 'Send report' button. Without ?page= it shows an address field; a known handle or custom domain resolves, an unknown one shows 'We couldn’t find that page. Check the address.'.

The 'Report this page' link in every public page footer (Milestone 2, pointing at /report?page={pageId}) now resolves: clicking it on http://mara.localhost:3000 opens this form with 'mara.hydlnk.com' prefilled, and a 'Report a page' link in the marketing footer opens it with the address field. The link is present on Free and Pro pages, on subdomain and custom-domain hosts and under every system theme, and cannot be hidden or restyled out of view by a block, a per-block override or a theme token (Vitest renders the page under each theme).

Submitting inserts one reports row with status open and shows 'Report sent. We’ll review it.'. The same hashed IP reporting the same page again within 24 hours inserts nothing but shows the same message. A filled hidden honeypot field also shows the same message and inserts nothing.

Validation runs server-side with Zod: a direct POST with 5000 characters of details, an unknown reason or an invalid email is rejected with a 4xx and no row is written; the inline errors name the field and what to do.
Using rateLimit, the 6th report from one IP within an hour shows 'Too many reports. Try again later.' and inserts nothing; a different IP is unaffected.

At 390x844 on http://localhost:3000/report the form has `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, inputs use 16px text and every tappable target measures at least 44px; the footer link on http://mara.localhost:3000 stays at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: it sits inside the marketing page chrome of Main.dc.html with field and error styles matching Signup.dc.html.

features.title: Admin report queue
acceptance: /admin/reports (admin only) lists reports newest first with a segmented control Open | Resolved | All (default Open): created time, page address (opens the public page in a new tab with rel=noopener noreferrer), reason, the first 120 characters of details, reporter email (admin only), a count of reports for the same page and a status chip. Empty state reads 'No open reports.'.
Row actions Dismiss (sets status dismissed and resolved_at) and Suspend owner (starts the suspend flow from the admin suspend feature), both guarded by requireAdmin().
A report whose page was deleted shows 'Page deleted' and offers Dismiss only.
Reporter-supplied text is rendered escaped: a report whose details are <script>alert(1)</script> shows the literal text and nothing executes.

Direct-API abuse: a signed-in non-admin GET {SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/reports with the publishable key returns no rows or permission denied, and the Dismiss action called by a non-admin returns 403 with the row unchanged.
At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/admin/reports the table collapses to stacked cards with `scrollWidth <= innerWidth` and Dismiss and Suspend measure at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the table matches the data-table style of Analytics.dc.html (mono numbers, header row on --hl-page).

features.title: Admin suspend and unsuspend an account
acceptance: /admin/pages?q= searches by handle, custom hostname or owner email and lists handle, owner email, plan, a state chip (Live, Unpublished, Suspended) and the number of pages the account owns.

Suspend account (from a page row or a report row) opens a confirm reading 'Suspend {handle}? All {n} of its pages stop serving right away.'. Confirming runs a requireAdmin() Server Action that sets accounts.suspended_at = now() with the secret key, calls `invalidateAccountPages` (Milestone 2) for the account and marks that account's open reports actioned.

Unsuspend clears suspended_at and invalidates the same tags; both actions are idempotent, so a double click shows no error. Suspending an account listed in ADMIN_USER_IDS is refused with 'Admins can’t be suspended.'.

Direct-API abuse: as the suspended owner, PATCH {SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/accounts?id=eq.{ownId} with {suspended_at: null} using the publishable key leaves suspended_at set (pgTAP); a signed-in non-admin calling the suspend action gets 403 and nothing changes; an unauthenticated call gets 401.
At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/admin/pages the search, confirm dialog and buttons are usable with `scrollWidth <= innerWidth` and every tappable target at least 44px.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the layout matches Analytics.dc.html.

features.title: Suspended pages stop serving
acceptance: After suspending the mara account, GET http://mara.localhost:3000/ returns HTTP 404 with a page reading 'This page isn’t available.' and <meta name=robots content=noindex>. The public query already reads the owner's accounts row for the plan; it now also reads suspended_at. The HTML contains none of the tenant's display name, bio, link titles, link URLs, avatar or OG tags. The same holds for a custom-domain host (Host header links.example.localhost against a verified domains row) and for the page's OG image URL.

No stale copy: Playwright fetches http://mara.localhost:3000/ (200 with content), runs the suspend action, then fetches again immediately and gets the 404 page, never the old 200 (cache tag invalidated).

Tracking stops at request time, not from cached HTML: after suspension GET /r/{pageId}/{blockId} returns 404 with no Location header and writes no events row, and POST /api/e returns 204 and writes no events row. Existing events and daily_stats rows are kept.
Unsuspend: the same URL returns 200 with the original published content without republishing, /r returns 302 again and /api/e records views again.

Direct-API abuse: the suspended owner cannot bring the page back by republishing (Publish returns 403 account_suspended) or by writing `published` with the publishable key (rejected), so the 404 holds until an admin unsuspends.
The handle stays held: the sign-up handle check for mara still says taken while suspended, and mara.localhost:3000 never shows the unclaimed 'Claim it' page. Other accounts' pages are unaffected.
At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/ the unavailable page is centered with `scrollWidth <= innerWidth` and its 'Go to hydlnk.com' link measures at least 44px.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: it uses HYDLNK UI tokens (Main.dc.html charcoal and brass), never tenant tokens.

features.title: Suspended owner: writes blocked and a banner shown
acceptance: A new migration (never an edit to a committed one) changes the pages update policy so the owner can update draft only while accounts.suspended_at is null, and applies the same condition to themes insert, update and delete. pgTAP: as a suspended owner, UPDATE pages SET draft leaves the row unchanged and a themes insert is rejected; after unsuspend both succeed; reads of the owner's own rows still work.

Direct-API abuse: with the publishable key and the suspended owner's JWT, PATCH {SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/pages?id=eq.{id} with a new draft leaves the stored draft unchanged. Publish, create page, add domain and upload each return 403 with code account_suspended when called directly with the owner's session cookie, and write nothing.

A suspended user can still sign in at http://app.localhost:3000 and sees every app screen with a persistent banner in the DESIGN.md error style (--hl-bad text, #E8C4BD border): 'Your account is suspended. Your pages are offline. Contact {SUPPORT_EMAIL} to appeal.' with a mailto link. SUPPORT_EMAIL is added to .env.example and the Zod env schema.

Publish, Add domain, Upload photo and New page render disabled with the same reason as a tooltip or helper text; Sign out still works. After an admin unsuspends the account, the banner is gone on the next navigation and Publish works again.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor the banner does not overlap the top bar or the bottom tab bar, there is no horizontal scroll (`scrollWidth <= innerWidth`) and every tappable target measures at least 44px.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the banner sits above the page header inside the main column per Editor.dc.html.

features.title: High-traffic flag job for Free pages, with admin review list
acceptance: A migration creates traffic_flags (id, page_id on delete cascade, window_start, window_end, views, flagged_at, reviewed_at nullable) with RLS on and no client policies. pgTAP, and direct-API abuse: select and insert with the publishable key (anonymous and authenticated) are rejected.

SQL function flag_high_traffic_pages(threshold integer default 100000) sums the page-level views in daily_stats over the trailing 30 days (ending yesterday) for pages whose owner has accounts.plan = 'free' and inserts a flag when the sum exceeds the threshold. pgTAP: a Free page with 100,001 views gets exactly one flag with views = 100001; a Free page with 99,999 gets none; Pro and Studio pages with 500,000 get none.

Idempotent: a second call the same night adds no row; no new flag is created while an unreviewed flag exists or for 30 days after reviewed_at; after that a still-over page is flagged again. A pg_cron job flag-high-traffic exists and is scheduled after the nightly rollup job (pgTAP asserts the cron.job row). The function is not executable by anon or authenticated (POST /rest/v1/rpc/flag_high_traffic_pages with the publishable key is rejected).
Flagged pages keep serving: after the job flags the seed page, http://mara.localhost:3000/ still returns 200 and pages.published is unchanged.

/admin/traffic lists unreviewed flags with handle, owner email, plan, views in the last 30 days (mono, thousands separators) and flagged date; Mark reviewed (requireAdmin) moves a row to the Reviewed filter; empty state reads 'No pages are over the Free-plan traffic line.'. A non-admin gets 404 on the page and 403 on the action.
At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/admin/traffic the list collapses to stacked cards with `scrollWidth <= innerWidth` and every tappable target at least 44px.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: it matches the data-table style of Analytics.dc.html.

features.title: Avatar upload pipeline: 400px WebP with long cache headers
acceptance: Upload photo posts to the existing `POST http://app.localhost:3000/api/media` with kind=avatar (signed-in owner). The route outputs one image/webp at most 400x400 (square cover crop), applies EXIF orientation, strips all metadata, stores it as `{uid}/avatar-{content-hash}.webp` in the `page-media` bucket (the Milestone 2 bucket, mime allowlist and 4 MB limit are unchanged; new objects are always image/webp) with cache-control max-age=31536000, and the draft's `profile.photo` becomes `{path, width, height}` for it. The original is never stored.

Test: a 3000x2000 JPEG with GPS EXIF produces a stored 400x400 WebP under 100 KB with no GPS metadata, and no JPEG object exists in any bucket afterwards. curl -I on the public avatar URL shows content-type image/webp and cache-control max-age=31536000, locally and on production.

Filenames contain the content hash: uploading different bytes yields a new URL and never overwrites a path; uploading identical bytes twice yields the same URL and does not double-count quota. Replace gives a different URL and updates the draft; Remove clears `profile.photo` and the initials fallback shows. The live page keeps showing the old avatar until Publish.

A 9 MB 6000x4000 phone JPEG chosen in the editor uploads successfully, including on production: the browser downsizes it (canvas, longest edge at most 2400px) before sending because Vercel caps function request bodies at 4.5 MB (confirm in current docs); a request body over 4 MB sent directly still gets 413 file_too_large.

Direct-API abuse: an unauthenticated POST to the route returns 401; a form field naming another owner or folder is ignored and the object lands under the session uid; with the publishable key a direct Storage upload is still rejected.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor the upload control shows uploading and done states, every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide) and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.

At 1440x900 on the same URL: the profile section matches Editor.dc.html, with no layout shift when the new avatar loads, and the public page markup has no /_next/image URL for the avatar (the img carries width, height and decoding=async).

features.title: Background and content image pipeline: 1600px WebP
acceptance: The same route with kind=background (Design background) and kind=content (image blocks and card images, an assumption: PLAN names only the avatar and background sizes) outputs an image/webp whose longest edge is at most 1600px, aspect ratio preserved and never upscaled, stored as `{uid}/bg-{content-hash}.webp` or `{uid}/img-{content-hash}.webp` with cache-control max-age=31536000. Metadata is stripped and the original is never stored. The draft's bgImage token receives the public URL and image and card blocks receive `{path, width, height}`.

features.title: Undo and redo history: one shared engine for every draft change
acceptance: Vitest (pnpm test): a framework-free module, src/lib/editor/history.ts, with no server-only import (it runs in jsdom and in node), keeps `past`, `present` and `future` as whole `DraftDoc` snapshots held by reference (immutable updates share untouched blocks, asserted with `===` on a block that did not change). `rev` is not part of a step: a restored draft takes the current `rev`.

Only real edits count: pushing the same draft object twice adds one entry, and the editor reducer’s no-op actions (which return the same state object) add none. Undo with an empty `past` and redo with an empty `future` return the same history object, which is what disables the buttons.

Coalescing, with an injected clock: edits tagged with the same group key (`profile/name`, `profile/bio`, `block:{id}:{field}`) that arrive less than 1000 ms after the previous one of that group merge into one step. Typing 'Hello world' as 11 keystrokes 100 ms apart and then undoing restores the text from before the first keystroke in one step; a pause of 1500 ms, or a different field, starts a new step. Add, insert, duplicate, delete, move, reorder, visibility, upload and theme changes never merge.

Cap: at most 100 undo steps; the 101st edit drops the oldest. Redo reapplies steps in order; any new edit clears the redo stack. A 100-step history of a 200 KB draft keeps untouched blocks shared between snapshots instead of copying them.

Images: when the snapshot an undo or redo would restore holds an image path that the present draft does not, the engine reports the paths and the screen first sends one HEAD request per path to its public URL. If every file answers 200 the step applies; if one answers 404 nothing changes, the history is untouched and the screen shows 'Can’t undo that. The earlier image was already deleted.' (for redo: 'Can’t redo that. That image was already deleted.'); a network error applies the step (fail open). Vitest with a stubbed fetch covers 200, 404 and a thrown error.

The history lives in memory only: nothing is written to localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, cookies or the database, and Undo makes no request except those HEAD checks (static scan plus a network log). A reload or leaving the screen starts with an empty history.

One write path: after Undo or Redo the restored draft goes to the autosave queue like any edit and is sent with `rev` equal to the stored rev plus one, never an older number. Stale-tab guard on the Undo write itself, with two browser contexts as mara: B loads at rev N, edits the bio and autosaves (rev N+1); A loads afterwards, edits the display name and saves (rev N+2); B presses Undo. B’s PATCH is conditional on rev N+1, matches 0 rows, B shows 'This page changed in another tab. Reload to keep editing.', and the database keeps A’s content (the new name and B’s first bio edit).

Coexistence: the 'Block deleted.' toast and its Undo (M2-13) and the 'Applied Ivory.' Undo (M3-20) keep restoring exactly what they restore today, and each of those restores is recorded as one history step, so history Undo right after the toast’s Undo removes the restored block again and history Redo brings it back.

features.title: Preview links: server-only table, 7-day expiry, create and turn off
acceptance: A new migration (the db-change skill; no committed migration is edited) creates `preview_links` (`id uuid` primary key, `page_id` references pages on delete cascade, `token_hash text not null unique` with a check for 64 lowercase hex characters, `created_at`, `expires_at not null default now() + interval '7 days'`, `revoked_at`) with a check that `expires_at > created_at and expires_at <= created_at + interval '7 days'`. RLS is on, no policy exists and every privilege is revoked from anon and authenticated; only service_role has grants. pgTAP: the table, RLS and the constraints exist; select, insert, update and delete as authenticated and anon are denied; an 8-day expiry and a 10-character hash are rejected; the server-only table list of test 010 includes it.

Active-link cap: a BEFORE INSERT trigger raises `preview_link_limit` when the page already has 5 links that are neither revoked nor expired (by the database clock), even for the postgres and service roles; two simultaneous inserts at 4 of 5 yield exactly one row (advisory lock). pgTAP covers the 6th insert, the freed slot after a revoke, and the freed slot after expiry.

Server Action `createPreviewLink(pageId)` (`'use server'`, imports the secret-key client under `server-only`): no session is rejected as unauthorized; a page of another account answers `not_found` and creates nothing; a suspended owner gets `account_suspended` and creates nothing (M5-09); Free, Pro and Studio accounts can all create links (no plan check). On success it returns `{ok:true, id, url, expiresAt}` where `url` is http://app.localhost:3000/share/{token}, the token is 32 bytes from the platform CSPRNG, base64url, 43 characters (256 bits), and only its SHA-256 hex is stored: a secret-key `select *` of the row has no token column and the hash does not equal the token. `expires_at` comes from the database default, never from the caller. The token is never logged.

`listPreviewLinks(pageId)` returns the owner’s active links newest first as `{id, createdAt, expiresAt}` and never a token or hash; `revokePreviewLink(id)` sets `revoked_at = now()` on an active link of a page the caller owns, is safe to repeat, and answers `not_found` for another account’s link id, for a random uuid and for a link of another user’s page, changing nothing. Vitest plus a two-user Playwright check.

Limits on write: at the cap the action returns `preview_link_limit` with 'You have 5 active preview links. Turn one off to make another.' and creates nothing; with `rateLimit('preview-link:{userId}', 20, 3600)` the 21st create within an hour returns 429 `rate_limited` with 'You’ve created a lot of links. Try again in a while.' and a different user is unaffected.

Direct-API abuse: with the owner’s JWT and the publishable key, GET, POST, PATCH and DELETE on /rest/v1/preview_links fail (permission denied or an empty result), so a client cannot read a hash, plant a row with a chosen hash or a one-year expiry, or revive a revoked link; calling the actions with another user’s page id from a replayed request returns `not_found`. A client import of the action module fails the build through `server-only`, and after `pnpm build` no `sb_secret_` string appears in `.next/static`.

Retention and cascade: a pg_cron job 'purge-preview-links' at '40 0 * * *' deletes links whose `expires_at` or `revoked_at` is more than 30 days old and keeps younger ones (pgTAP asserts the cron.job row and that its command text holds no secret); deleting the page or the account removes its links (test 070 extended).

Types and docs: `pnpm db:types` is regenerated; docs/PLAN.md (Data model table and Decided list) records the table as server-only and the share link as the one ungated route that reads `draft`, by an unguessable, expiring, revocable link; .claude/rules/tenant-pages.md keeps 'Never read draft on a public path' and names this one exception, and .claude/rules/editor-app.md notes that /share/* is the only ungated route on the app host that reads a draft with the secret key.

features.title: The shared preview page: your draft, by private link
acceptance: GET http://app.localhost:3000/share/{token} with a valid link returns 200 with no session needed (the route sits outside the signed-in screens: no gate, no sidebar, no tab bar; it works signed out and as another user). It finds the page by the token’s SHA-256, reads that page’s saved draft with the secret key under `server-only`, and draws it with `PageRenderer` in `mode='preview'` from `toPublishForm(draft, themeTokens)` with its fonts loaded as on the live page. `<title>` is 'Preview of {display name}'. A slim bar at the top (`role='status'`) reads 'Draft preview. Not published yet.' and 'This link expires October 10, 2026.'. The footer shows the 'Made with HYDLNK' badge by the owner’s plan and no report link.

It shows the draft as saved at the moment of the request, with no snapshot: after the owner edits the bio and autosave finishes, a reload of the same link shows the new bio. A string that exists only in the draft ('DRAFT-ONLY-7f3a') appears here and never on http://mara.localhost:3000/ (M2-22 still holds); hidden blocks are absent and incomplete blocks show the dashed placeholders ('Image', 'Embed').

Response headers: `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` (and a robots meta tag with the same value), `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, a Content-Security-Policy with `frame-src https://www.youtube-nocookie.com https://open.spotify.com; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, no Open Graph or Twitter tags, and the response is dynamic (never `x-nextjs-cache: HIT`). A page component cannot set response headers, so the proxy sets them by path for /share/* on the app host. For this path the proxy only rewrites: it neither reads nor refreshes the session, so there is no Set-Cookie even when a signed-in owner opens the link.

No tracking and no way out: the page renders no view beacon and sends no POST to /api/e; the `events` count read with the secret key is the same before and after ten visits; clicking a link, card, social icon or grid cell leaves the URL unchanged and sends no request to /r/ (the preview wrapper stops anchors as the editor does); embeds stay inert posters and play nothing.

Anything that is not an active link answers the same HTTP 404 with the same body, 'This preview link isn’t active. Ask the owner for a new link.', and no page content: an unknown 43-character token, a malformed one ('abc', a 100-character string, '../x'), an expired link (`expires_at` moved into the past with the secret key), a revoked link, a link whose owner is suspended (M5-09) and a link whose page was deleted. The bodies are compared and are identical; a malformed token never reaches the database (DB spy). After 'Turn off' (M6-12) the very next request is the 404, because nothing is cached.

Abuse case and rate limit: `rateLimit('share:{ip}', 60, 60)`: the 61st request in a minute gets 429 with `Retry-After` and the same plain page, another IP is unaffected, and a limiter failure lets the request through (logged without the key). A token for page A never draws page B whatever else is in the URL (extra path, query string or a `?page=` parameter are ignored), and a token from one account does nothing for another.

Isolation: a Vitest static scan shows that no module under src/app/(tenant), src/app/(marketing) or src/components/tenant selects `draft`, and that the share route is the only ungated page route that does; the route selects named columns only (never `*`) and reads nothing of the owner’s account but the plan and the suspension state.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/share/{token} the status bar wraps, the page fills the viewport width with no horizontal scroll (`scrollWidth <= innerWidth`), and every link and button in the footer has a bounding box at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the bar spans the top of the viewport, the page column is no wider than 480px and centered, and the background covers the viewport.

The icon sits at the start edge of the button; the label stays centered in the space left and wraps without going under it; the button keeps at least 58px at regular density and at least 44px at compact and airy; the icon follows the button style (fill, outline, soft, shadow, pill) and any color override because it uses `currentColor`.

Upload errors show inline under the buttons with role=alert and the M5-13 sentences ('That file type isn’t supported. Use JPEG, PNG or WebP.', 'That file is too big. Use an image under 4 MB.', 'We couldn’t read that image. Try a different file.'); a Free fixture at its upload limit sees 'Uploads are limited to 10 MB on Free. Delete an image or upgrade.' with a 'Try again' button (44px), and the existing icon is left unchanged in every failure.

Publish errors from M6-20 appear under the Icon field of that block ('Pick an icon from the list.', 'That image isn’t in your uploads. Upload it again.', 'That image is no longer available. Upload it again.'); the editor expands the block and moves focus to 'Choose icon'. A suspended owner (M5-09) sees the upload button disabled with the suspension reason, as for every other upload.

features.title: Featured link: bolder style with optional gentle motion
acceptance: Schema: a link block gains an optional `featured` of `'bold'`, `'pulse'` or `'shine'` (absent means not featured; `pulse` and `shine` are the bold style plus that motion). Vitest: the three values parse; `'blink'`, `true`, `1` and a string with quotes are rejected at Publish; unknown keys are stripped; `toPublishForm` copies `featured` only when set. It is a block field, not a token override: the M3-18 rule still holds (the resolver and the schema keep exactly the allowed override keys, Vitest) and the `overrides` object never carries it.

Limit on write: at most 3 visible featured links per page (`LIMITS.featuredLinks`). Publish rejects a 4th (in page order) with 'Feature up to 3 links. Turn one off to feature another.' naming that block; hidden blocks do not count because Publish drops them. A direct PostgREST draft with 5 featured links (publishable key, owner’s JWT) is accepted by the database like any draft but Publish rejects it and `pages.published` stays unchanged. In the editor the 'Feature this link' switch on a 4th link is disabled and shows the same sentence.

Editor panel of a link block (Playwright 1440x900 as mara at http://app.localhost:3000/editor): a 'Feature this link' toggle switch (the DESIGN.md toggle in a 44px row) with the hint 'Makes this link stand out. You can feature up to 3.'; turning it on shows a 16px 'Motion' select with 'None', 'Gentle pulse' and 'Soft shine' and the hint 'Motion turns off for people who ask their device for less motion.'; turning it off removes `featured`. The block row shows a 'Featured' chip (mono 11px, brass-soft background, hidden below 760px like the override chip). The feature is on every plan.

Renderer: the anchor carries `data-featured` set from a lookup of the three allowed values (an unknown stored value renders no attribute: Vitest). Bold style: font weight 700, 8px more minimum height than a normal link at the same density, and a 2px ring in `--t-accent` drawn outside the border. Playwright computed styles on the page for each of the five button styles (fill, outline, soft, shadow, pill) and for a block with a color override: the featured anchor has weight 700 and a ring box-shadow, the shadow style keeps its offset shadow as well, the ring follows the block’s accent override, and every featured anchor is at least 44px tall.

Motion: `pulse` makes the ring breathe (about 2.4s, ease-in-out, infinite) and `shine` sweeps a soft highlight across the button about every 4s; both are CSS only, drawn from `--t-accent` and `color-mix` of tokens, and run only inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. Playwright with `reducedMotion: 'reduce'`: `getComputedStyle(anchor).animationName` and the same for `::after` are 'none' for every value and nothing moves; with `no-preference` the animation name is set. No JavaScript drives the motion.

The M2-05 static test is narrowed, not removed, and the change is recorded in PROGRESS.md as an accepted deviation for Gary to confirm: renderer CSS may contain `@media` only for `prefers-reduced-motion`; viewport or width media queries and `vw` units stay banned, every selector stays scoped under `[data-page-root]`, there are still no color literals and no `--hl-` references (the existing assertions in tests/unit/renderer-static.test.ts are updated to say exactly this).

Nothing else about the link changes: the href is still `/r/<pageId>/<blockId>` and clicks are tracked as in M4-22; the editor preview and the live page show identical markup for a featured link (Vitest `renderToStaticMarkup` in both modes, plus a Playwright compare after Publish); the change shows as 'Unpublished changes' until Publish (M2-27).

At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/ (published fixture with one 'bold', one 'pulse' and one 'shine' link and an 80-character label): the ring is not clipped by the column, `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, and every anchor is at least 44px tall.

At 1440x900 on the same URL: the featured buttons stay within the 480px column and the animation does not shift neighboring blocks (the page height is the same at the start and halfway through a cycle).

features.title: Image focus point and shapes: schema, Publish form and renderer
acceptance: Schema: the image reference `{path, width, height}` gains an optional `focus:{x, y}`, two numbers from 0 to 1 (0,0 is the top-left corner, 0.5 and 0.5 the center). Vitest: values outside 0 to 1, strings, `null` inside the object and extra keys are rejected or stripped; `toPublishForm` rounds to 3 decimals and omits a focus of exactly 0.5 and 0.5 so equal drafts stay deep-equal. Focus is kept only on card images, image blocks and the share image (M6-32); `toPublishForm` drops it from the profile photo and from link thumbnails, which are already square crops.

Image block: a new optional `shape` of `'square'`, `'landscape'` or `'wide'` (absent means the original shape, so every existing block keeps identical markup). Renderer: the image sits in a frame with `aspect-ratio` 1/1, 4/3 or 16/9 set in CSS before the file loads (no layout shift: the frame’s height is the same before and after load), `object-fit: cover`, the radius token, and `object-position` from the focus; an anchor still wraps the frame when the block has a link. With the original shape the image is drawn as today (`width` and `height` attributes, natural ratio) and focus has no effect.

Card banner: the 5:2 banner image uses the same `object-position` from the focus. The value is built only from the two numbers as `{x*100}% {y*100}%` with one decimal; no string from the document reaches a `style` attribute (Vitest static scan of src/components/page for how `object-position` is written). Playwright on a fixture image whose left half is red and right half blue: a card or a wide image with focus x=0 shows red at the center of the frame and focus x=1 shows blue, at 390 and 1440, and the computed `object-position` is exactly '0% 50%' or '100% 50%'.

Publish gate: an unknown shape fails with 'Pick a shape from the list.' and a focus outside the image fails with 'Choose a focus point inside the image.', each naming the block and leaving `pages.published` unchanged. Direct-API abuse: with the publishable key, a draft image block with `shape:'x"><b>'`, `focus:{x:5, y:'a'}` and `focus:{x:NaN}` written as raw JSON is rejected at Publish and the live page at http://mara.localhost:3000/ renders the old content; a hidden block with bad values does not block Publish.

Parity: the editor preview and the live page render identical markup for images with each shape and with a focus (Vitest `renderToStaticMarkup` in both modes and a Playwright compare of the block’s `outerHTML` after Publish); changing only the focus flips the chip to 'Unpublished changes'.

At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/ (published fixture: a portrait image as a wide block, a landscape image as a square block, a card with a focus): each frame is full column width at its ratio, the image fills it without stretching, `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, and every linked image and card anchor is at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: frames stay within the 480px column and keep their ratios.

features.title: Position dialog for the profile photo and link thumbnails
acceptance: Decision: the crop is made in the browser and the upload route does not change. The dialog draws the chosen square onto a canvas and uploads that file with `kind=avatar` through POST /api/media, so M5-11 still holds (a 400x400 WebP of at most 100 KB, metadata stripped, stored as `{uid}/avatar-{hash}.webp`) and no crop or focus value is stored for avatars. Vitest on `processUpload`: extra form fields named `crop`, `x`, `y`, `zoom` and `focus` are ignored, and a 3000x2000 JPEG gives the same stored bytes and path with or without them (abuse case: nothing in the request can steer the server’s crop).

Playwright 1440x900 as mara at http://app.localhost:3000/editor: choosing a file with 'Upload photo' or 'Replace photo' in the Profile card no longer uploads at once. After the real file type is checked (a text file renamed .jpg shows 'That file type isn’t supported. Use JPEG, PNG or WebP.' and no dialog), a dialog opens (`role='dialog'`, `aria-modal='true'`, labelled 'Position your photo', focus trapped) showing the picture under a square viewfinder with a circular outline. The picture can be dragged (pointer events, `touch-action: none` on the viewfinder) and zoomed with a 'Zoom' slider from 1x to 4x (a range input, 44px tall); the picture always covers the viewfinder, so there are never empty edges. Buttons: 'Reset' (secondary), 'Cancel' (secondary) and 'Use photo' (primary charcoal), each at least 44px tall.

Keyboard and screen readers: arrow keys move the picture by 10px (Shift moves 1px), plus and minus change the zoom, Escape is 'Cancel' and returns focus to the button that opened the dialog, Tab stays inside the dialog, and an `aria-live` region announces 'Zoom 200 percent'.

'Use photo' draws the viewfinder’s region at the source’s real resolution, at most 800px on a side, and uploads it (photos as JPEG at quality 0.9, PNG and WebP with transparency as PNG), then closes the dialog and shows 'Uploading...' on the button until the avatar appears. A fixture whose left half is red and right half blue, dragged so only the blue half is inside the viewfinder, gives an avatar whose center pixel is blue in the editor and in the live preview. A 6000x4000 phone JPEG with EXIF orientation 6 appears upright in the dialog and arrives as a small JPEG (so the 4.5 MB request cap is not an issue); the M5-11 downsizing still applies to uploads that do not go through the dialog.

'Cancel', Escape and a failed decode upload nothing (no POST /api/media in the network log) and leave `profile.photo` unchanged; an upload failure after 'Use photo' shows the M5-13 sentences inline under the buttons and keeps the old photo. An 'Adjust photo' button (secondary, 44px) appears when a photo exists and reopens the dialog on the stored image; if the browser cannot read it the dialog does not open and 'We couldn’t open that photo. Choose it again with Replace photo.' shows inline. Adjusting stores a new object (a new hash in the path); the live page keeps the old photo until Publish.

Supersedes the flow of M2-09 step 2 (and the file-chooser steps of the M5-11 tests): picking a file no longer uploads at once, so those tests now pick the file, click 'Use photo' and then expect 'Uploading...' and the new avatar; every other assertion of M2-09 and M5-11 stays as written, and the changed flow is recorded in PROGRESS.md as an accepted deviation for Gary to confirm. Link thumbnails (M6-20, M6-21) use the same dialog and the same upload kind: the title reads 'Position your image', the viewfinder outline is a square with the 6px radius, and the primary button reads 'Use image'. Everything else is identical, and the result is a square 400px WebP. The dialog never changes the profile photo’s shape on the page: that stays a CSS crop of the square image.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor: the dialog is a full-height sheet (`100dvh`) with Cancel and Use photo pinned at the bottom above the safe-area inset, every control is at least 44px tall, dragging the picture does not scroll the page behind it, and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the dialog is centered, about 440px wide, over a dimmed page that does not scroll; the viewfinder is 280px square.

features.title: Six more embed providers: parsing, rejection rules and Content Security Policy
acceptance: `parseEmbed(url)` accepts Vimeo, TikTok, Instagram, SoundCloud, Apple Music and Twitch in addition to YouTube and Spotify, and for each returns `{provider, kind, id, src}` with `src` rebuilt from validated parts only, never copied from the input. Vimeo: `vimeo.com/{id}`, `vimeo.com/{id}/{hash}` (unlisted) and `player.vimeo.com/video/{id}` (id 6 to 12 digits, hash 8 to 16 hex characters) become `https://player.vimeo.com/video/{id}?dnt=1`, plus `&h={hash}` when there is one. TikTok: `tiktok.com/@{user}/video/{id}` (also www. and m.) and `tiktok.com/embed/v2/{id}` (id 15 to 20 digits; the user name is checked, not copied) become `https://www.tiktok.com/embed/v2/{id}`. Instagram: `instagram.com/p/{code}`, `/reel/{code}`, `/tv/{code}` and `instagram.com/{user}/p/{code}` (code of letters, digits, `_` and `-`, 5 to 20 characters) become `https://www.instagram.com/{p|reel|tv}/{code}/embed`.

SoundCloud: `soundcloud.com/{user}/{track}`, `soundcloud.com/{user}/sets/{set}` and `soundcloud.com/{user}` (slugs of letters, digits, `_` and `-`, up to 100 characters; reserved first segments such as discover, you, search, stream, upload and pages are refused) become `https://w.soundcloud.com/player/?url=` followed by the percent-encoded `https://soundcloud.com/{user}/{track}` rebuilt from the validated slugs, with `auto_play=false`. Apple Music: `music.apple.com/{storefront}/{album|playlist|song}/{slug}/{id}`, with `?i={songId}` on an album link meaning a song (storefront two letters, slug of letters, digits and `._~%-` up to 120 characters, id 5 to 15 digits or `pl.` plus 8 to 60 letters, digits and dashes) becomes `https://embed.music.apple.com/{storefront}/{kind}/{slug}/{id}`. Twitch: `twitch.tv/{channel}` (3 to 25 letters, digits and `_`, not a reserved page such as videos, directory or settings), `twitch.tv/videos/{id}` (6 to 12 digits) and `clips.twitch.tv/{slug}` or `twitch.tv/{channel}/clip/{slug}` (slug of 8 to 100 letters, digits, `_` and `-`) become `https://player.twitch.tv/?channel={channel}`, `https://player.twitch.tv/?video=v{id}` and `https://clips.twitch.tv/embed?clip={slug}`, without a `parent` (the browser adds it when the visitor taps, see M6-27). Hosts are compared in lower case and must match exactly (no subdomain or suffix tricks, no userinfo, no port). YouTube and Spotify links parse exactly as before.

Vitest rejection table (all return null): `vimeo.com.evil.example/123456`, `evilvimeo.com/123456`, `player.vimeo.com.evil.example/video/123456`, `//vimeo.com/123456`, `https://user@vimeo.com/123456`, `https://vimeo.com:8443/123456`, `vimeo.com/channels/staffpicks`, a TikTok profile `tiktok.com/@mara`, a TikTok or Instagram or SoundCloud profile without a post, Instagram `/stories/` and `/explore/`, `soundcloud.com/discover`, Apple Music artist and browse pages, `twitch.tv/directory` and `twitch.tv/directory/game/Art`, ids with `"><script>` or percent-encoded slashes, ids over the length limits, and `javascript:`, `data:` and `blob:` URLs. Short links (`vm.tiktok.com/…`, `vt.tiktok.com/…`, `tiktok.com/t/…`, `on.soundcloud.com/…`, `spotify.link/…`, `instagr.am/…`) are not followed, because that would need the server to fetch a stranger’s URL: they return null and the form says so (step 4).

Copy: `EMBED_ERROR_MESSAGE` becomes 'Paste a link from YouTube, Spotify, Vimeo, TikTok, Instagram, SoundCloud, Apple Music or Twitch.' and the embed URL field shows it for any link that does not parse. A recognized short-link host instead shows 'That’s a short link. Open it in your browser, then copy the full address from the address bar.' Both sentences are plain text with no 'please' and no exclamation mark.

Supersedes two literals of M2-19 and one of M2-22, in the same change and recorded in PROGRESS.md as an accepted deviation for Gary to confirm: M2-19 step 2 listed Vimeo as rejected and M2-19 step 5 asserted the old sentence 'Paste a link to a YouTube video or a Spotify track, album, playlist or episode.'; their Vitest assertions are updated to the new behavior and message. Every other M2-19 rejection still rejects (a YouTube channel such as `youtube.com/@maraokafor`, `youtube.com.evil.example`, `youtu.be.evil.example`, a URL that only mentions youtube.com in its query, userinfo, `javascript:`), and the `src` of a YouTube or Spotify embed is unchanged.

Content Security Policy: `TENANT_CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY` becomes exactly `frame-src https://www.youtube-nocookie.com https://open.spotify.com https://player.vimeo.com https://www.tiktok.com https://www.instagram.com https://w.soundcloud.com https://embed.music.apple.com https://player.twitch.tv https://clips.twitch.tv; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'` (this supersedes the frame-src literal in M2-22; the other directives, `X-Content-Type-Options` and `Referrer-Policy` are unchanged, and there is still no script-src). The app host’s policy gains no frame-src, so the editor preview can load the players. Playwright on http://mara.localhost:3000/ with one embed of each provider: tapping each player (M6-27) mounts its iframe with no CSP violation in the console, and injected iframes to `https://evil.example`, `https://player.vimeo.com.evil.example` and `https://vimeo.com` (an origin that is not on the list) are blocked.

Abuse case: a direct PostgREST draft write (publishable key, owner’s JWT) of an embed block with url `https://vimeo.com.evil.example/123456`, `https://evil.example/x`, `https://www.tiktok.com/@mara/video/1"onload="alert(1)` or `javascript:alert(1)` is accepted as a draft but rejected at Publish with the new sentence naming the block, never reaches `pages.published` and never renders on http://mara.localhost:3000/. The renderer builds every iframe `src` from `embed.src` only and never reads `block.url` for an iframe (Vitest static scan, replacing the old facade assertion); a stored embed whose URL parses to nothing renders no iframe on the live page.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor: the longest of the new messages (the 'Paste a link from …' sentence, and the short-link sentence) wraps under the URL field, the URL input keeps 16px text and at least 44px height, and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the message sits under the field inside the expanded block (max 720px column) without shifting the Caption field.

features.title: Tap-to-play embeds for Vimeo, TikTok, Instagram, SoundCloud, Apple Music and Twitch
acceptance: Privacy: every new provider renders as a facade, like YouTube. Playwright network log on http://mara.localhost:3000/ (published fixture with one embed of each of the six new providers): loading the page makes no request to vimeo.com, vimeocdn.com, tiktok.com, tiktokcdn.com, instagram.com, facebook.com, fbcdn.net, soundcloud.com, sndcdn.com, apple.com, mzstatic.com or twitch.tv (and no request to youtube or google domains for a YouTube embed, as in M2-19); no thumbnail is fetched, because the server never fetches another site to build one.

Facade: a `<button>` on the same dark poster and play disc as the YouTube facade, with `aria-label` 'Play video: {caption}' for Vimeo and TikTok, 'Watch stream: {caption}' for a Twitch channel and 'Play video: {caption}' for a Twitch video or clip, 'Show post: {caption}' for Instagram and 'Play music: {caption}' for SoundCloud and Apple Music (without the colon and caption when the caption is empty), and the caption '{caption} · {Provider}' below, where Provider is Vimeo, TikTok, Instagram, SoundCloud, Apple Music or Twitch. Facade height: 16:9 for Vimeo and Twitch, the player’s own height for SoundCloud and Apple Music (so tapping shifts nothing), and a 120px bar for TikTok and Instagram (their players are tall, so the page grows after a tap, which is a shift the visitor asked for).

After the tap the facade is replaced by an iframe with `src` from `parseEmbed(...).src` (adding `autoplay=1` for Vimeo, `auto_play=true` for SoundCloud and `autoplay=true` for Twitch; TikTok, Instagram and Apple Music add nothing), a `title` of '{caption} ({Provider} player)', the provider’s `allow` list, `allowfullscreen` where the player has a full-screen button, `referrerpolicy='strict-origin-when-cross-origin'`, and a height from one exported table `EMBED_HEIGHTS` (16:9 by aspect ratio for Vimeo and Twitch, 740 TikTok, 560 Instagram post, 640 Instagram reel, 166 SoundCloud track, 352 SoundCloud playlist or artist, 175 Apple Music song, 450 Apple Music album or playlist). Focus moves into the iframe. The old YouTube facade becomes this one shared component; the M2-05 static assertion about facade code is updated to it and keeps its rule: an iframe `src` is built from the parsed embed only, never from `block.url`.

Twitch `parent`: Twitch only plays inside a site it knows. When the visitor taps a Twitch facade the client appends `&parent={window.location.hostname}` to the parsed `src`; on http://mara.localhost:3000/ the iframe `src` ends with `parent=mara.localhost`, on a verified custom host it is that host, and in the editor preview it is the app host. The value is only ever read from `window.location.hostname` and must match `^[a-z0-9.-]{1,253}$` (anything else mounts no iframe and shows 'This embed can’t load here.'); it never comes from the document, so a stored `parent=evil.example` in a URL is dropped by `parseEmbed` (Vitest).

Editor: the embed form’s hint under the URL field names what was recognized: 'YouTube video', 'Spotify track' (and the other Spotify kinds) as before, and now 'Vimeo video', 'TikTok video', 'Instagram post', 'Instagram reel', 'SoundCloud track', 'SoundCloud playlist', 'SoundCloud artist', 'Apple Music album', 'Apple Music song', 'Apple Music playlist', 'Twitch channel', 'Twitch video' and 'Twitch clip'. The chip’s default caption 'Video or music' is unchanged (M2-10). In the editor preview a tap on a facade mounts the iframe without leaving the editor, the same as on the live page.

Parity and existing behavior: `renderToStaticMarkup` of the preview and live modes is identical for each provider, a published YouTube or Spotify embed renders as before (M2-19 steps 3 and 4 still pass), and switching an embed’s URL from one provider to another in the editor updates the preview facade at once.

At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/ (all eight providers published): every facade is full column width, every play button is at least 44px, after tapping each one its iframe does not widen the page, and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the facades and players stay within the 480px column.

features.title: Bold, italic and links in text blocks: marks, renderer and Publish form
acceptance: Schema: a text block keeps `text` (at most 600 code points, line breaks kept) and gains an optional `marks` list of at most 30 entries (`LIMITS.textMarks`): `{type:'bold', start, end}`, `{type:'italic', start, end}` and `{type:'link', start, end, id, url}`, where `start` and `end` are integer code point offsets into the trimmed text (`0 <= start < end <= length`) and a link’s `id` follows the block id rule. At most 10 links per block (`LIMITS.textLinks`), and the 256 KB draft cap (M2-04) still binds the whole draft. A text block without `marks` renders and publishes exactly as today.

M2-16 still holds because formatting is explicit data, never syntax inside the text: the renderer never parses `text`. Vitest and Playwright on a text block with no marks and the text `**bold** _italic_ x https://example.com javascript:alert(1)` render it literally: no ``, `` or ``, no auto-link, line breaks kept (`white-space: pre-line`), and the M2-16 escaping examples pass unchanged. A static scan finds no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` and no Markdown or HTML parsing dependency in package.json. Nothing in M2-16 changes.

Renderer: `

` holds text nodes, ``, `` and ``; overlapping bold and italic ranges nest (``), two links never overlap (Publish refuses that, so the renderer skipping the later one is only defense in depth), and every piece of text is a React text node (escaped). A link’s anchor takes `href` and `rel='nofollow noopener'` from `outboundHref(url, {pageId, id})`, so it points at `/r//` and never carries the destination in the markup. Link text uses `--t-accent`, is always underlined (color is not the only cue) and has vertical padding so its box is at least 44px tall without changing the line spacing; bold and italic use no color literals and only `--t-*` variables.

Publish form and gate: `toPublishForm` trims the text and shifts and clips the marks to match, sorts them, drops empty ones and, as defense in depth, drops the later of two overlapping links. Vitest table: `'  Hello world '` with bold 2 to 7 gives text 'Hello world' and bold 0 to 5; a mark entirely inside trimmed whitespace is dropped; `'a👍b'` with bold 1 to 2 wraps only the emoji (offsets count code points); CRLF becomes LF before offsets are read. `publishDocSchema` is strict about each mark: a link `url` must pass the http(s) rule ('Enter a full web address, like https://example.com.'), a link `id` must match the id rule and be unique across the whole page (the unique-id check now includes link marks: 'Ids must be unique within a page.'), two link marks that overlap fail with 'Links can’t overlap. Remove the other link first.', more than 10 links fails with 'Use up to 10 links in one text block.', more than 30 marks fails with 'This text has too much formatting.', and a mark with another `type` or extra keys such as `href`, `style` or `class` is rejected or stripped.

features.title: QR code for your page, as PNG and SVG
acceptance: Playwright 1440x900 as mara at http://app.localhost:3000/editor: the editor header’s action row has a secondary 'QR code' button (44px, visible at 390 and at 1440, next to 'View live page') that opens a dialog titled 'QR code for your page' (`role='dialog'`, `aria-modal='true'`, focus trapped). Escape and a 'Close' button close it and return focus to the 'QR code' button. The feature is on every plan: a Free fixture sees the same button with no 'Pro' chip.

States: for a page that has never been published the dialog says 'Publish your page first. Then you can download its QR code.' with only 'Close' (no code, no download buttons); after the first Publish in the same session, without a reload, reopening it shows the code. For a suspended owner (M5-09) it says 'This page isn’t available right now.' with no code and no downloads, because the page answers 404 (M5-08). For a published page it shows the code (inline SVG), the address under it in Geist Mono, the line 'Scan it to open your page.', and two buttons, 'Download PNG' (primary charcoal) and 'Download SVG' (secondary).

What it encodes: only the page’s public address, decided on the server and passed to the screen as a prop, never read from a query string or a field: `https://{hostname}/` for the page’s primary domain (the oldest verified custom domain, the same `getPrimaryDomain` rule that gives M2-30 its og:url) and otherwise `{tenantOrigin(handle)}/` (`http://mara.localhost:3000/` locally). The dialog has no input, adds no query string and no tracking parameter. A decoder (jsQR as a dev dependency) run on the downloaded PNG’s pixels, and on the SVG drawn into a canvas, returns exactly that string; with a verified custom domain (Vercel stub) and a reload the encoded address and the address shown become the custom domain.

Files: the PNG is 1024x1024 pixels (IHDR parsed in the test), black modules on a white background with a quiet zone of 4 modules and error correction level M, whatever the page’s theme (so it always scans); the SVG is one `<svg xmlns viewBox>` made of one background `<rect>` and one `<path>`, with no `<script>`, `<foreignObject>`, `<image>`, `href`, `style`, event attribute or external reference (Vitest parses it). Playwright’s download events are named `mara-qr.png` and `mara-qr.svg` (`{handle}-qr.png`, `{handle}-qr.svg`), the PNG starts with the PNG signature and the SVG with `<svg`.

No new service and no server route: the code is generated in the browser by one small bundled MIT-licensed package (named in package.json), and opening the dialog and downloading either file makes no network request (Playwright network log), so no third-party QR service is involved and nothing is paid for. There is no endpoint to abuse: GET http://app.localhost:3000/api/qr and /qr return 404, and the encoded string comes from nothing the owner or a visitor can type into the dialog.

Static check: the QR dialog and its generator import nothing from the tenant renderer or theme tokens (two token systems stay apart), use HYDLNK UI tokens only, and the copy contains no 'please', no exclamation mark and no 'successfully'.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor: the header row wraps with the 'QR code' button at least 44px tall, the dialog is a centered sheet that fits the viewport with the code 240px square, the two download buttons are stacked, full width and at least 44px tall, a long custom domain wraps (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`) and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.

acceptance: Schema: the draft and published documents gain an optional `share:{title, description, image}`. Publish gate: `placedImages` and `collectImageRefs` include `share.image` under the field `share.image`: a path outside the owner’s folder fails with 'That image isn’t in your uploads. Upload it again.', a missing object with 'That image is no longer available. Upload it again.', and a declared width under 600 with 'Use an image at least 600 pixels wide.', each leaving `pages.published` unchanged. Share fields are part of the published document, so they change only at Publish and ride on the page’s cache tag (M2-26).

Metadata, on `http://mara.localhost:3000/` and on a verified custom host (the `/sites/[pageId]` route, same rules): `og:title` and `twitter:title` are the share title, else the display name; `og:description` and `twitter:description` are the share description, else the bio; `og:image` and `twitter:image` stay the page’s own `/og?v=<published_at ms>` URL on the same host, `og:type` is website and `twitter:card` is `summary_large_image` (M2-30). The document `<title>` stays '{name} - links' and `<meta name='description'>` stays the bio (M2-22). With no share fields every tag is byte-identical to today’s (snapshot of `generateMetadata` for both routes). A share title of `"><script>alert(1)</script>` appears HTML-escaped inside the `content` attribute and no element is injected (parse the response HTML).

Social image: with `share.image` set, GET `/og` still returns `image/png`, 1200x630 (IHDR parsed), now showing the uploaded picture drawn to cover the frame around its focus with no text on it; with a fixture whose left half is red and right half blue, focus x=0 gives a red center pixel and x=1 a blue one. The picture is loaded only when its path matches `IMAGE_PATH_PATTERN` and its URL’s origin is the configured Supabase Storage origin, with `redirect: 'error'`, a 4 second timeout, at most 4 MB and at most 16 megapixels (sharp `limitInputPixels`); a mocked `fetch` shows no other request and no font download; any failure (object deleted, wrong type, too big) falls back to today’s generated card with HTTP 200, never a 500. `OG_TEMPLATE_VERSION` is bumped and the share fields are part of the cache key, so no stale image is served; a page without share fields gets the same bytes as before.

Timing: editing share fields in the draft changes nothing on the live page until Publish (view-source tags and the `/og` bytes before and after an autosave are identical); Publish changes the tags and the image at once (same cache tag as the page, no stale copy) on the handle host and on the custom host, whose `og:url` and `og:image` name that host.

Abuse cases (publishable key, owner’s JWT): a draft with `share.image.path` of `<user B id>/img-0123456789ab.webp`, of `https://evil.example/x.png` or containing `..` is accepted as a draft but rejected at Publish, so tags and `/og` stay as they were; a 10 000-character share title is accepted by the database (under the draft size cap) and rejected at Publish; a `share` key on a page whose owner is suspended returns the M5-08 404 for the page and for `/og` with none of the share text in the HTML; no plan check exists anywhere on this path (Vitest renders the same tags for plans free, pro and studio).

At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/ a page with all three share fields set renders exactly like the same page without them (the share fields change tags and the social image only): `scrollWidth <= innerWidth` and every anchor is at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the page is unchanged, within the 480px column, and the response HTML contains the share title in `og:title` exactly once.
