features.title: Gradient tokens: direction and two colors, stored safely
acceptance: Vitest on the token schema: three tokens join the 23 existing ones (26 in all). gradientAngle accepts exactly 0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270 and 315 (default 180, top to bottom, today's direction); gradientFrom and gradientTo accept #RGB, #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA or null (default null, which means follow the page's surface and bg colors, as the gradient does today). All three reject 'red', 'rgb(0,0,0)', 'url(x)', '#fff;}body{display:none', '45deg', '180deg; background:url(//evil.example/x)', 181, 360, -45, NaN, numeric strings and any string longer than 9 characters (the angle accepts no string at all). The page-level overrides schema accepts any subset including the new keys and still rejects unknown keys; block-level overrides do not accept them (M6-45).

CSS variables (Vitest, extending M3-02): the serializer emits --t-gradient-angle as '<n>deg' and --t-gradient-from and --t-gradient-to as the stored hex, or as the resolved surface and bg colors when the value is null; a value that fails its schema is replaced by the default for that token and is never concatenated into a style string; no stylesheet gains a color literal (tests/unit/renderer-static.test.ts still passes). With both colors null the page root's gradient keeps today's exact stops, surface at 0% and bg at 55%, whatever the angle; once either color is set the gradient runs from the From color at 0% to the To color at 100% along the chosen angle.

Playwright 1440x900 as mara: with draft overrides {bgType:'gradient', gradientAngle:135, gradientFrom:'#C46A4F', gradientTo:'#1B1814'} (set with the secret key in test setup), the editor preview root has --t-gradient-angle '135deg', --t-gradient-from '#C46A4F' and --t-gradient-to '#1B1814' and a computed background-image that is a linear-gradient from rgb(196, 106, 79) to rgb(27, 24, 20); before Publish http://mara.localhost:3000 still shows the old background and after Publish it shows the same gradient. The Smoke system theme (gradient, no gradient colors) still computes to the M3-14 gradient, surface at 0% to bg at 55% at 180deg, and the gradient still fills the whole viewport on a one-block page with no unfilled strip (M3-14).

Publish freezes the three tokens (page overrides, then the theme, then the defaults) into pages.published.tokens and the public page reads only that. Backward compatibility is required, because a published document that fails the schema is served as a 404: a published document stored before this change (the 23 old token keys, kept as a Vitest fixture copied from a real pre-change row) still parses with publishedDocSchema, resolves the three new tokens to their defaults and renders markup and styles identical to before; theme rows with 23 keys (system and saved) still resolve; a theme saved after this change carries all 26 keys and stays under the 8192-byte cap; PUBLIC_READ_CACHE_VERSION in src/lib/publish/tags.ts is bumped to '3' so no cached page from before the release is served.

A new migration (never an edit of an existing one, same pattern as 20261002100004_normalize_legacy_token_values.sql) adds gradientAngle 180, gradientFrom null and gradientTo null to every stored complete token set that lacks them: themes.tokens (system and saved themes) and pages.published -> tokens. Nothing else changes: published_at, the draft, rev and every other value are untouched, and re-running it changes nothing. The block between the markers is repeated verbatim in a pgTAP file and a Vitest compares the two; pgTAP asserts that afterwards no themes row and no published page lacks the three keys and that a sample row's other values are unchanged.

Direct-API abuse (Playwright with PostgREST as mara, publishable key): PATCH the draft's theme.overrides with gradientAngle '45deg; background:url(//evil.example/x)', then gradientFrom '#FFF;}</style><script>window.__x=1</script>', then gradientTo 'red', then gradientAngle 181. RLS accepts each as a draft write; the editor preview shows no script element, window.__x stays undefined and the value falls back to the default; Publish fails with the existing 'Publish stopped: … Reset it in Design.' message naming that field, pages.published and published_at stay unchanged and the live HTML never contains 'evil.example' or '<script>window.__x'. A saved theme whose tokens hold a hostile gradientFrom (inserted through PostgREST, which only checks size) is ignored by Publish like any theme whose tokens do not parse; a published row holding a hostile gradient value (written with the secret key in test setup) serves the 404 page (fail closed) and never emits the value.
At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/ with a custom gradient published at 135 degrees the background fills the viewport, `scrollWidth <= innerWidth` and every link is at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the gradient spans the full viewport width and height behind the 480px column with no unfilled strip below the content.

features.title: Style overrides on every block type: schema, renderer and Publish
acceptance: Vitest on the schemas and the resolver: BLOCK_OVERRIDE_KEYS grows from eight keys to ten, accent, buttonBg, buttonText, text, textMuted, surface, border, buttonStyle, radius and borderWidth (the two additions, textMuted and borderWidth, take the same values and ranges as the page-level tokens). Every block type (link, card, header, text, image, social, embed, grid and divider) accepts an optional overrides object in the draft, publish and published schemas, and a document without it, including every document stored before this change, still parses. Keys outside the ten are stripped on parse and ignored by resolveBlockTokens even when present in stored JSON (fonts, text scale, heading weight, letter case, density, width, alignment, background, gradient and overlay keys), so M3-18's rule of no font, spacing or background override still holds. Social icons and grid cells carry no overrides of their own; styling is per block.

What each block reads (Vitest for the resolver, Playwright on a published page, siblings unchanged each time): link buttonStyle, buttonBg with accent and buttonText, and radius (M3-17 and M3-18, unchanged); card accent with border, and radius (unchanged); header text (the heading's color); text textMuted (the paragraph's color); image radius, borderWidth and border (an image has no border until borderWidth is set, so its default look does not change); embed radius, borderWidth and border (the YouTube poster and player and the Spotify frame); grid border with text, radius and borderWidth (the cells); social text with border (the icons); divider border (the line). With #C46A4F on each color key, 20 on radius and 2 on borderWidth, the computed styles on http://<handle>.localhost:3000 are: header color rgb(196, 106, 79); text paragraph color rgb(196, 106, 79); image 20px radius and a 2px solid rgb(196, 106, 79) border; embed frame the same; grid cells a 2px solid rgb(196, 106, 79) border, a 20px radius and title color rgb(196, 106, 79); social icons color and border rgb(196, 106, 79); divider background rgb(196, 106, 79).

Renderer mechanics: every block renderer applies its own overrides as inline --t-* variables on its own element, only for the keys that have a value, in the editor preview and on the live page with the same markup; a block without overrides renders exactly as today (the renderer snapshot tests for all nine types pass unchanged). Every property an override must reach reads its variable explicitly in page-renderer.css: the header gains color: var(--t-text), because it inherits its computed color from the page root today and an inline variable on the heading would not change it (still a variable, so tests/unit/renderer-static.test.ts passes); an image or embed border is emitted only when that block overrides borderWidth (keyed to the block, not a new default rule), so no existing image gains the page's 1px border. No --hl-* variable appears inside the page root; an override never leaks to a sibling, to the page root or to another block of the same type.

Publish: toPublishForm keeps, for every block type, only the ten keys that have a value (and omits overrides when there is none), still drops hidden blocks and stays canonical (two equal drafts give deep-equal forms); setting an override on a header flips the editor chip to 'Unpublished changes' and removing it flips it back; publishedDocSchema validates the stored form; a published document stored before this change, with no overrides on these types, parses and renders unchanged.

Direct-API abuse (Playwright with PostgREST as mara, publishable key): PATCH the draft so a header carries overrides {fontHeading:'Geist', bg:'#000000', text:'#C46A4F'}; Publish stores only {text:'#C46A4F'} in pages.published and the live header's font-family and the page background are unchanged. Then an image with {radius:-5}, an image with {borderWidth:99}, a divider with {border:'red'} and a grid with {text:'#FFF;}</style><script>window.__x=1</script>'}: each makes Publish fail with a message naming the block ('Corner radius isn’t valid. Use 0 to 32, or reset it to the theme default.', 'Border thickness isn’t valid. Use 0 to 4, or reset it to the theme default.' and 'Color isn’t a valid hex color. Use #RRGGBB, or reset it to the theme default.'), pages.published and published_at stay unchanged and the live HTML never contains the injected string. A published row holding a hostile block value (written with the secret key in test setup) serves the 404 page (fail closed), while the editor preview, which serializes through the sanitizing step, shows the default and no script element.

Theme interplay: applying a theme (M3-20) and 'Save as theme' (M3-21) neither copy nor clear block overrides of any type, and a block's own override keeps winning when the page-level token for the same property changes (a header with text #C46A4F stays that color after the page's text color changes).

At 390x844 on http://<handle>.localhost:3000/ with an override on every block type, the page has `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, social icons and grid cells stay at least 44px tall and 2px borders do not push any block past the page padding.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: every block stays inside the 480px column and the editor preview shows the same computed styles as the live page.

features.title: Published versions are recorded, and readable on Pro and Studio only
acceptance: A migration adds public.page_versions with RLS on and default grants revoked: id uuid primary key; page_id uuid not null references pages on delete cascade; version_no integer not null (1, 2, 3 and so on per page, unique together with page_id and never reused after pruning); document jsonb not null (an object of at most 524288 bytes, the exact stored publish form); published_at timestamptz not null (copied from pages.published_at); created_at timestamptz not null default now(). The authenticated role has select only; no role has insert, update or delete, because only a security-definer trigger function writes the table (tests that need a different row, such as the tampered document in M6-49, write it as the postgres role).

Recording: an AFTER UPDATE trigger on pages records a version in the same transaction whenever pages.published is not null and published_at changes (every Publish writes a new published_at, so a data migration that rewrites published without touching published_at, such as the backfill of M6-41, records nothing), the owner's plan keeps versions (plan_limits(plan).versions_kept > 0) and the document differs from the page's newest stored version. pgTAP: a Pro owner publishes three different documents (secret-key updates of published and published_at, as the Publish gate does) and gets versions 1, 2 and 3, each document equal to what pages.published held and published_at equal to the page's; publishing the same document again adds nothing; a Free owner publishing three times gets no rows; a page with no published document gets none. Playwright as a Pro fixture user: three Publish clicks with different bios give three versions.

Retention: after each insert the page keeps only its newest versions_kept versions (25 on Pro and on Studio), in the same trigger: 27 distinct publishes leave versions 3 to 27 and the next one is 28. Concurrency: two simultaneous Publishes of different documents on one page get distinct, consecutive numbers (an advisory lock on the page or a retry on the unique violation) and neither is lost.

Limits: versionsKept joins the one limits table (free 0, pro 25, studio 25) and plan_limits() gains versions_kept; tests/unit/limits-parity.test.ts loops over every plan and column and passes, and its mismatch case reports a changed copy of the table. No other module types the number: the history screen (M6-50) and the plan cards read it from the table (M4-02's rule).

Read gate (pgTAP): the policy on page_versions allows select only to the page's owner and only while plan_limits(owner's plan).versions_kept > 0. A Free owner with 5 stored versions (rows the trigger wrote while Pro, then the plan set back to free with the secret key) selects 0 rows; a Pro owner selects their own rows; Pro user B selects none of A's; anon selects none; a plan flip through the webhook takes effect on the next request in both directions with no data change. A downgrade keeps every row (M4-33) and an upgrade shows them again.

Direct-API abuse (Playwright with PostgREST, user JWT and publishable key): as a Free user GET /rest/v1/page_versions?page_id=eq.<mine> returns []; as a Pro user a GET with another user's page_id, or for another user's version id, returns []; POST /rest/v1/page_versions {page_id, version_no, document}, PATCH {document} and DELETE are rejected (401 or 403) and leave every row unchanged; with the anon key a select is denied; no RPC returns a version.

Versions are never public: the public page, its OG image and the click and view routes never query page_versions (the public query counter in tests/unit shows reads of pages and accounts only), and no version content appears in a response on a tenant host. Deleting a page (M4-19) or the account (M1-22, M4-34) removes its versions (pgTAP, and the existing deletion specs count zero rows left). Versions do not keep uploaded files alive: media_paths_in_use and the M5-14 cleanup are unchanged, so replacing a photo and publishing still deletes the old file even when a stored version names it.

features.title: Preview and restore a published version, server-only and Pro and Studio only
acceptance: Two Server Actions in a server-only module, loadVersionPreview(pageId, versionId) and restorePageVersion(pageId, versionId), take two ids and no document (type test) and check in this order, reading and writing nothing before the previous check passes: no session returns 'unauthorized'; a page the user does not own, or that does not exist, returns 'forbidden' (the version id is not looked at yet); a suspended owner returns 'account_suspended'; a plan whose versionsKept is 0, read from accounts.plan with the secret key, returns 'plan_required' (no version row is read); a version id that is malformed, unknown or belongs to another page returns 'not_found', the same answer for all three so ids cannot be probed; only then the work. A Vitest table covers each branch and shows that none of the failing ones writes.

loadVersionPreview returns {ok:true, doc, missingImages}: the stored document parsed with publishedDocSchema (a document that does not parse returns 'error' and never the raw JSON), with every image reference that points outside the owner's folder or whose object is missing from page-media replaced by null and counted, and the same for the version's frozen background image: when tokens.bgImage names a missing object, or one outside the owner's folder, the preview shows no background image (bgImage null, bgType 'solid') and counts it. It only reads: no write and no cache call, and the result never holds another page's data.

restorePageVersion writes pages.draft and nothing else (secret key, filtered on the page id, the owner id and the draft rev read at the start): pages.published, published_at, page_versions, themes and Storage are untouched and no cache tag is expired, so the live page does not change. The new draft is the version's document as a draft: profile, blocks (ids kept, all visible, in order), theme, rev = stored rev + 1, and images checked as in the preview (a missing photo, card image or image-block image becomes null, and a missing background image becomes bgImage null with bgType 'solid' in the page-level overrides, so Publish does not stop on it; each is counted in missingImages). It returns {ok:true, restored: <version number>, missingImages}. Afterwards the editor shows 'Unpublished changes' whenever the draft's publish form differs from the live document.

Theme fidelity: the restored draft resolves to the version's frozen tokens exactly (Vitest with three fixtures; resolveTokens(themeTokens, draft.theme.overrides) deep-equals document.tokens). The theme it used is unchanged: reference and overrides are kept. The theme was edited after that Publish: the reference is kept and the overrides gain every token whose value would otherwise differ. The theme was deleted, or belongs to another user: the reference becomes null and the overrides carry every token the theme used to supply.

Re-validation: the restored draft is parsed with draftDocSchema before writing, and the write goes through the same database triggers as any draft save. A version holding a link to a site added to the blocklist since (M5-03) returns 'blocked_link' with the hosts and changes nothing; a document that fails the schema returns 'error' and changes nothing; the 524288-byte draft cap holds.

Races and stale tabs: if the draft's rev changed between the read and the write (another tab saved), restore returns 'conflict' and changes nothing; after a successful restore an editor tab that was open on the old draft gets the existing 'This page changed in another tab. Reload to keep editing.' on its next save instead of overwriting the restore; two simultaneous restores leave one consistent draft.

Abuse matrix (Vitest on the action core plus Playwright with a Free and two Pro fixtures): a Free user with their own page and a version id gets 'plan_required' from both actions and the draft is unchanged; Pro user A with a version id of Pro user B gets 'not_found'; A with B's page id gets 'forbidden'; a version of A's other page given with this page's id gets 'not_found'; no session gets 'unauthorized'; ids such as 'x', an empty string, a 10,000-character string and SQL metacharacters get 'forbidden' or 'not_found' with no 500 and no write; a stored version whose document was tampered with (as the postgres role in test setup) to carry a photo path in another user's folder, or a background image URL in another user's folder, restores with that photo and background null and missingImages counted; a downgrade through the webhook makes the very next call return 'plan_required'.
Logging: failures log a short code and the ids only, never the document, a URL or a token; responses never include the secret key or another page's ids.

features.title: Version history screen
acceptance: Playwright 1440x900 as a Pro fixture user at http://app.localhost:3000/editor: the header gains a 'History' link (13px/600 underlined text link like 'View live page', at least 44px tall) to http://app.localhost:3000/editor/history, on every plan; on a Free account it carries a brass-soft 'Pro' chip beside the word. The route keeps 'Editor' as aria-current=page in the sidebar and the tab bar.

On /editor/history the header shows the mono breadcrumb '<handle>.hydlnk.com / history', an h1 'Version history' and a 'Back to editor' link. A Pro or Studio account with versions sees them newest first, at most 25, in rows: 'Version 12' (14px/600), the publish time in the viewer's time zone (mono 12px, for example 'Oct 3, 2026, 4:12 PM'), a green 'Live now' chip on the one whose document equals the page's current published document (publishFormsEqual), and two buttons 'Preview' and 'Restore' (aria-labels 'Preview version 12' and 'Restore version 12'). The list is read with the user's own session (RLS), not the secret key.

Preview: 'Preview' on a row loads that version through loadVersionPreview and draws it with the shared PageRenderer in the 310x660 bezel, in a sticky 330px column headed 'Version 12' with its time; the version's own tokens apply and the preview's fonts load only that version's two families; a polite status says 'Previewing version 12.'. When images are missing a line under the header reads '2 images in this version are no longer stored.' (singular: 'An image in this version is no longer stored.'). Previewing writes nothing: the network log shows reads only and no PATCH.

Restore: 'Restore' opens an inline confirmation on the row, 'Restore version 8? Your draft is replaced with this version. Your live page doesn’t change until you publish.', plus 'You have unpublished changes. They’ll be replaced.' when the draft's publish form differs from the live document, with 'Restore version 8' (charcoal) and 'Keep my draft' (secondary) buttons; Escape and 'Keep my draft' close it and return focus to 'Restore'. Confirming calls restorePageVersion, shows 'Restoring…' with aria-busy and sends one request on a double click, then shows 'Restored version 8 to your draft. Review it in the editor, then publish.' with an 'Open editor' link and an 'Undo' button (at least 44px, available at least 10 seconds); Undo writes back the draft the screen read, with its own session under RLS, just before calling restorePageVersion, through the normal draft save with its rev guard, and says 'Undone.'. The editor then shows the version's content with the chip 'Unpublished changes'; Publish makes it live, a new Version 13 appears in the list tagged 'Live now' and http://<handle>.localhost:3000 shows the restored content.

Failures keep the draft and say what to do: 'This version has a link to a blocked site (example.test), so it can’t be restored.' (blocked_link); 'Your page changed in another tab. Reload, then try again.' (conflict); 'Couldn’t restore that version. Your draft is safe. Try again.' with a Retry button (error); 'Couldn’t restore. Your account is suspended.' (account_suspended). A restore with missing images adds '2 images from this version are no longer stored. Add them again before you publish.' to the success message. If the plan no longer has history the screen switches to the locked card of the next step.

Locked and empty states: a Free account, and a Pro account that was downgraded, sees a card instead of the list: h2 'Version history comes with Pro', 'Pro keeps your last 25 published versions, so you can look back and restore one.' (the number comes from the limits table) and a 'See plans' link (44px) to /settings#plans; the screen makes no request to page_versions and calls neither action. A Pro account with no versions yet sees 'No versions yet. Each time you publish, that version is kept here.'. A failed load shows 'We couldn’t load your versions. Try again.' with Retry, as in M5-16.

Abuse: signed out, /editor/history redirects to the sign-in page (M1-07); with the hl-page cookie set to another user's page id the screen shows the signed-in user's own page (the fallback the Editor uses), never the other user's versions; the page id and version id travel only as server action arguments that the server re-checks (M6-49), so editing them in the browser changes nothing.

Plans tell the truth: the plan cards on http://app.localhost:3000/settings and the comparison in the landing page's pricing section list 'Version history' (a dash on Free, 'Last 25 versions' on Pro and Studio) with the number read from the limits table, and docs/PLAN.md moves Version history from Deferred into the Monetization table. Every other feature stays on every plan.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor/history the rows stack with 'Preview' and 'Restore' side by side, each at least 44px tall; the confirmation's buttons are stacked, full width and at least 44px tall; 'Preview' opens the version in a full-screen sheet (role='dialog' with 'Close' and 'Restore this version' buttons at least 44px tall, the page behind does not scroll) showing the page at full width without a bezel; the locked card's 'See plans' link is at least 44px tall and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the list sits in the 720px column and the preview in the sticky 330px column, the confirmation appears inline in its row without moving the preview, and Escape closes it.

features.title: Sidebar and tab bar: one Editor item, with Settings & billing in the account menu
acceptance: Playwright 1440x900 as mara at http://app.localhost:3000/editor: the sidebar `nav[aria-label='App']` holds exactly three links in this order, each 44px tall with a 16px icon: 'Editor' (/editor), 'Analytics' (/analytics) and 'Domains' (/domains). There is no 'Design' link and no 'Settings & billing' link in it. 'Editor' has `aria-current='page'` on /editor, /design, /share, /editor/history and any other path under those, and no other item does; on /analytics and /domains the item for that screen has it and 'Editor' has not; on /settings no sidebar item has it. The current item keeps the look of M1-16 (white 600 text on #2E2C29, brass icon), and the current screen still comes from the route, so it survives a redirect. A Vitest of the nav's matching, run against the real src/app route tree and not a stub, covers every case: `useSelectedLayoutSegment` reports a route group by its own name (Next.js does not skip it: next/dist/shared/lib/segment.js), so under the workspace's route group the segment for /editor, /design and /share is the group's name while /editor/history reports 'editor', and the nav must treat both as the Editor item.

Account menu: the user block at the bottom of the sidebar (a 30px initials circle with the name over the email, as in M1-18) is one `<button>` with `aria-haspopup='menu'`, `aria-expanded` and the accessible name 'Account menu', at least 44px tall. Enter, Space, ArrowUp and ArrowDown open a menu (`role='menu'`, named 'Account') above the block with two items, 'Settings & billing' (a link to /settings) and 'Sign out' (next step), each `role='menuitem'` and at least 44px tall. Arrow keys, Home and End move between the items, Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the block, Tab leaves it and closes it, a click outside closes it, and the menu stays fully inside the viewport at 1440x900 and at 1440x500. 'Settings & billing' opens http://app.localhost:3000/settings, which keeps its header and its h1 'Settings & billing'.

Sign out stays a POST: the menu item is a `<button type='submit'>` inside a `<form>` that calls the `signOut` Server Action. A Vitest static check finds no link and no `href` for it, so nothing a GET can reach logs anyone out. Pressing it ends the session and /editor then redirects to the sign-in page; the cross-site and no-JavaScript behavior of M1-21 is unchanged, and the 'Sign out' button on /settings is still there.

Selected and admin states: on /settings the user block shows the selected style (background #2E2C29) and the 'Settings & billing' item carries `aria-current='page'`; on every other screen neither does. For an admin the 'Admin' link of M5-04 still sits in the sidebar's user area above the block and the menu has no extra item; the admin shell (/admin) keeps the static, non-interactive user block it has today (the account menu belongs to the app shell and the admin shell renders the same block without the menu); for a non-admin there is no 'Admin' link in the DOM. The page switcher and the plan card are unchanged.

Phone: at 390x844 on /editor, /analytics, /domains and /settings the fixed bottom tab bar (`nav[aria-label='App sections']`) shows four tabs in this order: 'Editor', 'Stats', 'Domains' and 'Account', linking to /editor, /analytics, /domains and /settings, each with an icon and an 11px label, at least 56px tall and 44px wide, the current one with `aria-current='page'` and the 2px brass top marker. 'Editor' is current on /editor, /design, /share and /editor/history; 'Account' is current on /settings. There is no 'Design' tab and no account menu on a phone (the sidebar is `display: none` there), and `<main>` keeps at least 84px of bottom padding so the last button of /settings is above the tab bar.

Old links keep working: as mara, GET http://app.localhost:3000/design and /share answer 200 inside the workspace of M7-02 with no redirect; /settings, /settings#plans (the 'See plans' links of M4-18 and M6-50), /analytics, /domains and /editor/history answer 200 as before; signed out, each of them still redirects to the sign-in page. A Vitest scan of every app-host path literal under src/ finds only routes that exist.

Abuse case: the menu's name and email come from the verified session on the server and from nothing the browser sends, and are drawn as React text: with two users, A and B, signed in separately each sees only their own email, and a forged `Origin` on the Sign out form is refused as in M1-21. Opening and closing the menu sends no request.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, the four tab labels are not clipped at 390px or at 360px wide, every tab is at least 56px tall and 44px wide, and every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide).

At 1440x900 on the same URL: the sidebar is 240px wide and holds the logo, the page switcher, the three links, the plan card and the user block in that order from top to bottom without scrolling at 900px tall, and the tab bar is not rendered.

Supersedes: M1-16 step 1 (the sidebar nav lists Editor, Design, Analytics, Domains and 'Settings & billing') and step 2 (clicking each nav link goes to its route: Design is now a tab, Settings & billing is reached from the account menu); M1-17 step 1 (five tabs, Editor, Design, Stats, Domains and Account, on five routes) and step 3 (tapping each of them); M1-18 where the user block is a static block (it is now the account menu's button); M3-06 step 1 (the sidebar item 'Design' with aria-current=page); M1-20 step 5 still holds ('Account' is the active phone tab on /settings) and M6-50 step 1 still holds ('Editor' stays current on /editor/history). tests/e2e/m1/shell.spec.ts and every spec that clicks the 'Design' or 'Settings & billing' sidebar link use the Design tab (M7-02) and the account menu instead. docs/DESIGN.md (Layout and responsive rules, the App >= 760px and App < 760px lines) and .claude/rules/editor-app.md (Layout) say the sidebar has Editor, Analytics and Domains, the phone bar has Editor, Stats, Domains and Account, and Settings & billing lives in the account menu; nothing else in either file changes.

features.title: One workspace for Edit, Design and Share: shared layout, tabs, routes and one draft
acceptance: Playwright 1440x900 as mara at http://app.localhost:3000/editor, /design and /share: the three routes render inside one workspace layout (one Next layout file under src/app/(editor)/app/(screens)/ that holds the toolbar, the preview column and all the draft state; the three pages only fill its content slot). A `role='tablist'` named 'Workspace' holds three `role='tab'` links, 'Edit' (/editor), 'Design' (/design) and 'Share' (/share), with exactly one `aria-selected='true'` and `aria-controls` pointing at the one `role='tabpanel'` that holds the content. Only the selected tab is in the tab order; ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move and wrap, Home and End jump, every move selects and navigates, and focus stays on the tab. A tab is a real link, so a middle click opens it in a new browser tab. The document titles are 'Editor — HYDLNK', 'Design — HYDLNK' and 'Share — HYDLNK'; each route has exactly one `h1` (the page's name, M6-14) and one `<main>`.

Nothing remounts when the tab changes: Playwright tags the toolbar element, the preview bezel (`data-testid='preview-bezel'`) and `window` with sentinels, scrolls the bezel's screen (`data-testid='preview-screen'`) down 300px, then clicks Edit, Design, Share and Edit again. The toolbar and the bezel are the same DOM nodes, the `window` sentinel survived (no document load), the bezel's `scrollTop` is unchanged, text typed into Display name and not yet saved is still in the field when Edit comes back, and the network log of the switches shows no PATCH or GET to /rest/v1/pages, no Storage call and no document request. The draft is read from the database once, by the layout, when the workspace opens. The provider is keyed by the page id only: a refreshed draft, `revKey` or other props from the server (the toolbar's rename calls `router.refresh()`, Publish refreshes, and a tab switch re-runs the page modules) never recreate the save queue or clear the history while the page id is unchanged. Playwright: typing ' X' and renaming the page at once loses nothing, shows no 'This page changed in another tab. Reload to keep editing.' and leaves Undo enabled; after a Publish the very next edit is saved ('Saved', never 'Not saved'), without a reload.

One draft, one history, one save queue: as mara, type ' X' into Display name (Edit), choose radius 20 (Design) and type 'Hello' into the share Title (Share), waiting 1.5 seconds after each so each is saved. Undo three times, from whichever tab is open, steps back in reverse (the share title, the radius, the name) with the draft deep-equal to each earlier state, and Redo three times steps forward again. Every PATCH to /rest/v1/pages carries only `draft`, with `rev` one higher than the one before, in order. A Vitest static scan finds `useAutosave` and the history hook used once, in the workspace's provider, and in none of the Edit, Design or Share components. An edit and a tab switch within 100 ms are sent in one PATCH carrying both changes: no lost edit, no 'Not saved' and no 'This page changed in another tab. Reload to keep editing.'.

Leaving and coming back: type ' X' into Display name and click 'Analytics' in the same tick. The edit is written (leaving the workspace flushes, as in M2-04), and after 'Editor' is clicked again the name ends in ' X' on /editor and in the preview on /design. The history belongs to the workspace and is gone after leaving it: Undo and Redo are disabled when the workspace opens. A second tab that is behind still gets the M2-04 stale-tab refusal instead of overwriting.

Page switching: as a fixture user with two pages, on /design, choosing the other page in the sidebar's page switcher keeps /design and its tab selected, flushes the first page's pending edits first, and then shows the other page's name in the toolbar, its draft in the controls and the preview, and an empty history (Undo and Redo disabled); none of the first page's text is in the DOM afterwards, because the workspace is keyed by the page id.

Data the shared preview and chip need is loaded by the layout, not by a tab: next to the draft it reads the full theme library (`loadThemeLibrary`: system and own themes, under RLS), the template themes and the primary domain, and provides them through the same context, and the Design tab's Themes card consumes that library instead of loading its own. So a theme applied on /design reaches the layout's bezel, the mini phone, the toolbar's chip ('Unpublished changes') and the template previews in the same frame, with no reload and no tab switch (Playwright: apply 'Paper' on /design and check the bezel's `bg`). Gate and isolation, on all three routes (M2-03 steps 2 and 3 hold for each): signed out, GET /editor, /design and /share answer 302 to the sign-in page with none of any page's text in the body; as jonas with the `hl-page` cookie set to mara's page id, each shows jonas's own page and none of mara's draft text is in the body; the draft, the themes and the template themes are read with the user's own session under RLS, and a Vitest static check finds no workspace layout, page or component module that imports a secret-key client.

Load failures: with the 'draft-load' fault on (`failIfInjected`), each of the three routes shows the page header (the address breadcrumb and the page's name as the only h1) and the card 'We couldn’t load your page. Try again.' with a 44px 'Retry' (M5-15), and no toolbar, no tabs, no preview and no mini phone; the error goes to the server log, never to the page. With only the 'themes-load' fault on, the workspace and the Edit and Share tabs work as normal, and the Design tab's Themes card says 'We couldn’t load your themes. Try again.' with its own 'Retry' while the color, font, button, layout and background controls and the preview still work (M5-16).

One notices area: under the toolbar and above the tab's content, on every tab, the workspace shows once each the save banner of M2-04 and M5-15 ('Couldn’t save. Your changes stay here and will retry.'), the undo notice of M6-07, the corrupted-draft notice 'Some content couldn’t be read and was reset in the editor. Nothing is saved until you edit.' (M2-03), the publish note and the Publish alert of M2-24. With a failing PATCH set up on the Edit tab, switching to Design and to Share shows the same banner there and never a second copy of it.

The private preview links keep their URL and give up only `/share` itself: /share (exactly) is now the Share tab, a signed-in screen, and /share/{token} is still the ungated private preview of M6-10. The internal route of the token page moves off /app/share to a path no workspace tab uses (for example /app/shared-draft; the (share) route group, its own root layout and its import-graph test stay) and the proxy rewrites /share/{token} there. Vitest: `isSharePath('/share')` and `isSharePath('/share/')` are false and `isSharePath('/share/abc')` is true. As mara, GET /share answers 200 with the workspace and `Cache-Control: no-store`; signed out it answers 302 to the sign-in page; and requests to exactly /share do not count against the `share:{ip}` limit (70 in a minute get no 429). M6-10 steps 1 to 9 still hold for /share/{token} on its new internal route: no session read, no Set-Cookie even when the owner is signed in, the same 404 body for every inactive link, the same headers and nonce policy, and 60 requests a minute.

Accessibility: axe-core finds no serious or critical violation on /editor, /design and /share at 1440x900 and at 390x844; the focus order follows the visual order (toolbar, tabs, content); every tab shows the 2px brass focus outline with a 2px offset.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor, /design and /share `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, the tabs sit under the pinned row of M7-05 and switching between them keeps that row where it is, and every button, input and standalone link has a bounding box at least 44px tall (icon-only controls also 44px wide).

At 1440x900 on the same URLs: the content column is at most 720px wide beside the 330px preview column on all three tabs, the preview column has the identical bounding box before and after a tab switch, and at 800x900 and 1000x900 the layout still fits with `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.

docs/DESIGN.md (the 'Editor and Design < 760px' line under Layout and responsive rules) and .claude/rules/editor-app.md (Layout) each describe the one workspace, its three tabs and the pinned toolbar in one sentence, and the rules file's line about the (share) route group names its new internal path; nothing else in either file changes.

Supersedes: M1-19 step 1 (the Design screen's breadcrumb 'Theme…' and h1 'Design': every workspace route now has the page's name as its h1; the titles 'Editor — HYDLNK' and 'Design — HYDLNK' still hold); M2-03 step 4 (the header's breadcrumb and button row: see M7-05); M2-06 steps 5, 6 and 7 and M6-02 step 4 (the phone tablist 'Editor view' with 'Blocks' and 'Preview': see M7-09); M3-06 steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 (the Design header with 'Save as theme' and 'Done', Done going to /editor, the 'Design view' tablist 'Style | Preview'); M3-07 steps 6 and 7 (the Design screen's own save status chip: see M7-05); M6-07 step 6 and M6-08 step 5 (the Design screen's own history that 'Done' clears: the history is now the workspace's, shared by the three tabs, kept across tab switches and cleared when the workspace is left); M6-10 (the internal route /app/share and the `isSharePath('/share')` literal in tests/unit/m6-pages-share-proxy.test.ts).

features.title: Edit tab: a shorter Profile card with a collapsed 'Photo and header options' section
acceptance: Playwright 1440x900 as mara at http://app.localhost:3000/editor: the Profile card (h2 'Profile', hint 'Shown at the top of your page') shows only the photo row (avatar, 'Upload' or 'Replace', 'Remove'), the 'Display name' input and the 'Bio' textarea with its counter, and under them one button 'Photo and header options' (at least 44px tall, a chevron icon that is `aria-hidden`, `aria-expanded='false'`, `aria-controls` pointing at its region). features.title: Design tab themes as two swipeable carousels: Your themes and HYDLNK themes

Each row is a horizontal scroll container (`overflow-x: auto`, `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory`, every card `scroll-snap-align: start`, `role='region'` named like its heading, `tabindex='0'` so the arrow keys scroll it). The cards are compact: about 152px wide, a 48px swatch (the theme's background or gradient with a filled and an outlined accent bar, as M3-19) over a 44px name row, so every card is the same height (within 1px) whatever the name; a long name is cut with an ellipsis and carries the full name in `title`. Pressing the card still applies the theme with 'Applied <name>.' and its Undo exactly as M3-20 says.

Moving along a row. From 760px up each row has two 44x44 arrow buttons, 'Show previous themes' and 'Show next themes', overlaid on its left and right edges and vertically centered, `aria-disabled` at the start and end of the row and not shown when every card fits; a click scrolls by the row's visible width less one card and ends on a card boundary. Below 760px there are no arrow buttons and a drag with a finger scrolls the row (Playwright dispatches raw touch events) and ends snapped to a card. Tabbing to a card that is out of view scrolls the row to it. Scrolling a row makes no network request.

The applied theme: its card has a 2px brass outline, `aria-pressed='true'` and the tag 'Applied' ('Edited' once a page-level override differs, M3-19 step 2; an 11px mono label drawn on its swatch, so the name row keeps its room), and its row scrolls so the card is fully inside the row's visible box when the Design tab opens and again after an apply, an Undo, a Redo, a 'Save as theme' and a Retry that loads the themes. Only the row scrolls: `window.scrollY` and every other scroll position are unchanged (the scroll is a `scrollLeft` change on the row, never `scrollIntoView` with a vertical alignment). With the 14th HYDLNK theme applied, the 'HYDLNK themes' row opens scrolled to it; with an own theme applied, the 'Your themes' row does.

Per-card menu: every card has a 44x44 'More' button (`aria-label='More for Paper'`, `aria-haspopup='menu'`, `aria-expanded`) on its name row that opens a menu named like the theme. HYDLNK cards have one item, 'Preview' (accessible name 'Preview Paper'), and own cards have 'Preview', 'Rename' and 'Delete'. 'Preview' does exactly what M6-44 says (the bezel shows the page in that theme, nothing is written, 'Previewing Paper' with 'Apply Paper' and 'Stop previewing'). 'Rename' opens a small dialog 'Rename theme' with a 16px input 'Theme name' (prefilled and selected), 'Save' and 'Cancel' (Enter saves, Escape cancels; whitespace is trimmed; an empty name shows 'Give the theme a name.'; the rules of M3-23). 'Delete' opens the confirmation of M3-24 and removes the card; deleting the applied theme leaves the draft on the default theme with the notice of M5-16. Escape closes a menu and returns focus to its button, and the arrow keys, Home and End move between its items.

The card keeps its size whatever the count: with no message showing, the Themes card is between 290px and 340px tall at 1440x900 and between 290px and 370px tall at 390x844, and its height is the same (within 1px) with 0, 1, 3 and 30 saved themes. With none, 'Your themes · 0' shows the hint 'Saved themes appear here. Use Save as theme to reuse this design on any page.' in a dashed box as tall as a card row instead of cards. 'Save as theme' (secondary, 44px, M3-21: a new theme 'My theme N' of the page's resolved tokens, applied) is at the right of the 'Your themes' heading; after it the heading reads 'Your themes · 6' and the new card is last in its row, outlined and scrolled into view. The Free limit message ('You’ve used 3 of 3 saved themes. Delete one or upgrade to Pro.'), 'Update <name>' for an edited own theme (M3-23) and the 'Applied', 'Saved' and 'Deleted' messages with their Undo keep their text and sit above the rows in the one polite status region.

features.title: Template picker: a live preview, what is inside and the style on every card
acceptance: Playwright 1440x900 as a Free fixture user at http://app.localhost:3000/editor: 'Start from a template' (still the secondary button of the 'Add a block' card on the Edit tab, M6-40) opens the same modal dialog (`role='dialog'`, `aria-modal='true'`, named 'Start from a template', hint 'Pick a starting point, then change anything you like.') with the six cards in the order Musician, Podcaster, Artist, Shop, Coach, Streamer. Each card now shows, top to bottom: its name (h3), the one-line description of M6-40, a live preview, an 'Inside' line, a 'Style' line and 'Use this template' (`aria-label='Use the Musician template'`). The strip of background and accent colors of M6-40 is gone; the preview replaces it. The dialog is identical on Free, Pro and Studio.

The preview is the real page, small: the same `PageRenderer` (`mode='preview'`, `thumbnail`) fed `toPublishForm` of the template's blocks as `applyTemplate` builds them (fresh ids, empty addresses, so an embed or image shows the dashed placeholder 'Embed' or 'Image' as in the editor's preview) together with the person's own profile (display name, photo and photo options; the bio they wrote, or the template's sample bio when theirs is empty, which is what applying would give) and the template's own theme tokens from `templateThemes`, no page-level overrides. It is drawn at phone width (390px) and scaled to the card (about 190px tall, clipped, top of the page), `inert` and `aria-hidden='true'`, with no tab stop, no landmark and no `<h1>` in the accessibility tree, so the page keeps its one `h1`. Each preview root has the `--t-*` values of its theme (the computed `background-color` of `[data-page-root]` equals the theme's resolved `bg`) and no `--hl-*` variable is used inside it (style isolation, M2-06 step 4).

No cost to the page: opening the dialog sends no request except at most one stylesheet request to fonts.googleapis.com/css2 that names the families of all six themes together (none while the dialog is closed, none at page load); the previews send no view beacon, no request to /r/ or /api/e, mount no iframe (embeds are inert placeholders) and make no Supabase or Storage call (network log). A Vitest static check finds that the preview module imports no Supabase client and no `fetch`.

'Inside' lists what the template holds, in plain words, as the count of blocks and then each type in order of first appearance with its count: Musician '6 blocks: header, embed, 2 links, card, social'; Podcaster '8 blocks: header, 4 links, embed, text, social'; Artist '6 blocks: image, header, grid, link, text, social'; Shop '7 blocks: header, card, grid, 2 links, text, social'; Coach '6 blocks: text, 2 links, card, embed, social'; Streamer '5 blocks: 3 links, grid, social'. The words are the lower-case block type names with 's' added when the count is above 1 ('links', 'cards', 'headers', 'embeds', 'grids', 'images'; 'text' and 'social' never change). It is derived from the catalog by a pure function (`describeTemplate`), checked by a Vitest table of all six, and a catalog change changes the line with no other edit.

'Style' names the theme the template applies, from the catalog: 'Style: Midnight' (Musician), 'Style: Smoke' (Podcaster), 'Style: Ivory' (Artist), 'Style: Paper' (Shop), 'Style: Sage' (Coach) and 'Style: Ember' (Streamer). The catalog itself (names, descriptions, bios, themes, blocks) is unchanged and its Vitest of M6-40 step 3 still passes; the dialog's focus behavior is unchanged (focus starts on the first card's 'Use this template', Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside, Escape closes it and returns focus to 'Start from a template').

Edge states: a page whose display name is 60 characters long, or empty, and a photo of the person's own, draw in all six previews without overflowing the card (they clip); with a draft that has 50 blocks the previews still show the template's blocks, not the page's; a theme that failed to load (`templateThemes` is `{}`) draws the default colors and the card still works.

features.title: High-traffic flag: a Free page is flagged only after two complete months over the line
acceptance: A new migration (never an edit of 20261004000004_traffic_flags.sql) replaces `flag_high_traffic_pages(threshold integer default 100000)` with the same signature (`security definer`, empty `search_path`, the same grants: `service_role` only), adds the nullable column `traffic_flags.views_previous_month integer` (check: not negative), and drops and recreates `admin_traffic_flags(boolean, integer, integer)` with that column after `views` and the same `service_role`-only grant; `pnpm db:types` regenerates `src/lib/supabase/database.types.ts`. A flag now records `window_start` (the first day of the earlier month), `window_end` (the last day of the later month), `views` (the page-level views of the later month, which is the last complete UTC calendar month) and `views_previous_month` (those of the earlier one). Rows made by the old rule keep their 30-day window and have a null `views_previous_month`.

The rule, as a new pgTAP file (the fixtures build their days from `date_trunc('month', now() at time zone 'utc')`, so the test is right on any day of the month). A Free page is flagged only when the sum of its page-level views (`block_id = ''` in `daily_stats`) is strictly above the threshold in BOTH of the two complete UTC calendar months before the current one: 100,001 and 100,001 gets exactly one flag with `views = 100001`, `views_previous_month = 100001` and the exact window dates; 100,001 and 99,999 gets none; 99,999 and 100,001 gets none; 100,000 and 100,000 gets none; 500,000 in the later month and 0 in the earlier gets none (one big month, or one big week, never triggers a review); views only in the current month so far, or only in the month before the two, get none; block-level rows never count; the first and last day of a month count and the day on either side does not; Pro and Studio pages with 500,000 in both months get none.

Idempotent and quiet, as M5-10 step 3 says: a second call the same night adds no row; no flag is made while an unreviewed one exists (the partial unique index also refuses a second one with 23505); none for 30 days after `reviewed_at` (a review 29 days ago keeps it quiet); 31 days after a review, with both months still above the line, the page is flagged again; the function returns the number of flags it created; two overlapping calls create one (the advisory lock). The pg_cron job 'flag-high-traffic' is unchanged, '50 0 * * *', still scheduled after the rollup (pgTAP asserts the cron.job row and its command).

Server only, as before: `traffic_flags`, its new column and `admin_traffic_flags` stay unreadable and unwritable to `anon` and `authenticated` (RLS on, no policies; pgTAP `has_column_privilege` is false for both roles on every column); with the publishable key, anonymous and with a signed-in user's JWT, POST /rest/v1/rpc/flag_high_traffic_pages and POST /rest/v1/rpc/admin_traffic_flags are rejected and no row appears; only the secret key reaches them.

Flagged pages keep serving: after the job flags the seed page, http://mara.localhost:3000/ still returns 200 and `pages.published` and `published_at` are unchanged. An old-rule flag (a 30-day window, null `views_previous_month`) made before this migration is still listed at /admin/traffic and can still be marked reviewed.

The rule is written down where people look: src/lib/analytics/SCHEMA.md (the function table and the 'High-traffic flag' section), the header comment of the new migration, and the comments in src/lib/analytics/admin/ and src/app/(editor)/app/admin/traffic/page.tsx all say two complete UTC calendar months and the strict threshold, and a Vitest scan of those files finds no sentence that still says the flag sums 30 days. `TrafficFlagRow` gains `viewsPreviousMonth: number | null` for M7-11.

Supersedes: M5-10 step 2 (the sum of page-level views over the trailing 30 days ending yesterday: it is now each of the two complete calendar months; the 100,001, 99,999, Pro and Studio cases still hold in the new form) and step 3 (idempotency and the 30-day quiet period hold unchanged); M5-26 step 1 and M5-27 step 2 where a Free page over 100,000 views 'a month' appears in /admin/traffic (it now needs two months in a row, so a throwaway production account cannot show it within days: PROGRESS records the pgTAP table as the proof); supabase/tests/database/113-traffic-flags.test.sql (its job-section fixtures use a trailing 30-day window) and tests/unit/analytics-db-review-action.test.ts are updated to the new rule in the same change.

features.title: Blocked links: add and remove a domain, with the audit log and the pages that already link to it
acceptance: A new migration (never an edit of an old one) extends `admin_audit_action_check` with 'block_domain' and 'unblock_domain' (pgTAP: both are accepted, any other value is refused, the table stays append-only, server only, RLS on with no policies) and adds `admin_blocked_domain_impact(p_domain text, p_limit integer default 100)`: `security definer`, empty `search_path`, executable by `service_role` only. It reads `pages.published` with the existing `blocked_links_in` (so text links, icons, cells and every other URL are read the way the save-time check reads them) and returns, for live pages (published, owner not suspended) whose links point at the domain or a subdomain of it, one row per page: `page_id`, `handle`, `hosts` (the matching hosts, distinct), `link_count`, plus `total_pages` (all matching pages, not capped by the limit) and `draft_pages` (pages whose draft links to it). pgTAP: a link to the domain and to a subdomain count, `notexample.com` and `example.com.evil.test` do not, a page with two links to it is one row with `link_count` 2, an unpublished page and a suspended owner's page are not live pages but a draft that links to it is in `draft_pages`, a limit of 1 returns one row and the true total, and anon and authenticated cannot call it.

Two admin actions, registered in `ADMIN_ACTIONS` and reached only through `executeAdminAction`: `block_domain` (`POST /api/admin/blocked-links`, JSON body `{domain, reason}`) and `unblock_domain` (`POST /api/admin/blocked-links/{domain}/remove`, the domain is the path segment). `adminRoute` forwards the parsed JSON body to the action (a sibling factory is fine); every route file is still exactly one `export const POST = <factory>(<action>)` line. tests/unit/admin-actions-guard.test.ts is extended, not loosened: an anonymous caller gets 401 and a signed-in non-admin 403 for both actions with no database call and no secret-key client built, a cross-origin `Origin` gets 403 `forbidden_origin`, a body that is not JSON gets 415 and one that is not an object gets 400.

Normalizing the domain, in application code with the platform URL parser (the same one the Publish check uses, `browserHostOf`): the text is trimmed, `https://` is added when there is no scheme, the host is taken (so a pasted URL works), lower-cased, its trailing dot removed and one leading 'www.' removed. 'https://user:pw@Shop.Example.COM:8080/a?b#c' becomes 'shop.example.com'; 'EXAMPLE.com.' becomes 'example.com'; 'https://www.example.com/x' becomes 'example.com'; 'еxample.com' (Cyrillic е) is stored as its punycode 'xn--…' form. The result must satisfy the table's `blocked_domains_normalized` check and contain a dot. These are refused with 400 `invalid_input` and these sentences: nothing or no host 'Enter a domain, such as example.com.'; one label ('com', 'localhost') 'Use the full domain, such as example.com.'; an IP address 'IP addresses are blocked already.'; over 253 characters 'That domain is too long.'; an empty reason 'Add a reason so others know why.'; a reason over 120 characters 'Use 120 characters or fewer for the reason.' The reason is trimmed plain text; control and bidi characters are refused. A public-suffix list is out of scope: 'co.uk' passes (PROGRESS records that an admin must type the whole domain). A domain that is already listed answers 409 `already_blocked` 'example.com is already blocked.' and changes nothing.

`block_domain` inserts the row with the secret key, then calls `admin_blocked_domain_impact` and answers `{ok: true, changed: true, domain, pages, drafts, list}` (the list capped at 100 rows); it never touches `pages`, so nothing is unpublished, no page's `published` or `published_at` changes and http://<handle>.localhost:3000 of a page that links to the domain still answers 200. It writes one `admin_audit` row right after the state change, before anything that can fail after it: `action: 'block_domain'`, `admin_id` the actor, `account_id` and `report_id` null, `detail: {domain, reason, live_pages, draft_pages}`; a failed audit write fails the action (500 'That didn’t work. Try again.') and the retry, which finds the domain already listed, answers `changed: false` and writes the missing row (the pattern of `auditIfMissing`). `unblock_domain` deletes the row, answers `{ok: true, changed: true}` and writes 'unblock_domain' with `detail: {domain, reason}` of the removed entry; a second call answers 200 with `changed: false` and writes no second row; a domain that was never listed answers 200 with `changed: false`.

It takes effect at once and without a cache: after 'blocked-b.example.test' is added, PATCHing a draft with a link to https://x.blocked-b.example.test/ is refused with HL005 'blocked_link' (M5-03), the editor shows 'Not saved' with the blocked-site banner, and Publish refuses it ('Can’t publish. 1 link points to a blocked site: x.blocked-b.example.test. Remove or change it.'); after the domain is removed the same save and Publish go through. `loadBlockedDomains` reads the table on every Publish (a Vitest asserts no module-level cache), so the Publish gate never lags behind an add or a remove.

Abuse cases: a domain such as `example.com'; drop table pages; --`, one with spaces, a scheme-only 'https://', 'javascript:alert(1)' and a 5 kB string are all refused with 400 and no database write; the reason is stored and returned as plain text (`<script>` stays characters); `blocked_domains` stays server only (RLS on, no policies, no client grants: pgTAP and a curl with the publishable key, anonymous and signed in, read nothing and write nothing); the impact function is not callable with the publishable key.

src/lib/blocklist/README.md ('Entries are added by migration') says entries are also added and removed by admins at /admin/blocked-links, with audit rows, and the new migration replaces the comment on `blocked_domains` ('later entries arrive through migrations') with the same words; the starter list of twelve ip-logger domains stays and can be removed like any other.

Supersedes: M5-03 where 'later entries arrive through migrations' (admins can now add and remove domains; the save-time and Publish checks themselves are unchanged); the `admin_audit` action list of M5-07, M5-10 and its migration comments (suspend, unsuspend, dismiss_report, review_traffic_flag) gains block_domain and unblock_domain.

features.title: Images from our own address: a cached /media route in front of Storage
acceptance: Playwright and Vitest, with the local stack: a route handler at src/app/media/[...path]/route.ts (the root of the app, outside every route group) answers GET and HEAD for `/media/{uid}/{file}` on every host: http://localhost:3000, http://app.localhost:3000, http://mara.localhost:3000 and a verified custom domain's host (the M4-09 fixture). For an image uploaded through POST /api/media it returns 200 with the exact bytes (SHA-256 equal to a direct fetch of http://127.0.0.1:54321/storage/v1/object/public/page-media/{uid}/{file}) and the object's `Content-Type` (image/webp; an older .png or .jpg object keeps image/png or image/jpeg). HEAD returns the same status and headers with no body; POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE answer 405 with `Allow: GET, HEAD`. It sets no cookie and reads none: with an auth cookie on the request the response is the same and has no `Set-Cookie`.

The caching headers, which are the cost protection: a 200 carries `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (browsers keep an image for a year; the names are content hashes and are never reused, M2-08 and M5-11) and `Vercel-CDN-Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800` (Vercel's CDN keeps it seven days from one fetch of Storage, then fetches it again; the number is one constant, `MEDIA_CDN_MAX_AGE`, so a deleted image, an account's removed media and a removed photo stop being served within seven days instead of a year; Vitest pins both values and says why in a comment), plus `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and the upstream `Content-Length`. Every 404 this route makes (a path that fails the pattern, a query string, a refused content type or size, and a valid-looking path whose object does not exist) carries the same `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` and `Vercel-CDN-Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` (a short negative cache: a missing or deleted image costs one Storage request a minute, not one per view, and a flood of the same malformed path costs one function invocation a minute per address, not one per request). An upstream failure answers 502, a timeout 504, both with `Cache-Control: no-store`, so an outage is never cached.

Never an open proxy, tested as a table with a fetch spy that must record zero upstream requests for every refusal: only paths of exactly two segments that match `IMAGE_PATH_PATTERN` (`{uid}/{name}.{jpg|png|webp}`, a 36-character lowercase hex-and-dash folder, a lower-case name of 8 to 64 letters, digits and dashes) are served. Refused with 404 (with the short public cache headers of the step above, and no upstream request): a path with three or more segments or one; `..`, `%2e%2e`, `%2f`, `%5c` and a backslash; an empty segment; an upper-case folder or extension ('.WEBP'); a 37-character folder; '.svg', '.html', '.gif', '.webp.exe'; a trailing slash; and any query string at all ('?x=1': it is part of the CDN's cache key, so it would let anyone make endless cache misses; `mediaUrl` never adds one). The upstream URL is built only by `storageUrl(path)` from the validated path and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`: a request with `Host: evil.example`, `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Original-Host` or a `Referer` still fetches only the Supabase origin.

The upstream fetch is locked down (Vitest with an injected fetch): `redirect: 'error'` (a Storage redirect answers 502, never followed), `cache: 'no-store'` (so Next's data cache does not keep a second copy of every image), `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`, no `Cookie`, `Authorization` or `apikey` header sent, and only a 200 accepted. The upstream `Content-Type` must be image/webp, image/png or image/jpeg: image/svg+xml, text/html, application/json or a missing type answers 404 and the body is never relayed; an upstream `Content-Length` over 5 MiB (the bucket's limit is 4 MiB) answers 404. The body is streamed through, not read into memory first.

The proxy never runs for these paths: the matcher of src/proxy.ts excludes `/media/{uid}/{name}.webp`, `.png` and `.jpg` (the static-extension rule outside /app, /t, /sites and /r), asserted in tests/unit/routing-proxy-matcher.test.ts with real stored names, and an instrumented proxy shows zero calls, no host rewrite, no Supabase auth call and no `Cache-Control: no-store` from the app host's headers while the route's own headers stand on the app host too. A path the matcher does not exclude ('/media/x', '/media/x/y', '/media/x/y.html') still gets its host's routing and answers that host's plain 404, never an image; a path with an excluded extension that fails the pattern ('/media/x/y.svg', '/media/x/y.gif') skips the proxy and gets this route's own 404.

Local runs have no CDN, so every request here reaches Storage once and the tests assert headers, not hits. The proof of the cache is a release-time check like M4-15's production smoke, recorded in the PROGRESS.md release entry: two requests for one real image on a production tenant host, `https://{handle}.hydlnk.com/media/{uid}/{file}`, the second with `x-vercel-cache: HIT`; the Vercel dashboard figures to watch for the first week (Fast Data Transfer, Edge Requests, Fast Origin Transfer and Function invocations for /media; the seven days is the one constant `MEDIA_CDN_MAX_AGE`, and Gary can raise it to a year, 31536000, if he prefers fewer Storage fetches to faster removal of deleted images) and Supabase's Egress and Cached Egress; and the caveat that the CDN keeps a copy per host and region, so one image costs a Storage fetch per host and region every seven days, not one in total. PROGRESS.md also lists under Open for Gary: set a Spend Management budget with alerts on the Vercel team, and read the plan's own page for what Pro includes, because this feature lowers Supabase egress and function work but does not make traffic free.

Abuse and load: 200 requests for 200 different well-formed but missing paths in a row each answer 404 and the process stays healthy; a hot-linked image costs the same as any other request and is not blocked (recorded as accepted); malformed paths cost no Storage egress and, with the 60-second 404 cache, at most one function invocation a minute per distinct address; the route has no logging of request headers or cookies; a Vitest static scan finds the route imports no secret-key client, no `server-only` module that holds a key, and that `storageUrl` is the only place the Storage URL is built for it.

Supersedes: none. M2-08 step 3 (the Storage public URL returns 200 with a long cache-control) and M3-15 step 3 (the Storage URL of an old image still returns 200) still hold, because Storage itself is unchanged; M5-26 step 1 (images long-cached, no optimizer calls) still holds and gains this layer.

Where Google serves one variable file for several weights of a family (Fraunces 400 and 700 are one 36.5 KB latin file today), one file serves them all. A Vitest walks `FONT_CATALOG` x supported weights and fails when a family, weight or subset has no file, when a referenced file is missing or under 1 KB, when a file name does not contain the hash of its bytes, or when a family has no license entry in the notices file shipped beside the fonts. One server-only builder, `tenantFontFaces(tokens)`, writes the page's `@font-face` rules from `fontHeading`, `fontBody` and `weightHeading` through the same allowlist and `nearestWeight` rules `tenantFontStylesheetUrl` uses (that URL builder stays, for the editor's previews). Preloads and subsets: the document preloads only the faces the page will use, as `<link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin href="...">` pointing at the same URLs as the `@font-face` rules, so each font is one request and not two, and the console shows no 'preloaded but not used' warning within 3 seconds of load. A page whose text needs latin-ext characters (a name like 'Łukasz Żółć') also fetches the latin-ext file of the family it is set in and no other subset; a page with ASCII text never requests latin-ext. `document.fonts` reports the faces the page uses as `loaded` and `document.fonts.check('700 16px "Fraunces"')` is true at 390x844 and 1440x900 with every other host blocked at the network (Playwright `route('**', ...)` aborting anything that is not the page host).

HEAD returns the status and headers of GET with no body; POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE answer 405 with `Allow: GET, HEAD`. A stored document that fails `publishedDocSchema` is the plain 404 and the issues are logged as today; one with a block type this version does not know still renders the rest of the page.

With JavaScript disabled (Playwright `javaScriptEnabled: false`) every block is visible, links follow `/r/` to their destinations (M4-22 step 5) and the report link is present (M2-29 step 2).

Docs and rules, in the same change: `.claude/rules/tenant-pages.md` and docs/PLAN.md describe the new path (the live page is finished HTML built from the one renderer, fonts are self-hosted, one script, Twitch's parent comes from the script, the rule 'Pages are static and cached with a per-page cache tag' still stands); the old `TenantPage`, `ViewBeacon` and `TenantFonts` modules are removed or no longer imported by any live path.
