M2-05, M2-22 steps 1 and 3 to 9, M2-28, M2-29, M2-30, M2-31 step 3 and M6-34 steps 2 and 6 hold unchanged and run against the new path; the unit tests that import `TenantPage` (tests/unit/m6-pages-static.test.ts, renderer-parity.test.ts, renderer-static.test.ts, publish-public-query.test.ts, m6-share-meta.test.ts) are re-pointed to the live builder.

features.title: Placeholder, 404s and the error page from the same lightweight path
acceptance: No HTML a tenant or custom host answers with is rendered by the framework any more. A Playwright crawl on `next start` of these URLs, each asserted below, finds in none of the responses a `/_next/` URL, `__next_f` or a `<script>` element (only the published page of M8-02 has the one script): a published page; a claimed handle with nothing published; an unclaimed handle; a reserved handle (`admin.localhost`); an invalid one (`ab.localhost`); a suspended owner's page; `http://mara.localhost:3000/anything` and `/a/b/c`; a custom host with no domains row (`/sites/unknown`); and the 500 of step 5. The tenant group's `layout.tsx`, `error.tsx` and `not-found.tsx` and its two `[...rest]` pages no longer produce any of these (removed, or only reachable by a path no request takes: a Vitest scan of `src/app/(tenant)` finds no `page.tsx`).

Claimed but unpublished (M1-15 steps 1 and 2): 200, `<title>{handle}.hydlnk.com</title>`, exactly one h1 with the handle, 'Nothing published here yet.', `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`, the root carrying the system-default `--t-*` variables, system fonts, no script and no request except the document and the favicon. It is a tenant page, not HYDLNK UI: no `--hl-*` property and no app-shell markup in the response.

Not claimed, reserved, invalid and plain (M1-15 steps 5 and 7, M5-20 step 2): an unclaimed handle answers 404 with `noindex` and the HYDLNK-styled panel 'This address isn’t claimed.', a primary link 'Claim {handle}' to `{app origin}/signup?handle={handle}` and a secondary 'Go to hydlnk.com'; a reserved handle 404 'That address is reserved.' and an invalid one 404 'That address isn’t valid.', both with no claim link and no echo of the address; `/anything` on a tenant host (and any path on a host with no domains row) is the plain 404 'Page not found' with 'This page doesn’t exist or hasn’t been published yet.' and `noindex`. The copy, status codes, panel colors and links are those of the components `UnclaimedPanel`, `AddressPanel`, `PlainNotFound` and `UnavailablePanel`, which stay the one source (rendered to markup by the builder, not copied), and none of them has a `'use client'` directive.

Cache behavior of these states is unchanged (M2-26, M1-15 step 6): a 404 for a handle nobody owns is cached for no longer than `MISSING_REVALIDATE_SECONDS` (5) under `handleTag(handle)`, so claiming the handle shows the placeholder on the very next request (`invalidateHandle`) and deleting the owner's account shows the 404 again at once; a flood of requests to the same invented handle costs at most one regeneration per 5 seconds and no request reads the document (`readPublic`), only the handle lookup and the availability check, as today (counter test with `HYDLNK_QUERY_COUNTER`).

Suspended owner (M5-08 steps 1 to 4): 404, `noindex`, 'This page isn’t available.' with 'It has been taken offline.' and a 'Go to hydlnk.com' link in the HYDLNK charcoal and brass look; the HTML contains none of the tenant's display name, bio, link titles or URLs, avatar or OG tags; the handle stays held (never the claim panel); the same on a custom host; unsuspending brings the page back without a republish. Tracking stops at request time as before (`/r` 404 and `/api/e` 204 with no row).

Failure is a 500 panel and is never cached or confused with a 404: when the public read or the handle lookup throws (a Vitest with an injected failing reader, and one Playwright run with Postgres unreachable for one request), the response is status 500 with `Cache-Control: no-store`, `noindex`, the sentence 'Something went wrong. Try again.' (`data-testid="error-message"`, `role="alert"`), a Retry control and 'Reference: {id}' (`data-testid="error-reference"`), in the same charcoal look, with no stack trace and nothing of the tenant's page. Retry is a plain link to the same URL, so it works with the script blocked; the reference is the digest or 8 random base-36 characters (`errorReference`) and the same value is written to the server log as `[error {id}]` with the error; the request after the failure clears serves the page or placeholder normally and the failure left no cache entry.

All of these carry the tenant security headers of M8-07 and set no cookie, on a handle host and on a custom host. At 390x844 and 1440x900 each panel is a centered column with `scrollWidth <= innerWidth` and its links at least 44px tall (M1-15 step 8, M5-08 step 7, M5-20 step 5); the HYDLNK-styled panels use literal HYDLNK colors inline and never a `--t-*` token, and the placeholder never an `--hl-*` property (the checks of tests/unit/states-pages.test.ts, re-pointed to the markup).

Supersedes: M5-20 step 1 for tenant pages (the 'error boundary with a Retry button' is now the 500 panel above, with Retry as a link; `src/app/(tenant)/error.tsx` and `TenantErrorPanel`'s `onRetry` callback are gone), M1-15 step 5's 'Cache-Control: no-store' on an unclaimed handle where it describes `next dev` only (production serves it for at most 5 seconds, as since M2-26), and the comment in `(tenant)/not-found.tsx` that a tenant 404 is a framework not-found boundary. M1-15 steps 1 to 4 and 6 to 9, M5-08 and M5-20 steps 2 and 5 hold unchanged and run against the new path; tests/unit/states-pages.test.ts is re-pointed to the markup builder.

features.title: The finished page keeps its cache: one cached read, and every change shows on the next request
acceptance: Production build, the M2-26 harness (`NEXT_PUBLIC_ROOT_DOMAIN=localhost:3100 HYDLNK_QUERY_COUNTER=1`, `pnpm build`, `next start -p 3100`, `HL_PROD_PORT=3100`): two consecutive GETs of `http://{handle}.localhost:3100/` for a freshly published user answer 200, the first `x-nextjs-cache: MISS` and the second `HIT` (a static route handler's entry carries the same header in Next 16.3.8: node_modules/next/dist/build/templates/app-route.js), the bodies are byte-identical, `cache-control` carries `s-maxage=`, and `GET /hl-query-count` reads 1 after both. The same holds on a verified custom host (Host header, the M4-09 fixture), for HEAD, and for ten requests that differ only in their query string (`/?utm_source=a`, `/?x=<random>`, ...): the counter stays 1 and the body is unchanged, so a query string cannot force a regeneration. If a later Next release stops emitting `x-nextjs-cache` for these routes, only the header literal is dropped and recorded; the counter and the byte-identical body are the proof.

The routes are cached, not dynamic: `pnpm build` prints `/t/[handle]` and `/sites/[pageId]` as static or ISR routes with a revalidate time (never as dynamic), a Vitest pins `export const dynamic = 'force-static'` (or the equivalent that keeps them static) on both route files, and the public read keeps its key and tag: `unstable_cache` under `pageTag(pageId)`, `PAGE_REVALIDATE_SECONDS` (86,400) as the backstop under a missed invalidation, `PUBLIC_READ_CACHE_VERSION` unchanged unless the document schema changes. No request API (`headers()`, `cookies()`, `searchParams`, `request.url`, `request.headers`) is read anywhere on the live path (static scan), and `next dev` still reads Postgres on every request, as now.

Publish (M2-26 steps 2 to 6, re-run unchanged against the new routes): changing the bio, clicking Publish and GETting `http://{handle}.localhost:3100/` immediately (no wait, no second request) returns the new bio in the body, in `<title>` and in og:description, with the handle host and the custom host both showing it at once and the `/og?v=` URL changed; a draft autosave does not invalidate (still `HIT`, byte-identical body); tags are per page (publishing one page leaves another page's response `HIT` with its counter unchanged); a Publish that fails validation calls no `updateTag`; a PostgREST write to `draft` changes nothing live and a write to `published` is rejected.

Every other change shows on the very next request, on the handle host and on the custom host at once, one Playwright test per row, each reading the counter before and after: the first Publish of a claimed handle (placeholder to page); unpublish (page to placeholder, nothing of the page left in the body); suspend (200 to the 404 'This page isn’t available.' with none of the tenant's content) and unsuspend (the page returns without a republish); a plan change free to pro and back through the signed webhook (the badge goes and returns, M4-08 steps 1 and 3, and only that account's pages are refreshed, step 2); claiming an unclaimed handle (the cached 404 becomes the placeholder: `invalidateHandle`, M1-15 step 6); deleting a page and deleting an account (404 at once: `expireDeletedPage` and `expireDeletedPages`); adding, verifying and removing a custom domain (og:url follows `getPrimaryDomain`). The same functions do it as today (`updateTag` in Publish, `invalidateAccountPages`, `invalidatePage`, `invalidateHandle`, `expireDeletedPage` and `expireDeletedPages`): the new routes add no tag of their own, so no caller changes (Vitest: `src/lib/publish/invalidate.ts` is still the only module that calls `revalidateTag`, and the Publish action the only one that calls `updateTag` for a page tag).

One document for every visitor: requests with different User-Agent, Accept-Language, `Authorization` and `sb-...` cookie headers and different X-Forwarded-For addresses return byte-identical bodies and the same headers, with no `Vary` on cookie or user agent, no `Set-Cookie`, and the counter still 1 (M4-21 step 6: the beacon is the only per-visit request).

Failures are not cached and not mistaken for a 404: with the public read forced to throw, the response is the 500 panel of M8-03 with `Cache-Control: no-store`, the request after the failure clears serves the page, and the failed attempt left no entry (the counter goes up by one for the retry only). A stored document that fails validation is the plain 404 and is not cached for longer than a 404 is today.

Abuse and cost: 200 requests to 200 distinct invented handles on `*.localhost:3100` each answer the 404 of M8-03 and the process stays healthy; repeated requests to one invented handle cause at most one handle lookup per `MISSING_REVALIDATE_SECONDS` window; none of them reads a document or writes a cache entry for a real page; the counter of a real page does not move while these run.

Supersedes: M2-26 step 1's literal 'x-nextjs-cache: HIT' and M4-08 step 2's 'x-nextjs-cache: HIT' only if the header is no longer emitted for these routes (they hold literally today, per the template above); in that case the counter and the identical body are the proof, and the literal is recorded in PROGRESS.md. M2-26 steps 2 to 6, M4-08, M5-08 step 2, M1-15 step 6 and M4-09 step 7 hold unchanged and are re-run in the same specs (tests/e2e/m2/publish-cache.spec.ts, m4/billing-badge.spec.ts, m5/suspend-cache.spec.ts).

features.title: One small script upgrades every embed: tap to play for all eight providers, Spotify included
acceptance: One script, plain and hashed: the whole client side of a published page is a single file whose name contains the hash of its contents (for example `/_t/p.3f9a1c7e2b40.js`), loaded as `<script src defer>`. It is plain browser JavaScript: no import, no framework and none of `eval`, `new Function`, `innerHTML`, `document.write`, `document.cookie`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `fetch` or `XMLHttpRequest` (a Vitest scans the source). At most 3 KB gzipped (8 KB unminified). The readable source is one file in the repo and the hashed file is produced from it by `pnpm dev`, `pnpm build` and `pnpm test`; a Vitest recomputes the hash and fails when the built file is missing or stale, and when the HTML names any other script. It is served on every tenant and custom host with 200, `Content-Type: text/javascript`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and no `Set-Cookie`; its path starts with none of /app, /t/, /sites/ or /r/, so the proxy never runs for it (tests/unit/routing-proxy-matcher.test.ts with the real file name).

Nothing is requested before a tap, for all eight providers: a published page with one embed of each (YouTube, Spotify, Vimeo, TikTok, Instagram, SoundCloud, Apple Music, Twitch), loaded at 390x844 and at 1440x900, draws no iframe (`document.querySelectorAll('iframe').length` is 0) and makes no request to youtube.com, youtube-nocookie.com, ytimg.com, google domains, spotify.com, scdn.co, spotifycdn.com, vimeo.com, vimeocdn.com, tiktok.com, tiktokcdn.com, instagram.com, facebook.com, fbcdn.net, soundcloud.com, sndcdn.com, apple.com, mzstatic.com or twitch.tv: the network log holds no host but the page's own and the root `/media` origin (M2-19 step 4 and M6-27 step 1, now including Spotify, which was a lazy iframe that asked open.spotify.com on every visit).

The facade is plain markup that the script upgrades. Every embed is `<div class="pg-embed" data-embed-provider="...">` holding a `<button type="button" class="pg-embed-play" aria-label="..." data-embed-fit="..." style="...">` with the same classes, labels, dark poster and play disc, 16:9 box or fixed-height bar and caption as M6-27 step 2, produced by one server-safe component that both the live HTML and the React `EmbedFacade` render for their first paint. The button also carries what the script needs, computed on the server from `parseEmbed(block.url)` and the helpers in src/lib/document/embed.ts: `data-embed-src` (the final player URL: `embedPlayerSrc` for every provider but Twitch; for Twitch the parsed `src` plus `&autoplay=true`, with no `parent`), `data-embed-title` (`embedPlayerTitle`), `data-embed-allow` (`embedAllow`), `data-embed-fullscreen` (present when `embedAllowsFullscreen`) and `data-embed-height` (pixels; absent for the 16:9 players). The script has no per-provider table. These attributes are written in every mode, so the markup of the editor preview and of the live page stays byte-identical (M6-27 step 6, M2-31 step 3), and `block.url` is still read by nothing that builds an iframe (the M6-26 step 7 scan, now over the markup component and the script).

After the tap: one delegated click listener on the document replaces the tapped button with an iframe that has the `src`, `title`, `allow`, `allowfullscreen` (where the provider has a full-screen button), `referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"`, class `pg-embed-iframe` and height the React facade mounts today. A table-driven Playwright test over every provider and kind compares the iframe's `outerHTML` on the live page with the one `EmbedFacade` mounts in the editor preview, and checks the heights of `EMBED_HEIGHTS` (16:9 by aspect ratio for YouTube, Vimeo and Twitch; 740 TikTok; 560 Instagram post, 640 reel and tv; 166 SoundCloud track, 352 playlist and artist; 175 Apple Music song, 450 album and playlist; 152 Spotify track and episode, 352 album, playlist, show and artist) and the autoplay flags (`?autoplay=1` YouTube, `&autoplay=1` Vimeo, `auto_play=true` SoundCloud, `autoplay=true` Twitch, none for TikTok, Instagram, Apple Music and Spotify). Focus moves into the iframe; a double-click, a second click and Enter or Space on the focused button mount one iframe only; tapping one embed leaves the others as posters; each tap adds exactly one iframe request from the page.

Spotify becomes a facade like the others: a poster as tall as the player (152 px for a track or episode, 352 px for album, playlist, show and artist, so a tap shifts nothing), `aria-label` 'Play music: {caption}' (no colon and caption when empty), the caption '{caption} · Spotify' below, `data-embed-fit="player"`; the iframe's `title` is '{caption} (Spotify player)' or 'Spotify player' and its `allow` is the list the old iframe had; `EMBED_HEIGHTS` gains the Spotify entries so one table serves every provider and `EmbedView` has no Spotify-specific branch left (the old iframe and the `pg-embed-spotify` inert placeholder are gone). In the editor preview and the mini phone dock Spotify now behaves like YouTube: a tap on the poster opens the block (M6-03 step 4), a thumbnail or inert copy (`thumbnail`, `inertEmbeds` in the shared draft) draws the same inert `EmbedPoster` as the other providers, at the player's height, and requests nothing (M6-10 step 4). Accepted and recorded in PROGRESS.md: Spotify's own player starts only on a press inside it, so a visitor taps Play on our poster and then play in Spotify's player, two taps instead of one.

Twitch keeps its rule (M6-27 step 4): on the tap the script appends `&parent={window.location.hostname}` to a Twitch embed and to nothing else, reading `window.location.hostname` and no attribute or other source; on `http://mara.localhost:3000/` the iframe `src` ends with `parent=mara.localhost` and on a verified custom host with that host; a hostname that does not match `^[a-z0-9.-]{1,253}$` mounts no iframe and shows `

This embed can’t load here.

` in its place (Vitest in jsdom with a stubbed location).

Defense in depth against a tampered DOM (Vitest in jsdom, plus one Playwright run): before mounting, the script checks the origin of `data-embed-src` against its own list of the nine frame origins (https://www.youtube-nocookie.com, https://open.spotify.com, https://player.vimeo.com, https://www.tiktok.com, https://www.instagram.com, https://w.soundcloud.com, https://embed.music.apple.com, https://player.twitch.tv, https://clips.twitch.tv: the `frame-src` list of M8-07, one shared source of truth pinned by a test that compares the two) and, for any other origin, a non-https scheme (`javascript:`, `data:`, `http:`) or an unparseable value, mounts nothing, shows the same 'can’t load here' line and makes no request: an injected button with `data-embed-src="https://evil.example/x"` or `"javascript:alert(1)"` does nothing. The `allow` value is applied as the iframe's `allow` attribute and nothing else is read from the DOM.

Robustness: with the script request aborted or JavaScript disabled, the page still renders in full, its links and the report link work, the Play buttons do nothing (accepted, recorded in PROGRESS.md) and the console shows no error besides the aborted request; with `navigator.sendBeacon` missing (M8-06) tap-to-play still works; a page holding the most embeds the document limit allows behaves the same, and the script's size does not depend on how many there are.

At 390x844 on `http://mara.localhost:3000/` with all eight providers published: every facade is the full column width, every play button is at least 44px tall, after tapping each one its iframe does not widen the page and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`; at 1440x900 the facades and players stay within the 480px column (M2-19 steps 6 and 7, M6-27 steps 7 and 8 pass unchanged).

Supersedes: M2-19 step 3's sentence 'Spotify: a lazy iframe, height 152 for track and episode and 352 for album, playlist, show and artist' (now a facade of the same heights that mounts the same iframe on a tap); M2-19 step 4's and M6-27 step 1's lists of hosts that must see no request on load gain Spotify's; M6-27 step 3's 'the old YouTube facade becomes this one shared component' (the shared piece is now the server-safe facade markup plus the one script on the live page, and the React `EmbedFacade` stays for the editor preview only); M6-03 step 6's static scan 'no click handler in src/components/page other than the YouTube facade's Play button' (now: the one facade wrapper); M6-27 step 6's 'a published YouTube or Spotify embed renders as before (M2-19 steps 3 and 4 still pass)' for Spotify. tests/unit/m6-embeds-facade.test.ts, m6-preview-static.test.ts and renderer-static.test.ts are updated; tests/e2e/m6/embeds-tenant.spec.ts runs against the script.

features.title: The view beacon comes from the shared script, with the same contract as before
acceptance: Same call, same timing (M4-21 step 1): on a published page at `http://mara.localhost:3000/` and at the custom host, the script calls `navigator.sendBeacon('/api/e', JSON.stringify({pageId, referrer: document.referrer}))` exactly once per load, after the `load` event (at once if `document.readyState` is already 'complete', otherwise on `load`, `{once: true}`), with the relative URL so the request goes to whichever host served the page. Playwright counts one POST to `/api/e` per navigation in both projects (390x844 with an iPhone user agent, 1440x900 with a desktop Chrome user agent string), and the captured body parses to an object with exactly the two keys `pageId` and `referrer`, the `Content-Type` is the `text/plain;charset=UTF-8` a string beacon gets (the same request the inline script sent).

Where the page id comes from: the shared script reads it from a `data-page-id` attribute on its own `<script>` element (`document.currentScript`), never from the shared body markup (so the editor preview and the live page keep byte-identical `[data-page-root]` markup, M2-31 step 3), and sends nothing unless it matches the UUID pattern the old `viewBeaconScript` checked: a script tag whose attribute is missing, empty or tampered with (`'"><x`, a non-UUID) sends no request and throws no error (Vitest in jsdom, and one Playwright run that edits the attribute before `load`). The builder writes the id from the database row after the same UUID check `viewBeaconScript` made, so a non-UUID id still fails the render rather than reaching an attribute.

Never in a draft: the editor preview on `http://app.localhost:3000`, the full-size Preview page, the shared draft page and the template and marketing demos produce zero `/api/e` requests (M4-21 step 3, M6-10 step 4, M6-11 step 3, M7-07 step 3), because the script is part of the live HTML builder's output and of nothing else; a published page with unpublished draft changes records views against the published version only. A Vitest scan finds the script's file name in no module outside the live builder and the proxy matcher test.

The server side is untouched and its specs pass unchanged against the new client: 204 with `Cache-Control: no-store` and no `Set-Cookie`, the one `events` row with its referrer hostname rule, device, country and 64-hex visitor hash (M4-21 step 2); the ignored cases with an identical 204 and no insert, the 413, the Origin rules and the direct-API abuse cases (M4-21 steps 4 and 5); bots and HEAD dropped (M4-23); the per-IP limit (M5-01); suspended pages recording nothing (M5-08 step 3). A forged curl beacon with the right pageId and Origin `https://evil.example` still inserts nothing.

No cookie, no storage, no banner (M4-21 step 6): the script contains no `document.cookie`, `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` (the scan of M8-05), the page response sets no cookie and is identical for every visitor, and the beacon is the only per-visit request; a failing `navigator.sendBeacon` (absent, throwing or returning false) is swallowed and never reaches tap-to-play (M8-05), which keeps working.

The beacon is one of the page's counted requests (M8-09): the request log of a first visit shows exactly one `POST /api/e` among the at most six requests to the page's own host, sent after `load`, and a reload sends one more, not two.

Supersedes: none of M4-21's behavior changes. M4-21 step 1's means (an inline script rendered by `ViewBeacon`) is replaced by the shared script, and the Vitest that evaluates the inline string (`viewBeaconScript`, tests/unit/analytics-ingest-static.test.ts and m6-pages-static.test.ts) is re-pointed to the shared script; `src/components/tenant/view-beacon.tsx` is removed. M4-21 steps 2 to 6, M4-23, M5-01 and M5-08 hold unchanged.

features.title: Tenant page headers: a script-src of 'self' and one directive per resource type
acceptance: The policy on every response the proxy rewrites on a tenant host or a custom host (set by `setTenantHeaders`, as now, so it rides along with a page the cache serves) is exactly this string, a new exported constant (for example `TENANT_PAGE_CSP`) that `setTenantHeaders` uses and tests pin; `TENANT_CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY` itself is not touched, byte for byte, because the private share policy extends it (step 2): `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; font-src 'self'; img-src 'self' {root origin}; connect-src 'self'; frame-src https://www.youtube-nocookie.com https://open.spotify.com https://player.vimeo.com https://www.tiktok.com https://www.instagram.com https://w.soundcloud.com https://embed.music.apple.com https://player.twitch.tv https://clips.twitch.tv; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, where the root origin is `https://hydlnk.com` in production and `http://localhost:3000` locally (the same value `MEDIA_IMG_SRC` holds). `script-src` has no `'unsafe-inline'`, `'unsafe-eval'`, nonce, wildcard or `data:`; `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` is the one inline allowance, because the theme arrives as inline `--t-*` custom properties, `style` attributes and one `<style>` element, and a stylesheet link is refused (M8-02 ships none). The nine frame origins are one exported list that this policy and `TENANT_CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY` both build from.

Everything else is unchanged or stricter, on a handle host and on a custom host, for the page, the placeholder, every 404 panel and the 500 panel: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, no `Set-Cookie` and no cookie read (M2-22 steps 6 and 7, M4-09 step 5). `/r/*` and `/api/e`, which the proxy leaves unrewritten, the app host, the root host and the private share route keep exactly the headers they have: the share policy (`TENANT_CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY` plus its nonce script policy, M6-10 step 3), the app host's policy (no `frame-src`, no `img-src`) and every test that pins them pass unchanged. The share policy must not be rebuilt from the new live-page string: it keeps appending its own directives to `TENANT_CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY`, so `/share/*` never carries `default-src 'none'` or a second `script-src` (a second `script-src 'self'` ahead of the nonce policy would make browsers ignore the nonce and block Next's bootstrap scripts), and a Vitest pins the whole share header string byte-identical to today's. features.title: Done when: a first visit to a full page makes at most 6 requests to its own host, under 90 KB, and none to a third party
acceptance: Baseline, measured on https://links.hyde-co.com/ on 2026-10-04 and kept for the before and after table in PROGRESS.md: 18 requests and about 325 KB to the page's own host (1 document of 6 KB; 2 preloaded HYDLNK UI font files of 50 KB that the page never uses; 3 CSS files of 18 KB; 11 JavaScript files of about 250 KB, the Next and React runtime, the turbopack runtime, the router and two client components; the view beacon), plus requests to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com for the theme's stylesheet and fonts. Images load from https://hydlnk.com/media/... and are not counted here.

The fixture (a Free page made with the secret-key helpers, published, with a real `/media` avatar and card image uploaded through POST /api/media): a profile photo, a name and a bio; a header; three link blocks (one with a built-in icon); a text block with bold, italic and a link; a social block with four icons; a card with an image; a YouTube embed and a Spotify track embed; a divider; the Free badge and the report link; theme tokens with a Fraunces heading at weight 700 and an Inter body. Playwright against the production build on :3100 (the HL_PROD_PORT harness of M2-26, one Chromium CDP session with `Network.enable` per run) opens `http://{handle}.localhost:3100/` in a fresh browser context at 390x844 (iPhone user agent) and at 1440x900 (desktop Chrome user agent) and waits for `load` and for the network to be idle for 1 second.

The budget on that first visit, in the same test for both viewports. Requests to the page's own host, not counting images on the root `/media` origin and the favicon: at most 6, and the test lists them by kind and asserts exactly this shape: 1 document, at most 2 `font/woff2` files (Fraunces latin, Inter latin), 1 script file (M8-05) and 1 `POST /api/e` (M8-06). Bytes transferred from the page's own host: at most 90 KB (92,160 bytes), summed from the CDP `encodedDataLength` of those requests, response headers included, of which the document is at most 16 KB and the script at most 3 KB (the fonts for the Fraunces 700 plus Inter pair are at most 64 KB, M8-01). Requests to any host other than the page's own and the root origin's `/media`: zero (the log holds no fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com, youtube, spotify or any other host). Framework runtime: no request whose path starts with `/_next/` and ends in `.js` or `.css`, no `<script>` without a `src`, `document.scripts.length` is 1, `window.__next_f` and `window.next` are undefined, and there is no `<link rel="stylesheet">`.

Quality of that load: no console error or warning, no `pageerror`, no `securitypolicyviolation` (M8-07), no 'preloaded but not used' warning; the layout-shift entries (a `PerformanceObserver` for `layout-shift` registered before navigation) sum to at most 0.05; `scrollWidth <= innerWidth` at 390x844 and the column is no wider than 480px at 1440x900; every link, button and social icon is at least 44px tall at 390x844; the images (the avatar and the card image) are requested from `{root}/media/...` once each and nothing else leaves the host.

A second visit in the same context (a reload): the requests to the page's own host are the document (a conditional or normal request) and the one beacon, at most 2, and zero font and script requests (all from the HTTP cache: `immutable`); and a first visit to the same page on a verified custom host (`--host-resolver-rules` mapping `links.example.test` to 127.0.0.1) and to a Pro page of the same content (no badge) meet the same budget.

Interactions add nothing to the page's own host: tapping the YouTube poster and then the Spotify poster mounts two iframes, and the only new requests are the two iframe navigations to youtube-nocookie.com and open.spotify.com (the first third-party requests, made because the visitor asked); no second beacon is sent and no CSP violation is raised; a tap on a link follows `/r/{pageId}/{blockId}` (302) to its destination (M4-22).

Before and after, in the PROGRESS.md entry of this wave (numbers from the same fixture on the previous commit's production build and on this one): requests to the page host 18 to at most 6, bytes about 325 KB to at most 90 KB, third-party hosts 2 to 0, JavaScript files 11 to 1 and framework JavaScript about 250 KB to 0, CSS files 3 to 0 (inlined), the document size, and the Fraunces plus Inter font bytes; plus the table of all 18 families' latin file sizes against Google's (M8-01).

Release proof, recorded in the PROGRESS.md release entry after `/release` (like M7-14 step 6): the same measurement, run in the interactive `/release` session (never by a wave agent) against `https://links.hyde-co.com/` (Gary's page, read only: no publish, no edit), lists at most 6 requests to the page's own host, at most 90 KB, no request to a third-party host, one script, no `/_next/` JavaScript or CSS, and two requests for the document show `x-vercel-cache: HIT` on the second; the figures to watch in the Vercel dashboard for the first week are Edge Requests, Fast Data Transfer and Function Invocations for the two page routes (an invocation should now happen only when a page is regenerated, never per view), with the 18 requests and 325 KB baseline quoted beside them.

Supersedes: M5-21 step 3's budget lines for the public page ('first-load JavaScript <= 100 KB gzipped' becomes one script of at most 3 KB and no framework JavaScript; 'fonts load with display=swap and preconnect' becomes preloaded self-hosted faces with no preconnect; 'no request to ... the app host on load except the /api/e beacon' stays) and its thresholds in step 2 stay as the floor for a Lighthouse run when one exists; M6-34 step 3 and M7-15 step 7's lists of hosts the page may talk to (now: only `/media` images on the root origin); M3-04 step 1 and M2-22 step 7 as listed in M8-01 and M8-07. M2-22 steps 8 and 9, M2-31 steps 5 and 6 and M6-34 steps 7 and 8 hold unchanged and are re-run on the new build.

features.title: Custom-domain lookups are cached: a minute for a verified host, ten seconds for one with no verified domain
acceptance: What is cached: `resolveCustomDomain(host)` keeps its answer per normalized hostname, either `{pageId}` for a `domains` row with that hostname and status 'verified', or 'none' (no row, or a `pending` or errored one), for `CUSTOM_DOMAIN_FOUND_SECONDS` = 60 and `CUSTOM_DOMAIN_NONE_SECONDS` = 10 (two exported constants; a Vitest pins both values and a comment says why: the first is the longest a removed or re-pointed domain can be served stale if an expiry cannot reach the proxy, M8-11; the second is how long a typo or a not-yet-verified domain costs one lookup instead of one per request). A request inside the window reads Postgres zero times (Vitest with a client that throws when called; and, in the production build with `HYDLNK_QUERY_COUNTER=1`, a response header `x-hl-domain-cache: MISS` or `HIT` on the proxy's response for a custom host, set only when that test flag is on and absent from every other run, which a production-flag-off test asserts). After the window the next request reads again (fake timers: a hit at 59 s and a read at 61 s for a found host, a hit at 9 s and a read at 11 s for a missing one); a hit does not extend an entry's life, so a host requested every second is still read once a minute.

What is not cached: anything about the page. The cached value is the hostname's mapping and nothing else, so the lookup no longer joins `pages.published_at`: whether a page is published, suspended or deleted is decided per page by the page route (`/sites/{pageId}` answers the plain 404 for a draft-only page, a suspended owner and an unknown id: M4-09 step 3, M5-08), and `/r/*` and `/api/e` already check `published` and the host themselves (M4-22 step 3, M4-21 step 4), so Publish and unpublish change nothing in this cache and need no expiry. The decision is recorded in PROGRESS.md; if the implementer keeps the join instead, the first Publish and an unpublish must expire the hostname entry as well. Either way a custom host never serves a draft: M4-09 step 3's cases (a row whose page has published = null, a `pending` row, a hostname with no row, a `*.vercel.app` host) are re-run against the cache, warm and cold, and return the same 404 with no tenant data.

It has to work where the proxy runs: `src/proxy.ts` is bundled apart, runs on the Node runtime, cannot import `server-only` modules, and on Vercel may run in a different function instance from the Server Action that changes a domain. The mechanism is chosen only after a throwaway proof in a production build shows it works from the proxy (candidates: Next's data cache with a tag per hostname, if the proxy can use it; Vercel's Runtime Cache with tag expiry; a bounded in-memory map, which is per instance, so a changed domain can show stale on another instance for up to 60 seconds). The mechanism, the proof and the largest staleness it allows on Vercel are written in PROGRESS.md and listed under 'Open for Gary'; the cache lives in `src/lib/routing/` behind `resolveCustomDomain`, so `proxy.ts` and its tests change only where they must.

Abuse and bounds (full tests, a Vitest table with a counting fake client): 200 requests for one random, well-formed, unknown hostname read the database once in 10 seconds; 200 requests for 200 different well-formed unknown hostnames read it 200 times, once each, and the store never holds more than `CUSTOM_DOMAIN_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES` (1,000) entries however many distinct hosts arrive (10,000 inserts, then the size is asserted, oldest evicted first); a hostname that fails `lookupKey` (an IP address, an underscore, a label over 63 characters, a name over 253 characters, `*.vercel.app`, an empty Host) never reads the database and is never stored, so malformed hosts can neither fill the store nor cost a lookup; a lookup that throws or times out (the 3-second limit) answers 404 as today (M4-09 step 8), is not stored (the next request retries) and never replaces a good cached answer.

Keys cannot be split or crossed: the key is the hostname after `lookupKey` (lower case, no port, one trailing dot removed), so `LINKS.Example.Test:3000`, `links.example.test.` and `links.example.test` share one entry and one lookup (M4-09 step 2); two different hostnames never share an entry (a.example.test on page A and b.example.test on page B each return their own page, in either order and after a hit); `X-Forwarded-Host` and `X-Original-Host` still change nothing; the stored value holds no cookie, header or other request value.

Everything else about a custom host is unchanged and M4-09's steps 1 to 6 and 8 are re-run against the cached lookup: the page and its OG image, `/r/*` and `/api/e` pass through; `/login`, `/signup`, `/settings`, `/domains`, `/analytics`, `/auth/callback`, `/api/stripe/webhook` and `/anything-else` are 404; no response carries Set-Cookie even when the request sends an `sb-*` cookie; the lookup stays a server-only query on `domains` with the secret key and the hostname is only ever a filter value (never fetched: SSRF). A warm entry costs the proxy no network call (the counter header above and the server log show no Supabase request).

Supersedes: the statement 'nothing is cached between requests' in the header comment of `src/lib/routing/custom-domain.ts` and the rule 'A custom-host lookup is a database query on a normalized hostname' in `.claude/rules/routing.md` (both are rewritten to describe the cache and its two numbers); M4-09 step 3's 'a row whose page has published = null' is now decided by the page route instead of the lookup, with the same visible result. M4-16 step 2 and M4-17 step 2 ('the very next request') are unchanged by this feature alone and are relaxed only as M8-11 records. M4-09 steps 1 to 8 hold unchanged.

features.title: Every domain change expires the hostname lookup, so a removed or re-pointed domain stops within seconds
acceptance: One function, `expireDomainHost(hostname)` (normalizes with `lookupKey`; never throws: a failed expiry is logged and the TTLs of M8-10 are the backstop), is called after every server-side change to a `domains` row and nowhere else: add (the insert as pending), verify (pending or errored to verified, by the live poll, 'Check DNS now' and the five-minute sweep: M4-15), a stale pending row removed (M5-18), re-point (`page_id` changed: M4-16), removal by the owner (M4-17), removal of a page's domains when the page is deleted (M4-19), removal of every domain of an account on account deletion (M4-34) and any admin action that deletes or changes a domain. A Vitest static scan: every `.from("domains")` insert, update, upsert or delete, and every RPC that changes a domain's mapping or status (`mark_domain_verified`; not `claim_domain_check` or `claim_domain_live_email`, which only stamp times), under `src/` sits in a module that also calls `expireDomainHost` after the write has succeeded; a poll that changes nothing expires nothing (no churn).

Order and failure: the hostname entry is expired after the database change has succeeded (a request in between cannot put the old answer back after the expiry); a failing expiry never turns a successful add, verify, re-point or removal into an error response (the action returns its normal result and logs); and the existing page-tag expiry that follows a domain change (`expirePage`, whose og:url names the domain) is still called as before. The Vercel domains stub removal still happens before the row is deleted, as in M4-17.

End to end, Playwright against the production build on :3100 with the Vercel stub (the M4-09, M4-16 and M4-17 fixtures; the custom host by Host header), one test per row, each expecting the first request after the change to be right: a hostname that answered 404 (so it sits in the ten-second 'none' entry) serves the page on the first request after it is verified; re-pointing the domain to another of the account's pages serves that page's published content; removing it answers 404 (M4-17 step 2); deleting the page and deleting the account answer 404; a stale pending row removed by the sweep answers 404 and a later add of the same hostname works. If the chosen mechanism cannot expire across instances, these tests poll every 500 ms for at most 5 seconds on the one local server, where the change is still immediate, and the larger bound is stated in step 5.

Other people's data (full test): A has `links.example.test` verified on A's page and a request has just been served from the cache; A removes the domain, then B, another account, adds and verifies the same hostname for B's page. The first request after B's verification returns B's page and no request after A's removal ever returns A's content; with B's domain re-pointed to B's second page the same holds; a hostname cached for A is never answered for another hostname (separate keys); and a request for A's removed hostname leaks neither A's name nor handle in the 404 body.

How long a stale answer can live, as numbers recorded in PROGRESS.md beside the mechanism M8-10 chose. With a shared tagged cache the first request after any change is right on every instance. With a per-instance cache a removed or re-pointed domain can serve its old page for up to `CUSTOM_DOMAIN_FOUND_SECONDS` (60) and a newly verified domain 404 for up to `CUSTOM_DOMAIN_NONE_SECONDS` (10), on an instance the action did not run on. A change made outside the app (SQL, the Supabase dashboard) is bounded by the same two numbers: a Vitest with fake timers and no expiry call shows a removed row still served at 59 seconds and gone at 61, and a newly verified one still missing at 9 seconds and served at 11.

No extra work for pages and no new way in: expiring a hostname touches no page tag and no page tag expiry touches a hostname; `expireDomainHost` is callable from Server Actions and Route Handlers alike (the verify sweep is a route), is exported from `src/lib/publish` or `src/lib/domains` and not from client code, and takes no input from a request (a Vitest feeds it hostile strings: it normalizes or ignores them and never throws).

Supersedes: only if the chosen mechanism cannot expire entries across instances: M4-16 step 2 ('the very next request to links.example.test serves the other page's published content') and M4-17 step 2 ('the very next request to links.example.test returns 404 (no stale cache)') then read 'at once on the server that ran the action, and within `CUSTOM_DOMAIN_FOUND_SECONDS` (60 s) anywhere'; tests/e2e/m4/domains-core-routing.spec.ts, domains-ui-actions.spec.ts and domains-ui.spec.ts poll for up to 5 seconds on the single local server, and the relaxation is written in PROGRESS.md and under 'Open for Gary'. M4-09 step 7 (a publish shows on the custom host at once) is about the page cache and is unchanged. M4-11 to M4-17, M4-34 and M5-18 hold unchanged.

features.title: Raw events are kept for 60 days, and the rollups for good
acceptance: A new migration (a timestamp after 20261007000002, never an edit of 20261004000002_analytics.sql) replaces `public.purge_old_events()` with `create or replace`: the same signature and body, with the cutoff `((now() at time zone 'utc')::date - 60)::timestamp at time zone 'utc'`, so the events of every UTC day more than 60 days before the current UTC day are deleted (day -60 stays, day -61 goes), each such day rolled up first in the same transaction (a failing rollup aborts the delete). It stays `security definer` with an empty `search_path`, callable by `service_role` only (the revokes and the grant are restated), its comment says 60, and the cron job `purge-old-events` stays at `30 0 * * *` with the command `select public.purge_old_events()` (the migration does not touch it). `pnpm db:reset` applies it and `pnpm db:types` leaves `src/lib/supabase/database.types.ts` unchanged.

pgTAP (supabase/tests/database/060-analytics-and-server-only.test.sql updated, or a new file): events at 00:00:00 and 23:59:59 UTC of day -60, at 23:59:59 of day -61 and on days -59, -90 and -120. After `purge_old_events()` both day -60 rows and the day -59 row remain and the day -61, -90 and -120 rows are gone; the rollups of the three purged days exist in `daily_stats` and `daily_dim_stats` with the right views, clicks, referrers, devices and countries, including a day that had no rollup row beforehand; no `daily_stats` or `daily_dim_stats` row is deleted by the job; a second run deletes 0 events and changes no rollup; the return value is the number of events deleted; the `cron.job` row `purge-old-events` still exists with schedule `30 0 * * *` and the same command; and the abuse case of M4-25 step 4 stands: `POST /rest/v1/rpc/purge_old_events` with the publishable key as anon and as authenticated is rejected and no events row is deleted (tests/e2e/m4/analytics-db-api.spec.ts).

Nothing that reads history changes. The 7, 30, 90 day and 1-year ranges, the Free plan's 30-day window (`plan_limits('free').analytics_history_days` is 30, pinned by pgTAP) and the Pro and Studio one-year range read `daily_stats` and `daily_dim_stats`; the dashboard reads raw events only for today and for completed days among the last three with no rollup row (`ROLLUP_DAYS`, src/lib/analytics/stats.ts). With raw events older than 60 days gone, Playwright and Vitest show a Pro page whose views from 70 days ago were rolled up and purged still shows them in the 90-day and 1-year ranges, with their referrers, devices and countries (M4-28 step 4 now seeds 70 and 120 days ago), and a Free page still gets 30 days and the upgrade cards for 90 days and a year (M4-30).

The high-traffic rule needs no raw rows: `flag_high_traffic_pages` reads `daily_stats` only (M7-10), so purging the raw events of the earlier complete month (up to about 92 days back) changes no flag. A pgTAP case rolls up views for each of the two complete months, runs `purge_old_events()` with their raw rows older than 60 days, and the page is still flagged with the same `views` and `views_previous_month`.

The copy says 60 days everywhere it described the raw retention: `src/app/(marketing)/privacy/page.tsx` (the 'Retention.' sentence and the list item 'Individual visitor events: 60 days, then only daily totals remain, for as long as the page exists'), `src/app/(marketing)/link-analytics/page.tsx` (the FAQ line 'Individual views and clicks are kept for 60 days, then combined into daily totals.'), `src/components/marketing/guides/understanding-analytics.tsx`, docs/PLAN.md ('Keep 60 days raw'; its 7/30/90-day/1-year dashboard ranges stay), `src/lib/analytics/SCHEMA.md` (the heading and table of the retention section, the 'day -60 stays, day -61 goes' note, and the schedule paragraph's raw-fallback sentence, which no longer says 90) and the comment in src/lib/analytics/stats.ts. One exported constant, `RAW_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS` = 60 in `src/lib/analytics`, is what the marketing copy renders, and a Vitest reads the newest migration that defines `purge_old_events` and fails when its day count differs from the constant, so the text and the SQL cannot drift. A scan of src/, docs/ and supabase/ finds no sentence that says raw events, views or clicks are kept 90 days (the 'Last 90 days' range label, the 90d button and the prose about ranges stay).

Fixtures and comments that assumed 90 days of raw events are updated, not worked around: tests/e2e/m4/analytics-dash-breakdowns.spec.ts (the '90 day retention' comments and the 120-day-old rollup), tests/e2e/m4/analytics-db-api.spec.ts (the describe title), tests/e2e/m4/lifecycle-downgrade.spec.ts, tests/e2e/marketing/site.spec.ts (the privacy page now contains '60 days'), tests/unit/analytics-db-review-action.test.ts, tests/unit/m7-policy-traffic-db.test.ts and tests/e2e/m5/traffic-helpers.ts, whose raw events for the earlier month 'inside the 90 days' are now inserted and rolled up in the same test so they never depend on raw rows still existing. The 'Last 90 days' range tests (M4-26 step 1) are unchanged.

features.title: One class-name helper, cn, for the HYDLNK UI
acceptance: File `src/lib/cn.ts` exports `cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]): string` and nothing else but the `ClassValue` type: `twMerge(clsx(inputs))`. It imports only `clsx` and `tailwind-merge`, has no `'use client'` and no `server-only` import, and is safe in server and client code. Both packages are in package.json at the exact versions of the approved list (clsx 2.1.1, tailwind-merge 3.7.0, no `^` or `~`) and a Vitest reads their `license` fields (MIT).

Vitest table, using the classes this app really writes: `cn('p-2','p-4')` is 'p-4'; `cn('text-sm', false, undefined, null, ['font-semibold', { hidden: true, block: false }])` is 'text-sm font-semibold hidden'; `cn('text-ink','text-sm')` keeps both (a color and a size are not in conflict); `cn('bg-surface','bg-page')` is 'bg-page'; `cn('hl:size-11','hl:size-[280px]')` is 'hl:size-[280px]' (the custom `hl:` breakpoint is read as a variant, so a later rule in the same breakpoint wins and a rule in another breakpoint is kept); `cn('min-h-11','min-h-12')` is 'min-h-12'; `cn()` and `cn(undefined)` are ''.

Use, no mass rewrite: the commit changes `src/lib/cn.ts`, its test and at most five existing files that already build a conditional class string by hand (for example the selected-tab class in `src/components/workspace/workspace-tabs.tsx` and the align-based class in `toolbar-menu.tsx`), each to call `cn`. Every other component is untouched (`git diff --stat` in review). From this wave on, every new or touched component that joins conditional class names uses `cn` (the Wave K features follow it), and none writes a template literal with a `${cond ? 'a' : 'b'}` class.

The tenant side never gets it: a Vitest module-graph scan from the two tenant route files and everything under `src/lib/tenant-render`, `src/lib/tenant-assets` and `src/components/page` finds no import of `@/lib/cn`, `clsx` or `tailwind-merge` (tenant pages use their own `pg-*` classes and `--t-*` variables, never HYDLNK utilities, `.claude/rules/tenant-pages.md`), and the one tenant script stays byte-identical (the hashed file name is the same as before this feature).

No visible change: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` pass, and `pnpm screens /editor --host app` before and after give identical screenshots at both viewports (pixel diff of 0 on /editor, /design and /share).

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor, /design and /share: no layout change from the commit before this feature (`scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, every button, input and standalone link at least 44px tall, the toolbar and tabs where M7-05 puts them).
At 1440x900 on the same URLs: no layout change (the toolbar is one 56px row, the content column and the 330px preview column start under it).
Supersedes: nothing.

features.title: Lucide icons replace the hand-drawn UI icons in the app
acceptance: Scope: every icon the person sees on the app host and in the editor: the sidebar and the phone tab bar (Editor, Analytics, Domains, Account), the page switcher, the workspace toolbar (Undo, Redo, the chevron on 'Preview', the '⋯' of 'More actions', the pencil of 'Rename page'), the editor (add-block chips, block rows, drag grip, upload, the focus marker, the position and preview controls), Design (font picker, gradient panel, themes carousel arrows and card menu), Settings, Analytics, Domains (step list), Admin, the template picker, versions and the mini phone. Not in scope, unchanged: the public page renderer (`src/components/page`), the marketing site (`src/components/marketing`), the HYDLNK logo (`logo.tsx`, `app-logo.tsx`), the QR code drawing and the favicon.

Import rule: named imports from 'lucide-react' only (`import { Pencil } from 'lucide-react'`), never `import *`, never `lucide-react/dynamic` or `DynamicIcon`. A Vitest scan of `src` finds none of those, finds no `lucide-react` import in `src/components/page`, `src/components/marketing`, `src/lib/tenant-render`, `src/lib/tenant-assets` or the two tenant route files (Lucide's `Icon` is a client component, and the static HTML pipeline may not reach one, M8-02), and the production build's marketing and tenant chunks contain no Lucide code (a scan of the chunks those two routes load for the string 'lucide' finds nothing).

Size and stroke keep what the hand-drawn icons had, so nothing looks heavier: each icon is drawn on the 24 grid at the size its predecessor had (16px in the sidebar and tabs, 18px for the toolbar's '⋯' and 'Undo', 15px in the editor's chips, 14px for the 'Preview' chevron) with `strokeWidth` 1.8 (1.9 where the editor icons had it), round caps and joins, `currentColor`. docs/DESIGN.md has no icon rule today: this feature adds a short 'Icons' paragraph to it (Lucide, 24 grid, stroke 1.8, the four sizes, decorative by default) and the Vitest reads that the paragraph exists. One small wrapper or the library's own default props sets `aria-hidden='true'`, `focusable='false'` and `shrink-0` once, so a call site passes only the icon and the size.

Accessible names do not change: every icon-only control keeps its `aria-label` or visible text exactly ('Undo', 'Redo', 'More actions', 'Rename page', 'Show previous themes', 'Show next themes', 'More for Paper', 'Move up', 'Move down', 'Remove'), every Lucide icon is `aria-hidden='true'`, and no existing Playwright locator by role and name changes. A Vitest renders each converted component and finds no `<title>` inside an icon.

Clean-up: the now-unused hand-drawn components are deleted, not left behind: `src/components/app/icons.tsx` (EditorIcon, DesignIcon, AnalyticsIcon, DomainsIcon, BillingIcon and the rest of that file) and `src/components/editor/icons.tsx` (UploadIcon, GripIcon and the rest), and every inline `<svg>` that drew a UI icon in `src/components/app/page-switcher-menu.tsx`, `workspace/toolbar/more-menu.tsx`, `workspace/toolbar/preview-menu.tsx`, `editor/undo-redo-controls.tsx`, `editor/page-name.tsx`, `design/font-picker.tsx`, `design/sections/gradient-panel.tsx`, `blocks/forms/focus-picker.tsx`, `domains/step-list.tsx`, `billing/manage-billing-button.tsx`, `themes/card-menu.tsx`, `themes/theme-carousel.tsx` and `workspace/mini-preview/*`. A Vitest scan of `src/components` (except `marketing`, `page` and `tenant`) and `src/app/(editor)` finds an inline `<svg` only in an allowlist inside the test (the QR code in `qr-card.tsx`, the two logo components, and any drawing that is not an icon, each with a one-line reason), so a new hand-drawn icon fails the test.

States and color: an icon follows its control's text color in every state (default, hover, focus, `aria-pressed`, `aria-disabled`, selected tab, the brass icon of the current sidebar item from M1-16, the disabled Undo at the start of the history). Playwright computed-style check on the sidebar item, the Undo button and a selected tab: the icon's `stroke` equals the control's computed `color`. No icon uses a `--t-*` variable and none appears inside a tenant renderer.

Bundle: only the imported icons ship (a production build's /editor chunks contain none of the unused Lucide icon names, for example 'Anchor' and 'Zap'), and opening the editor, the design tab, the share tab and analytics logs no console error or warning and no request to any host but the app's own.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor, /design, /share, /analytics, /domains and /settings: no icon is clipped or shifted (the bottom tab bar's four icons sit 16px above their 11px labels, as before), `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, and every icon-only control is still at least 44px tall and 44px wide.

At 1440x900 on the same URLs: the sidebar items keep their 44px rows with a 16px icon, the toolbar keeps its 56px row with 44x44 icon buttons, and a screenshot of each screen differs from the commit before only where an icon's shape changed (no spacing or size difference measured on the controls' bounding boxes, within 1px).

Supersedes: nothing in the steps; every step that names an icon's size or accessible name (M1-16, M1-17, M6-21, M7-05, M7-06) holds unchanged. The hand-drawn glyph shapes are no longer a requirement anywhere.

features.title: Six more social platforms: Reddit, Snapchat, Pinterest, Discord, Twitch and Spotify
acceptance: Schema: `SOCIAL_PLATFORMS` becomes instagram, tiktok, youtube, x, facebook, linkedin, github, threads, reddit, snapchat, pinterest, discord, twitch, spotify, email, website (Email and Website stay last), and `SOCIAL_PLATFORM_LABELS` gains 'Reddit', 'Snapchat', 'Pinterest', 'Discord', 'Twitch' and 'Spotify'. The six store a `url` like every web platform; `email` still stores an address. A social block still holds 1 to 8 icons (`LIMITS.socialIconsMax` is unchanged) and `version` stays 1. Vitest table: each of the sixteen platforms parses in the draft and the publish schema with a valid https URL (the email icon with an address); 'Reddit' (capitalized), 'mastodon', '__proto__', 'constructor' and '' fail with the platform error; the Wave G and M2-31 fixtures give a byte-identical `toPublishForm` before and after, so every older document is unchanged.

URL rules: the six use the same `url()` rule as the other web platforms (M2-17): http or https only, no credentials, no whitespace or control characters, at most 2048 characters, and the draft keeps any string until Publish. No per-platform host allowlist is added, because none of the existing platforms has one; that decision is recorded in PROGRESS.md. Publish names the failing icon by id.

Abuse cases (Vitest, and a Playwright run with the owner's JWT and the publishable key writing the draft as raw JSON): for each new platform a `url` of `javascript:alert(1)`, `data:text/html,x`, `//evil.example`, `https://user@host.example/`, a 4,000-character URL and a URL with a line break is refused at Publish with the icon's id in the errors, never reaches `pages.published` and never renders an anchor on http://mara.localhost:3000/. A hidden social block with a bad icon does not stop Publish (it is dropped).

Blocklist: no new migration is needed because `blocked_links_in` reads the `url` of every entry of `icons` by shape, not by platform name; pgTAP and Vitest (extending the M5-03 files) prove it with a `discord` and a `spotify` icon pointing at a listed domain: the save fails with `blocked_link` (HL005, host in the detail, the block id in the hint) and Publish refuses it on the final published form with the platform URL parser, and the same icons pointing at an unlisted host pass. The editor shows 'That site is blocked. Use a different link.' under the icon's row (M5-03).

Click redirect and analytics: `findLinkUrl` resolves the id of each new icon, so GET http://mara.localhost:3000/r/<pageId>/<icon id> answers 302 with `Location` exactly the published URL, `Cache-Control: no-store`, no `Set-Cookie`, and inserts one `events` row of type 'click' with `block_id` equal to the icon id; an icon id that exists only in the draft, in a hidden block or on another page answers 404 and inserts nothing. 'Clicks by link' on the Analytics screen names the icon by its platform label ('Reddit', 'Discord'), and after the icon is removed and the page republished its old clicks read 'Removed link' (M4-27; Vitest on `linkLabelsFromPublished`).

Editor: the platform select of an icon row lists the sixteen platforms in the order above; 'Add icon' still picks the first platform not already in the row, so a block of eight starts with the first eight; the block row's title lists the labels ('Reddit, Discord, Email'); the sub line stays '{n} icons'. Changing a row from Email to a new platform clears the address and shows the URL field (and back), as for the existing platforms. Every platform has a glyph: a Vitest iterates `SOCIAL_PLATFORMS` and fails for a platform with no entry in the glyph table (the shapes themselves are M9-04, and the two features ship together).

Parity: `renderToStaticMarkup` of the editor preview and of the live mode give identical markup for a social block holding all six new icons, and a Playwright compare of the block's `outerHTML` in the editor preview and on http://mara.localhost:3000/ after Publish matches; each anchor's `aria-label` is the platform name and its href is `/r/<pageId>/<icon id>`.

At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/ (published fixture: a social block of eight icons made of the six new platforms plus Instagram and Email): the row wraps, every icon is at least 44x44, `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the icons are centered in the 480px column.

Supersedes: M2-17 step 1's platform list of ten (now sixteen, in the order above) and the 'Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Email' example order of its step 2 only in that Add icon walks the longer list; every other step of M2-17 and M5-03 holds.

features.title: Real brand marks from Simple Icons in the social row and the link icons
acceptance: Source and shape: the thirteen brands that Simple Icons has (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X, Facebook, GitHub, Threads, Reddit, Snapchat, Pinterest, Discord, Twitch, Spotify) are drawn from the package's own path data, imported by name (`import { siInstagram } from 'simple-icons'`, never `import *`, never a dynamic import) at version 16.34.0, and rendered unaltered: the `d` of each rendered `<path>` equals `siX.path` byte for byte (Vitest table over all thirteen), in the package's 24x24 box, with no transform, scale, rotation, recolor or edit. Each mark is one filled `<path>` with `fill: currentColor` and `stroke: none`, so it takes the anchor's `--t-text` (or the block's Icon color override, M6-46) and never the brand's own hex.

LinkedIn is not in Simple Icons at the pinned version (a Vitest asserts the package has no LinkedIn export, so an upgrade that adds one is noticed). Its mark is the official 'in' square from LinkedIn's brand guidelines, drawn as one `<path>` in the same 24x24 box and the same single color, with a code comment naming the source (LinkedIn's brand and media guidelines page, the date it was checked) and saying that it was drawn from the published proportions, so no file was downloaded. Vitest: exactly one `<path>`, at most 1.5 KB of path data, every coordinate inside 0 to 24.

Server render only, no library JS on public pages: the live document holds each mark as inline `<svg class='pg-social-glyph' viewBox='0 0 24 24' aria-hidden='true' focusable='false'><path d='...'/></svg>` written by the static renderer. A Vitest module-graph scan from the two tenant route files reaches `simple-icons` (plain data, no `'use client'`) and reaches no `lucide-react`, no Radix, no Tiptap and no client library (M9-14 pins the list), the one tenant script's hashed file name is unchanged by this feature, and a scan of the built server chunks of the two tenant routes finds the paths of the marks in the list and none of an unrelated icon (for example Adobe, Zoom, Notion), so the package's whole index is not bundled.

Budget (M8-09 holds on its own fixture): the fixture's social block (four icons) still gives a first visit of 1 document, 2 fonts, 1 script and 1 beacon to the page's own host, 0 third-party requests and at most 90 KB, with the document at most 16 KB as the edge sends it; the before and after document sizes are listed in the PROGRESS.md entry. A page with no social block carries no social rule and no mark (the M8-02 selector check still passes).

CSS: the `.pg-social-glyph` rule keeps the 18px box, and a brand glyph gets `fill: currentcolor; stroke: none` while the generic Email and Website glyphs keep their outline style (`fill: none; stroke: currentcolor`), selected by one modifier class, so a page whose social block holds only Email and Website renders byte-identical markup to before. The static scans of M2-05 and M6-34 (no color literals, no `@media` but prefers-reduced-motion, no `--hl-` reference) still pass on the CSS.

Link icons: the eight brand entries of `LINK_ICONS` (instagram, tiktok, youtube, x, facebook, linkedin, github, threads) use the same marks from one shared glyph table, filled `currentColor` at 20px; the sixteen other names (link, mail, globe, music, video, mic, camera, calendar, bag, ticket, heart, star, book, gift, pin, phone) keep their current outline glyphs and render byte-identical markup. `LINK_ICONS` stays 24 names in the same order: the six new brands are not added to it (decision recorded in PROGRESS.md; M6-20 and M6-21 hold, the picker still shows 'No icon' and 24 icons). Playwright on a published page: every brand glyph's computed `fill` equals its anchor's computed `color` and its `stroke` is 'none', at both viewports.

Editor: each icon row of the social block shows the platform's mark in a 24px tile next to the platform select (decorative, `aria-hidden`), so the picker shows what visitors will see; the 'Choose icon' grid of a link block (M6-21) shows the brand marks filled and keeps every button's `aria-label` ('Instagram', 'LinkedIn', ...). The tile is drawn by the same component the renderer uses, so editor and page cannot drift.

Escaping and trust: no string from the document reaches a path, an attribute or a class: the platform name is looked up in a fixed table (a Vitest feeds `__proto__`, `constructor` and `<script>` as a platform and gets no glyph and no throw). Licensing: Simple Icons is CC0-1.0 (a Vitest reads the package's `license`), the marks are trademarks of their owners and are used only to link to those services, and a one-line note says so next to the glyph table.

Parity: `renderToStaticMarkup` in preview and live mode is identical for a social block with all fourteen platforms' marks (eight icons per block, two blocks) and for a link block with each of the eight brand icons, and a Playwright compare of the `outerHTML` after Publish matches.

At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/ (published fixture: two social blocks covering all fourteen brand platforms and link blocks with the eight brand icons): every mark is drawn inside its 44x44 circle without clipping (the path's bounding box lies inside the 18px glyph box), `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, every anchor at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the same marks, centered in the 480px column, with the link icons at the start edge of their buttons.

Supersedes: M2-17 step 3's 'bundled inline SVG at 18px' keeps its size and 'no remote icon fonts', but a brand icon is now a filled mark, not a stroked line (the hand-drawn brand glyphs are gone); M6-20 step 4's 'the eight brand glyphs reuse the social row's glyphs' still holds, with stroke `currentColor` replaced by fill `currentColor` for those eight.

features.title: Radix dropdown menus for Preview, More actions and the account menu
acceptance: Scope: `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu` 2.1.24 drives exactly three menus: the workspace toolbar's 'Preview' menu, its '⋯' menu (`aria-label='More actions'`) and the sidebar's account menu ('Account menu'). The shared `ToolbarMenu` (used by the first two) and `AccountMenu` are rebuilt on it; their hand-written open state, arrow-key code, outside-press listener and focus code are deleted (a Vitest scan of `toolbar-menu.tsx` and `account-menu.tsx` finds no `onMenuKeyDown`, no `pointerdown` listener on `document` and no `focusOnOpen`). Every other menu, among them the page switcher's, the theme card's 'More' and the marketing menu, stays as it is (a scan finds the Radix import in exactly these two files).

Items and links keep their meaning: 'Preview your draft' is still a real link with `target='_blank'` and `rel='noopener'` that writes pending edits first on a plain click (M6-11, M7-05), 'View live page' stays focusable and `aria-disabled` with the description 'Not published yet' until the first Publish (an `aria-disabled` item whose select is canceled, not Radix's `disabled`, which would remove it from keyboard focus), 'Private preview link…' goes to /share#preview-links and focuses 'Create link', 'QR code' goes to /share#qr, 'Version history' keeps its plain-click flush and the brass-soft 'Pro' chip on Free, 'Settings & billing' stays a link to /settings with `aria-current='page'` on that screen, and 'Sign out' stays a `<button type='submit'>` inside a `<form>` that calls the `signOut` Server Action (a POST, never a link: the M7-01 static check still passes). The `data-menu-item`, `data-history-link`, `data-history-pro-chip` and `data-account-menu` attributes are kept for the specs.

Behavior (Playwright at both viewports where the control exists): the trigger has `aria-haspopup='menu'`, `aria-expanded` and (open) `aria-controls`; Enter, Space and ArrowDown open the menu with focus on the first item and ArrowUp on the last (a pointer open leaves focus on the menu itself); inside, the arrows move and wrap (`loop`), Home and End jump, Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger, a press outside closes it, and choosing an item closes it. Typing a letter jumps to the item that starts with it. Each item is at least 44px tall and the menu is named 'Preview', 'More actions' and 'Account'.

Not modal, no page shift: the menus use `modal={false}`, so opening one does not lock the page's scroll or add padding. Playwright at 1440x900: the toolbar's, the content column's and the preview bezel's bounding boxes are identical (within 0.5px) before and after opening each menu, and with 30 blocks scrolled 800px down the toolbar's top is still 0 with the menu open. The panel is portaled to `body` and positioned by Radix: 'Preview' and 'More actions' open under their buttons aligned to the end, and the account menu opens above the user block, full width of the block, and stays fully inside the viewport at 1440x900 and at 1440x500 (collision handling flips and shifts it).

What changes and is recorded: Tab no longer leaves an open menu (Radix keeps focus in it; Escape or a press outside closes it) where M7-05 step 3 and M7-01 step 2 said 'Tab leaves'; the menu element is no longer a sibling inside the toolbar's DOM but a `body`-level portal; the unmounted-when-closed behavior is kept. The M7-05 and M7-01 specs are updated for those two facts and every other assertion in them passes as written.

Nothing else moves: opening a menu changes no draft, adds no undo step and sends no request (network log); Escape inside an open menu while the page-name field holds an unsaved rename does not cancel the rename (the key is consumed by the menu); the 'Rename page' pencil, the status chip, the save indicator, 'Undo', 'Redo' and 'Publish' keep their order and sizes; the phone toolbar still has no Preview and no '⋯' menu (M7-05).

Styled with HYDLNK UI tokens only (the existing menu classes, `border-line-3`, `bg-surface`, `bg-ink-raised` for the account menu), no `--t-*` variable, with the focus ring and hover color the old menus had; a Vitest scan finds no Radix import in `src/components/page`, `src/components/marketing`, `src/lib/tenant-render` or the tenant routes (the tenant pages ship no library JS).

Accessibility: axe-core finds no serious or critical violation with each menu open at 1440x900 and with the account menu open at 1440x900 (the phone has no sidebar); `role='menu'` and `role='menuitem'` are what the specs already query; focus is visible with the 2px brass outline.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor: no Preview, no '⋯' and no account menu exists (the phone's account route is the 'Account' tab, M7-01), `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, and every button, input and standalone link is at least 44px tall.

At 1440x900 on the same URL: the three menus open as described, inside the viewport, at the sizes above, and a screenshot of each open menu matches the commit before within the shape of the panel (width `min(15rem, 100vw - 2rem)`, 6px corners, the same item rows).

Supersedes: M7-05 step 3's 'Keyboard as the page switcher's menu' sentence (Radix is now the reference: Tab does not leave an open menu) and 'Tab leaves'; M7-01 step 2's 'Tab leaves it and closes it'. Everything else in M7-05 steps 3 and 4 and M7-01 steps 2 to 4 holds.

features.title: Radix dialog for the template picker
acceptance: Pick: `@radix-ui/react-dialog` 1.1.23 replaces the template picker's dialog (`src/components/templates/template-dialog.tsx`), because it carries the most hand-written focus code (a `FOCUSABLE` Tab loop, `useScrollLock`, a `showModal` effect and a refocus ref). The QR code is no longer a dialog (it is the inline card on the Share tab since M7-04), and every other dialog (Position your photo, Rename theme, Delete theme, Delete page, Delete account, the publish alert) stays a native `<dialog>`. A Vitest scan finds `@radix-ui/react-dialog` imported in exactly one file, and finds none of `showModal`, `FOCUSABLE`, `documentElement.style.overflow` and `<dialog` in `template-dialog.tsx`.

Structure: `Dialog.Root` controlled by the caller's open state, `Dialog.Portal`, `Dialog.Overlay` (the `bg-ink/60` backdrop), `Dialog.Content` (`data-testid='template-dialog'`, `role='dialog'`, `aria-modal='true'` passed explicitly so the M6-40 and M7-07 assertions hold, labelled by `Dialog.Title` 'Start from a template' and described by `Dialog.Description` 'Pick a starting point, then change anything you like.'), the 'Close' button, and the same six cards in the order Musician, Podcaster, Artist, Shop, Coach, Streamer with their previews, 'Inside' and 'Style' lines and 'Use this template' buttons. The card and preview code is not touched.

Behavior kept exactly (Playwright as a Free fixture user at 1440x900 and 390x844): opening the dialog puts focus on the first card's 'Use this template' (`onOpenAutoFocus`); Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside it and wrap; Escape and 'Close' close it without touching the draft and return focus to the 'Start from a template' button that opened it (`onCloseAutoFocus` focuses it explicitly, because the opener sits outside the dialog); 'Use this template' opens the choice in place and Cancel puts focus back on that card's button (M6-40, M7-08); a click on the backdrop does not close it (as today: `onPointerDownOutside` is prevented); the page behind does not scroll (wheel, touch and keyboard) and is not reachable by Tab; the previews stay `inert` and `aria-hidden` and add nothing to the accessibility tree, so the page keeps its one `h1` and the dialog adds no landmark.

No page shift: opening the dialog leaves `window.scrollY` and the toolbar's and column's bounding boxes unchanged (within 0.5px) and closing restores them; the test also runs with classic 15px scrollbars forced on (an injected `::-webkit-scrollbar` rule), so Radix's scroll-lock padding compensation is the path under test, not the hidden scrollbars of headless Chromium. The fonts stylesheet request (at most one `fonts.googleapis.com` request while the dialog is open, none before) and the previews' no-network rule of M7-07 are unchanged (network log).

What changes and is recorded: the dialog element is a `div` in a portal at the end of `body`, not a `<dialog>` and not a child of the editor, so the specs that selected `dialog[open]` or `page.locator('dialog')` use the role and the test id instead (the same specs M6-40, M7-07 and M7-08 already use for `getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Start from a template' })` pass unchanged). The dialog is still `aria-modal='true'` with a focus trap.

Accessibility: axe-core finds no serious or critical violation with the dialog open at 1440x900 and 390x844; each card's accessible name is its name and description; focus is visible with the 2px brass outline; the title and description ids are wired by Radix (no duplicate ids).
