features.title: A color picker for the Design colors and the per-block color overrides
acceptance: Scope: `react-colorful` 5.8.1 (`HexColorPicker`, six-digit hex, no alpha: the tokens and overrides are `#RRGGBB`, M3-18, M6-46) replaces every `<input type='color'>`: the color rows of the Design screen (Background, Text, Accent, Buttons and the gradient stops 'From' and 'To') and the color control of each block's 'Style this block' group (Color, Text color, Icon color, Line color, Border color). A static scan of `src` finds no `type='color'` and no `type="color"` left. The 16px hex field and the 'Theme default' button stay, with every rule they had: `#12` shows 'Use a #RRGGBB color, for example #C46A4F.' and writes nothing partial, a full six-digit value applies as it is typed, and the hostile string `#FFF;}</style>` shows the same message and writes nothing (the draft PATCHes in the network log never carry a value the schema rejects).

Control: each row keeps a 44x44 swatch, now a `<button type='button'>` named '{name} color' (for example 'Accent color') with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, that opens an inline panel (not a modal, not a popover: only the two approved Radix components exist) directly under the row holding the picker and a 'Done' button (secondary, 44px). Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the swatch; choosing another row's swatch closes this one; a theme or swatch change made some other way updates the open picker.

Picker behavior: dragging in the saturation square or on the hue strip writes the draft as it moves (the preview follows, `#RRGGBB` upper case, the same format the native input wrote) and the autosave status reads 'Saved' within 3 seconds of the last move; one pointer drag adds one undo step, so Undo after a drag restores the color from before the drag in one press and Redo restores the dragged color (Playwright reads the draft). The two interactive areas have `role='slider'` with the accessible names 'Color' and 'Hue' and `aria-valuetext`; the arrow keys move them by one step, and the keys do not trigger the workspace's undo or any other shortcut. Touch: a finger drag works and does not scroll the page (`touch-action: none` on the two areas only; the rest of the panel scrolls).

Targets: the saturation square is at least 160px tall and the hue strip, its thumb and the 'Done' button measure at least 44px tall (the library's default 24px strip is raised by the app's stylesheet), at 390 and at 1440; the swatch shows the current color with a 1px `--hl-line-2` border and the checked-state ring for the open row.

Nothing leaves the browser: the picker makes no request, uses no `localStorage`, and the stylesheet the library injects raises no Content Security Policy violation on the app host (Playwright listens for `securitypolicyviolation`). Public pages never ship it: a module-graph scan from the tenant routes, `src/components/page`, `src/lib/tenant-render` and the marketing site reaches no `react-colorful`, and the production build's tenant script and public chunks contain none.

Persistence and abuse: a picked color survives a reload, flips the status chip to 'Unpublished changes' and reaches http://mara.localhost:3000/ only after Publish; a color picked for a block that is then reordered, deleted and restored with Undo keeps its override (M6-46); a stored color in another form (`#RGB`, `#RRGGBBAA`) opens the picker on its six-digit equivalent without rewriting the draft until the person changes it. The picker never writes a value that fails `normalizeHex` (a Vitest feeds it NaN, Infinity and hostile strings through its `onChange`).

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/design and /editor (a block's style group expanded): the open panel is the row's full width inside the 358px content width, the square is at least 160px tall, nothing scrolls the page sideways (`scrollWidth <= innerWidth`), and every swatch, hex field, 'Theme default' and 'Done' is at least 44px tall.

At 1440x900 on the same URLs: the panel sits under its row inside the 720px column with no horizontal scroll, the live preview bezel updates while dragging, and a screenshot matches the commit before except for the swatch and the panel.

Supersedes: M3-17 and M3-18 where they describe 'a color control is the swatch plus 16px hex field plus Theme default button' as a native color input, and M6-46 step 1's sentence of the same shape (the swatch now opens the picker); every other assertion of those steps holds. Specs that drove `input[type=color]` drive the hex field instead.

features.title: Position your photo with react-easy-crop: drag, zoom and pinch
acceptance: Scope: `react-easy-crop` 6.2.3 draws the viewfinder of the existing 'Position your photo' dialog (M6-24), which is also 'Position your image' for link thumbnails (M6-21). The hand-written drag (`onPointerDown`, `movePicture`), the viewfinder layout and the pointer capture are replaced by the library's `Cropper` (`aspect` 1, `minZoom` 1, `maxZoom` 4, `restrictPosition` on so the picture always covers the viewfinder and there are never empty edges, `showGrid` off, `zoomWithScroll` off so a wheel over the dialog scrolls the dialog as today). The dialog stays a native `<dialog>` (Radix is for the template picker only), with the same titles, 'Zoom' slider (1x to 4x, 44px), 'Reset', 'Cancel' and 'Use photo' or 'Use image' buttons.

Shapes: the photo's outline is a circle (`cropShape='round'`) and the link thumbnail's is a square with the 6px radius (`cropAreaStyle`); the outline, the dimmed area outside it and the focus ring use HYDLNK UI tokens only. The picture is never stretched, and a 6000x4000 phone JPEG with EXIF orientation 6 opens upright within 2 seconds.

Input (Playwright at 1440x900 with the mouse, and at 390x844 with raw touch events through CDP): a drag moves the picture; the slider and the plus and minus keys zoom (0.25 steps); a two-finger pinch zooms from 1x to at least 1.5x in one gesture and the slider and the polite live region follow ('Zoom 200 percent'); the arrow keys move the picture by 10px and Shift+arrow by 1px when the viewfinder has focus (the dialog's own key handler drives the library's controlled `crop` and `zoom`); the viewfinder is focusable with the name 'Picture position' and the hint text of M6-24; a touch drag inside the viewfinder moves the picture and leaves `window.scrollY` unchanged (`touch-action: none` on the viewfinder only).

Output and stored data are unchanged: 'Use photo' draws the chosen square from the `croppedAreaPixels` the library reports, at the source's real resolution and at most 800px on a side (a JPEG at quality 0.9, or a PNG for a PNG or WebP with transparency) and hands the file to `onUse`; the upload route, `kind=avatar`, the 400x400 WebP of at most 100 KB and the `{uid}/avatar-{hash}.webp` path are exactly M5-11. No crop, focus or zoom value is stored or sent: the image reference schema still has no `zoom` key (a Vitest feeds `{path, width, height, zoom: 2}` and the key is stripped), `processUpload` ignores `crop`, `x`, `y`, `zoom` and `focus` form fields as before, and the focus control of card and image blocks (M6-25) is untouched and keeps its `focus: {x, y}` from 0 to 1, because the document has no zoom to keep. The red-and-blue fixture of M6-24 dragged so only blue is inside the viewfinder still gives an avatar whose center pixel is blue.

Dialog behavior kept: Escape and 'Cancel' upload nothing (no POST /api/media in the network log) and return focus to the button that opened it; Tab stays inside; the page behind does not scroll; a failed crop shows 'We couldn’t prepare that picture. Try again.' inline; 'Reset' returns to 1x centered; 'Use photo' shows 'Uploading...' until the avatar appears (M6-24).

No library on public pages and nothing remote: a module-graph scan from the tenant routes, `src/components/page`, `src/lib/tenant-render` and the marketing site reaches no `react-easy-crop`; the library makes no network request and the stylesheet it injects raises no CSP violation on the app host (it is loaded only when a file is picked: the /editor first load holds no 'easy-crop' chunk).

Accessibility: axe-core finds no serious or critical violation with the dialog open at both viewports; focus is visible; the live region announces zoom changes from the slider, the keys and the pinch.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor: the dialog is a full-height sheet (`100dvh`) with the two buttons pinned at the bottom above the safe-area inset, the viewfinder fills the width, `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, and every button, the slider and the viewfinder's controls are at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the dialog is centered, about 440px wide, with a 280px viewfinder, and the same fixture images give the same outputs as before this feature (center pixel and dimensions).

Supersedes: M6-24 step 2's internals ('pointer events, `touch-action: none` on the viewfinder' and 'a 'Zoom' slider' as hand-written code) and step 3's key handling as the dialog's own code; every outcome and copy in M6-24 holds, and pinch-to-zoom on phones is added.

features.title: The 'your domain is live' email, rebuilt with react-email
acceptance: Template: `src/emails/domain-live.tsx` exports one component taking `{ hostname }` and built from the components of `react-email` 6.11.0 (Html, Head, Body, Container, Text, Link or Button); `src/lib/domains/live-email.ts` calls `render(<DomainLive hostname={...} />)` for the HTML and `render(..., { plainText: true })` for the text part (awaited: `liveEmailContent` becomes async and `sendDomainLiveEmail` awaits it). The copy is M5-23's: subject '{hostname} is live', the sentence 'Your page is now served at https://{hostname}.', one link 'Open {hostname}' to `https://{hostname}/`, an HTML part and a plain-text part, no exclamation marks, nothing else.

Same sending path and sender: `sendDomainLiveEmail` keeps its three transports (SMTP through nodemailer when `SMTP_HOST` is set, with `EMAIL_FROM` or 'HYDLNK <hello@hydlnk.com>'; the local Mailpit HTTP API with From hello@hydlnk.com named HYDLNK otherwise; skipped with the existing log line when neither is configured) and its `EmailSenderDeps` injection points; the existing tests of `email.ts` with a fake `createTransport` and a fake `fetchImpl` pass unchanged except where they read the body. Verification of a domain never fails because of the email (an error is logged and swallowed, as before).

Hostile input: `hostname` comes from a stored `domains.hostname` (lower-case letters, digits, hyphens and dots), and anything else is refused before rendering: a value that does not match the hostname pattern (`"><script>alert(1)</script>.example`, one with a space, a newline, an uppercase letter or more than 253 characters) sends no email and logs one line without the value, and the verification result is unaffected. A Vitest renders the nearest valid-looking hostile strings through the component directly and finds every character escaped and no extra element.

End to end against the local Mailpit (the M5-23 flow, Vercel stub): verifying a custom domain delivers one message to the owner's address with subject '{hostname} is live', From hello@hydlnk.com (HYDLNK), and Mailpit's API shows both a non-empty `HTML` and a non-empty `Text` part with the content above; no second email goes out on a repeat verification poll.

Server only: `src/emails/` is imported by `src/lib/domains/*` server code and nowhere else, `react-email` is not in any client bundle, any tenant route or the marketing site (a module-graph scan and a scan of the production build's client chunks find none), no route, preview server or CLI script for the library is added, and the library makes no network call at render time (Vitest with `fetch` stubbed to throw).

At 390x844 (Playwright `page.setContent` of the HTML part in a phone viewport): no horizontal scroll (`scrollWidth <= innerWidth`), the link's box is at least 44px tall, and the container is at most 480px wide.
At 1440x900 the same rendering is a single readable column with the link visible without scrolling.

features.title: Sentry on the app side only, off by default and scrubbed of personal data
acceptance: Scope: `@sentry/nextjs` 11.4.0 reports errors and 10% of traces for the app host only: pages under `src/app/(editor)/app`, server actions and API routes there. It does not run on the marketing site, on public tenant pages (the static pipeline in `src/lib/tenant-render` and the one tenant script never load or call it), on `/r`, `/api/e`, `/media` or `/_t`. There is no `tunnelRoute` and no new route on any host: GET http://localhost:3000/monitoring and http://mara.localhost:3000/monitoring answer the same plain 404 as any unknown path.

Off unless configured: with `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` unset or not an https URL, `Sentry.init` is never called, no Sentry chunk is downloaded (the /editor network log holds no resource whose URL or contents name Sentry, the chunk is loaded by a dynamic import only when the DSN is set), no request goes to any Sentry host, and the console is silent; a malformed value is ignored with one server log line that names the variable and never the value. The client is started from one component mounted in the app host's layout (`src/app/(editor)/app/layout`) and the server from `instrumentation.ts`'s `register()`, which imports the server config only when the DSN is set; `instrumentation-client.ts` is not used because Next.js 16 would run it on every page including marketing.

No marketing and no tenant: a Vitest module-graph scan finds no import of `@sentry/*` or `src/lib/sentry/*` from `src/app/(marketing)`, `src/app/(tenant)`, `src/app/r`, `src/app/api/e`, `src/app/media`, `src/lib/tenant-render`, `src/lib/tenant-assets`, `src/components/page`, `src/components/marketing` or `src/components/tenant`; the production build with the DSN set shows no request to a Sentry host and no chunk containing `@sentry` on `/` and on http://mara.localhost:3000/ (network log and chunk scan), the M8-09 assertions pass unchanged (1 script, 0 third-party requests), the tenant script's hashed name is unchanged, and the tenant CSP (`connect-src 'self'`) is unchanged. A server event whose request URL is not on the app host, or whose path starts with /t/, /sites/, /r/, /api/e, /media/ or /_t/, is dropped by `beforeSend` (Vitest table of URLs).

Privacy: `sendDefaultPii` is false; `event.user` is removed and `Sentry.setUser` is never called; request cookies, headers (Cookie, Authorization, Set-Cookie), bodies and query strings are removed; breadcrumbs of console output are dropped and fetch and XHR breadcrumbs keep the path without a query. A pure scrubber (`scrubEvent`, Vitest) runs over the message, every exception value, the stack-frame variables, tags, extras, the request URL and the transaction name: an email address becomes '[email]'; a handle host (`mara.hydlnk.com`, `mara.localhost:3000` for the configured root domain) becomes '[handle].{root}'; `/t/{handle}`, `/sites/{id}` and `/share/{token}` become `/t/[handle]`, `/sites/[id]` and `/share/[token]`; the values of `token`, `code`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `key` and any `sb-` cookie or JWT-shaped string (three base64url parts) become '[Filtered]'. A fake-transport test (no network) throws an error whose message holds an email, a share-link URL and a JWT, and the envelope the SDK would send contains none of them.

Sampling and features: `tracesSampleRate` is 0.1 (read from one exported options object, Vitest), there is no session replay (no `replayIntegration`, both replay sample rates 0 or absent, and no `#sentry-feedback` or other widget in the DOM), `maxBreadcrumbs` is at most 20, and `sendClientReports` stays on. The DSN is the only destination and comes from the environment, never from a request.

Source maps upload only when `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT` are all set at build: `next.config.ts` wraps the config with `withSentryConfig` only in that case (telemetry off, `silent`, no tunnel route), and otherwise exports the plain config. Vitest imports the config with each combination (none, two of three, all three) and checks which one is wrapped; `pnpm build` with none of them makes no request to a Sentry host (the build log has no upload line).

Errors still behave: `global-error.tsx` and the app's error boundaries call one `reportError(error)` that does nothing when Sentry was not initialized (marketing and tenant errors never reach it); a thrown error in a server action of the app host and in an app API route is captured once with the scrubbed fields (Playwright against a build with the DSN pointing at a local stub endpoint, one envelope per error, none for an error on the marketing page or the tenant page); the visitor-facing error pages and the 'Page not found' panels are byte-identical to before.

Environment for Gary, documented in `.env.example` (names only, empty values), in the environment table of docs/PLAN.md and in the PROGRESS.md entry: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` (public by design, inlined at build), `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` (secret, build only), `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT`. All four are optional in `src/lib/env` (the Zod schemas parse with none set, the app builds and boots with none set, and `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is never exposed to the client: a client-bundle scan finds neither the name nor a value). Unattended runs never need them.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor, /design, /share, /analytics and /domains with the DSN set to the stub: the screens look and measure the same as with it unset (no banner, no overlay, no layout shift: the layout-shift sum differs by at most 0.01), `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, and every button, input and standalone link is at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the same URLs: the same, and a thrown test error on an app screen shows the app's own error panel and sends one scrubbed envelope.

Supersedes: M8-09 step 3's and M5-21's request lists are unchanged on public pages (this feature adds no request there); `.claude/rules/tenant-pages.md`'s rule that tenant pages never import client libraries gains Sentry in its list through the Dependencies section (M9-14). Nothing else.

features.title: Strikethrough, underline and paragraph alignment in text blocks: marks model, Publish form and renderer
acceptance: Schema (extends M6-28; `src/lib/document/marks.ts`): the text block's `marks` list gains `{type:'strike', start, end}`, `{type:'underline', start, end}` and `{type:'align', start, end, align:'left'|'center'|'right'}`, with the same code point offsets into the trimmed text as bold, italic and link. An `align` mark covers exactly one paragraph, meaning one line of `text` (the text between two line breaks): `start` is 0 or just after a `\n`, `end` is the text's length or just before a `\n`. No mark means 'follow the page's alignment'; an explicit `left`, `center` or `right` overrides it for that paragraph. Limits: `LIMITS.textMarks` stays 30 and counts the inline marks (bold, italic, strike, underline, link; at most 10 links as before); align marks are counted by a new `LIMITS.textAligns` of 20; the 600 code point text limit and the 256 KB draft cap are unchanged. A text block without the new marks renders and publishes exactly as today.

Draft and Publish rules: the draft schema is lenient about positions and keeps any finite offsets (as M6-28); `publishDocSchema` is strict about each mark (a mark with another `type`, such as `code`, `highlight`, `color` or `font`, fails with 'This text has formatting that can’t be published.'; extra keys such as `style`, `class`, `href` and `color` are stripped; an `align` value other than the three words fails with the same sentence; more than 30 inline marks or 20 align marks fails with 'This text has too much formatting.'); links keep every rule of M6-28 (http or https, at most 10, never overlapping, ids unique across the page). `sortMarks`, `clipMarks`, `textSegments` and `requireMarkRanges` know the new types: order at one position is bold, italic, strike, underline, link, align.

Publish form (`toPublishForm`, Vitest table): the text is trimmed and CRLF becomes LF, and every mark shifts and clips as before (`'  Hello world '` with strike 2 to 7 gives text 'Hello world' and strike 0 to 5; `'a👍b'` with underline 1 to 2 wraps only the emoji); an `align` mark is snapped to the whole line that holds its start (a mark in the middle of a line becomes that whole line), two align marks on one line become one (the later wins), an align mark on an empty line or on trimmed whitespace is dropped, and the result is sorted; two equal drafts give deep-equal publish forms. The stored published form is held to whole numbers inside the text, whole-line aligns that do not overlap, and no overlapping links (`publishedDocSchema`), else the page is the plain 404 with the issues logged (as M8-02).

Renderer (the one shared `TextView`, editor preview, live page and share page): `

` keeps its root and attributes and holds text nodes, ``, ``, ``, `` and ``; overlapping inline marks nest in the order `` and a link wraps whatever it covers (its text is always underlined anyway). When a block has at least one align mark, every line becomes `` (display block; an empty line keeps one line of height) and the line-break characters themselves are not written as text (the spans carry the breaks, so no paragraph gains a blank line: Vitest counts the rendered lines of 'a b c' as four, one of them empty), while `white-space: pre-line` still applies inside a line and an aligned line carries `data-align='left|center|right'`, written from the closed enum, never from the document's string; the CSS sets `text-align` from those attributes, so no `style` attribute and no tenant string reaches the markup. Every piece of text is still a React text node (escaped); the block's title in its row (the first 60 characters of the plain text) is unchanged by marks.

Old documents are unchanged: Vitest `renderToStaticMarkup` of the M2-31 fixture, the Wave G fixture and a text block with only bold, italic and links is byte-identical before and after this feature, in preview and live mode, and the live document of such a page is byte-identical (the `<style>` too: the new text rules are in the text block's CSS and appear only when the page has a text block, as M8-02's selector check requires; two pages with the same block types but different text give a byte-identical `<style>`). The static scans of M2-05 and M6-34 on the CSS (no color literals, no `@media` but prefers-reduced-motion, no `--hl-`) still pass, and a scan finds no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` and no Markdown or HTML parser in package.json.

Escaping and abuse (Vitest, and Playwright with the owner's JWT writing the draft as raw JSON): marks with `type:'underline'` plus `style:'x'`, `align:'center"><script>alert(1)</script>'`, `align:'justify'`, negative, fractional, NaN and past-the-end offsets, 40 inline marks, 25 align marks and an align mark that cuts a line in half are refused or normalized at Publish, never throw in the renderer or the preview, and never reach `pages.published` unnormalized; text `<s>x</s> <u>y</u> **b**` with no marks renders literally (M2-16 holds); a link `url` of `javascript:alert(1)` still fails. A hostile mark in a hidden block does not stop Publish.

Database and links: no migration is needed because `blocked_links_in` reads only `type = 'link'` marks (M6-29): pgTAP stores a draft with strike, underline and align marks without error and still refuses a link mark to a blocked host; `findLinkUrl`, the analytics labels (`linkLabelsFromPublished`) and the blocklist's `urlFieldsOf` ignore the new types (Vitest with a fixture of all five inline types and three aligns plus two links).

Parity: marks survive `toPublishForm` and render the same in the editor preview, the share page and the live page (Vitest in both modes and a Playwright compare of the block's `outerHTML` after Publish, with strike, underline and a centered and a right-aligned paragraph); changing only an alignment flips the chip to 'Unpublished changes'.

At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/ (published fixture: a 600-character text with bold, italic, strike, underline, two links, a centered paragraph, a right-aligned paragraph and a line made of a 200-character unbroken string): the text wraps inside the column (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), the aligned lines' computed `text-align` is 'center' and 'right', `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, every link box is at least 44px tall and every other anchor on the page too.

At 1440x900 on the same URL: the text stays within the 480px column; the centered and right-aligned paragraphs align inside it; strike and underline show (`text-decoration-line` is `line-through` and `underline` on the computed style).

Supersedes: M6-28 step 1 (the mark types are now bold, italic, strike, underline, link and align, with `LIMITS.textAligns`), and its renderer step's 'holds text nodes, `<strong>`, `<em>` and `<a>`' (now also `<s>`, `<u>` and the line spans when an align mark exists). Every other step of M6-28 and M2-16 holds.

features.title: Tiptap rich text editor for text blocks
acceptance: Component: a text block's edit panel replaces the textarea, the 'Bold, Italic, Link' toolbar and `adjustMarks` with one Tiptap editor (`@tiptap/react` 3.31.4 with `@tiptap/starter-kit` and the pinned Underline, Link and TextAlign extensions) in `src/components/blocks/forms`, loaded by a dynamic import when a text block is first expanded (the /editor first load with no text block open fetches no chunk whose name or contents hold 'prosemirror' or 'tiptap'; expanding one fetches it once). The schema allows only `doc > paragraph > text` with the marks bold, italic, strike, underline and link; StarterKit's headings, lists, quotes, code, rules, hard breaks, drop and gap cursors and trailing node are off, and Underline and Link are registered once (the console shows no 'Duplicate extension names' warning). Enter makes a new paragraph, Shift+Enter does the same, and each paragraph is one line of the block's `text` (an empty paragraph is an empty line). Label 'Text' on a `role='textbox'` with `aria-multiline='true'`, the hint and the counter wired with `aria-describedby`, the counter '{n} / 600' counting code points of the text only; focus shows the 2px brass outline; Tab leaves the editor (no tab indentation).

Storage boundary: nothing but the existing structured model is stored (M9-11): two pure functions, `marksToTiptapDoc(text, marks)` and `tiptapDocToTextAndMarks(doc)`, convert at the edge, and `editor.getHTML()`, `generateHTML` and `generateJSON` are never called in application code (a static scan; the draft never holds HTML or Tiptap JSON). Vitest tables, both directions: 'Hello world' with bold 6 to 11; `'a👍b'` with bold 1 to 2 (our offsets count code points, ProseMirror's count UTF-16 units: the emoji is one position for us and two for it); two paragraphs 'One' and 'Two' with 'Two' centered give text 'One\nTwo' and an `align` mark 4 to 7; a blank line between paragraphs; CRLF input; overlapping bold, italic, strike and underline; adjacent equal marks merging into one; a link across a paragraph break coming back as one link mark with one id. The TextAlign extension is configured so its default alignment is not written as a value (the converter treats a paragraph with no explicit alignment as having none, never as 'left'), so `tiptapDocToTextAndMarks` emits an `align` mark only for an alignment the person chose, and a page aligned to the center with one paragraph explicitly set to 'left' round-trips as exactly one `align` mark of 'left'. A seeded property test of 200 random texts and mark sets (including that page-centered block with an explicit 'left' paragraph) proves `tiptapDocToTextAndMarks(marksToTiptapDoc(t, m))` equals `{ text: t, marks: normalized(m) }`. A link keeps its id when its range is edited or extended, and a new link gets a fresh id from `newBlockId`.

Toolbar: the fixed toolbar (`role='toolbar'`, label 'Text formatting', left and right arrow keys move between buttons) holds ten buttons of 44x44 with icons and accessible names: 'Bold', 'Italic', 'Strikethrough', 'Underline', 'Link', 'Align left', 'Align center', 'Align right', 'Undo text change' and 'Redo text change' (the last two are named so they never collide with the workspace's 'Undo' and 'Redo'). Bold, Italic, Strikethrough, Underline and the three alignments use `aria-pressed` for the selection; pressing the active alignment again removes the mark (back to the page's alignment); every button keeps the selection and the focus in the editor (the phone keyboard stays open). Playwright pastes `

Hi x there

` and the draft holds text 'Hi x there' with one bold mark, no link, no dialog event and no `` in the DOM; a drop of the same content behaves the same. features.title: Faster CI: the browser suite runs on a production build over eight shards
acceptance: Workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `e2e`): the matrix becomes `shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]`, the job name 'Browser suite (n/8)', the run step `pnpm test:e2e --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/8`, `fail-fast` stays false, and the header comment (4 runners becomes 8) is updated. The `verify` job, the integration step's `--retry 2` and the triggers (nightly, manual, the `full-ci` label) are unchanged.

Production build per shard: after 'Write .env.local' each shard runs `pnpm build` once with `NEXT_PUBLIC_ROOT_DOMAIN=localhost:3000` and `HYDLNK_QUERY_COUNTER=1` (the same values `.env.local` and the start step use, because the root domain is baked into the build) and Playwright then serves the app with `next start -p 3000` instead of `next dev`. The server is the built one: the shard's step names it, a failed build fails the shard before any test runs, and a Next build cache (`actions/cache` over `.next/cache`, keyed on the lockfile and a hash of `src/**` with a restore key on the lockfile) is added so a rebuild reuses compiled output.

Playwright config: `playwright.config.ts` chooses the web server from one pure function in `scripts/lib/e2e-server.ts` (Vitest): with `CI` and `HL_E2E_SERVER=start` it is `./node_modules/.bin/next start -p {port}` with `reuseExistingServer: false` and a 120 second timeout; in every other case (local runs, any shell without the variable) it is exactly today's `pnpm dev --port {port}` with `reuseExistingServer: true` and today's timeouts. `HL_DEV_PORT`, the Vercel stub server entry, the two projects (phone 390x844, desktop 1440x900), `retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0` and `playwright.prod.config.ts` are unchanged. `playwright test --list` lists the same number of tests under both servers.

Cache and test-hook behavior on a production build: the specs that need a production build keep passing in the main suite and the production-only rows stay gated on `HL_PROD_PORT` as today; the `HYDLNK_QUERY_COUNTER` hooks work because `VERCEL_ENV` is unset on the runner (M8 security note); anything in the suite that relied on `next dev` behavior (compile-on-demand, the dev overlay, `/_next/webpack` paths, dev-only warnings) is fixed in the spec, not by skipping it. The suite's passed and skipped counts per shard are posted with the result.

The existing production cache-check step (M2-26, M4-08, M4-19, M5-08, M8-04, M8-09, M8-10, M8-11) keeps its behavior on shard 1: the same specs run against a production server with the same three start variants (default, `PAID_PLANS_OPEN=false`, `HYDLNK_QUERY_COUNTER=0`). Its servers need `localhost:3100` baked in, so where the suite's build can serve them (the specs accept `HL_PROD_PORT=3000`, same root domain) it reuses that build, and otherwise it builds a second time as today; the workflow comment says which, and the PR comment reports both build times. The publish-bundle test (`tests/unit/publish-bundle.test.ts`) runs on whichever build exists.

Server lifecycle and diagnostics: a start helper waits for `http://localhost:3000/` to answer (60 tries, fails with the server log if the process exits), stops the server with the TERM-then-KILL sequence the cache-check step already uses, and verifies nothing still answers on the port; 'Production server diagnostics' also prints `tmp/start-3000.log`; the Playwright report and traces are uploaded as before; the 'Screenshots at 390 and 1440' step on shard 1 still runs `pnpm dev` afterwards and still produces the three screenshot sets.

Measured and reported: label PR #21 `full-ci` (or run the workflow manually) once after the change and post one PR comment with: the previous full run's wall time (run 37182342186: total and slowest shard), the new run's total and slowest shard, the build time per shard, the install time, the number of tests passed, skipped and failed per shard, and the cost in runner minutes before and after. The target is that the slowest shard takes at most 60% of the previous slowest; if it does not, the comment says so with the numbers and names the next lever. No secret is added, no action but `actions/cache` joins the workflow, and every `uses:` is pinned like the existing ones.

Docs: CLAUDE.md's Commands and Git workflow lines and the workflow header say the browser suite runs against a production build in CI and `next dev` locally; docs/PLAN.md's CI paragraph says the same. No product behavior changes: `pnpm verify` is green and the PROGRESS.md entry holds the two wall times.

At 1440x900 (the suite's desktop project) every shard passes the same specs as before on the production build, and the screenshots artifact still holds the desktop images of /, the app host and mara.

features.title: Dependencies section in CLAUDE.md, with tests that hold the rules
acceptance: CLAUDE.md gains a short '## Dependencies' section (after 'Invariants') with these rules, one line each: (1) client libraries only on the app and editor side; public tenant pages (the static HTML pipeline in `src/lib/tenant-render/` and the one tenant script) never ship library JavaScript, and a library may be used there only at server render to produce static markup (for example Simple Icons SVG paths); (2) no library makes network calls (no telemetry, no CDN, no remote fonts, icons, images or schemas), the one Gary-approved exception being Sentry on the app side, off unless its DSN is set; (3) permissive licenses only (MIT, ISC, BSD, Apache-2.0, CC0-1.0, 0BSD, OFL for fonts); (4) exact pinned versions, no `^` or `~`; (5) a new library needs Gary's approval in chat before it is installed; (6) the approved list: runtime dependencies one per line (name, version, what it is for) and dev dependencies together on one line (every runtime and dev dependency in package.json, including lucide-react 1.51.0, simple-icons 16.34.0, @radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu 2.1.24 and @radix-ui/react-dialog 1.1.23 (only these two Radix components), react-colorful 5.8.1, react-easy-crop 6.2.3, react-email 6.11.0, clsx 2.1.1, tailwind-merge 3.7.0, @sentry/nextjs 11.4.0, and @tiptap/react, @tiptap/pm, @tiptap/starter-kit, @tiptap/extension-underline, @tiptap/extension-link and @tiptap/extension-text-align at 3.31.4).

`tests/unit/dependencies-policy.test.ts` holds it: (a) the section exists and the names in its list equal the names in package.json `dependencies` and `devDependencies` in both directions (adding a package without updating the list fails the test, and the failure message names CLAUDE.md); (b) every version in package.json matches `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` (no ranges, no tags, no `workspace:`); (c) every direct dependency's `license` field read from `node_modules/<name>/package.json` is in the allowlist above (an SPDX expression passes when one alternative is on the list; a package with no license or a copyleft one fails and is named), and the test prints the licenses of transitive packages outside the list for review, naming sharp's prebuilt libvips binaries (LGPL, dynamically linked, already in use) as the one known and accepted exception; (d) no source file under `src` contains a remote library or font URL (`cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com`, `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `fonts.googleapis.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com`), except `scripts/vendor-tenant-fonts.mts` which lives outside `src`.

Module-graph scan, the tenant boundary: starting from the two tenant route files and from every file under `src/lib/tenant-render`, `src/lib/tenant-assets` and `src/components/page`, the reachable imports of packages are a subset of a short allowlist inside the test (react, react-dom as Next ships it, next/server types, zod, simple-icons, and the other server-render-only packages that are already there); none of lucide-react, `@radix-ui/*`, react-colorful, react-easy-crop, `@tiptap/*`, `@sentry/*`, react-email, clsx, tailwind-merge, nodemailer or sharp is reachable, no reachable file has a `'use client'` directive (M8-02 (a)), and `src/lib/tenant-assets/script/tenant.js` has no `import`, `require`, `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `eval` or `innerHTML` (M8-05) and stays within its size limits.

Marketing boundary: `src/app/(marketing)` and `src/components/marketing` reach none of the client libraries of rule 1 that the app side owns (Radix, react-colorful, react-easy-crop, Tiptap, Sentry, react-email, lucide-react), except the ones the marketing pages already use today; the allowed set is listed in the test with a one-line reason each and a new entry needs a code change that Gary reviews.

Docs match: `.claude/rules/tenant-pages.md` gets one line pointing to the section ('Libraries on tenant pages: see CLAUDE.md, Dependencies'), docs/PLAN.md's decided-list gets the same five rules in one paragraph, and the PROGRESS.md entry lists the approved libraries with the date of Gary's approval (2026-10-04).

features.title: Wave K document contract: new fields, link targets, blocklist and ids in one place
acceptance: The contract the other Wave K features share (Zod, in `src/lib/document`; every new key is optional so `version` stays 1 and an older document parses and publishes unchanged). New block types, appended to `BLOCK_TYPES` in this order after the nine original ones: `faq` `{items:[{id, question, answer}]}`; `contact` `{name, phone, email, hours}`; `discount` `{code, description, url}` (its link id is the block's id); `book` `{title, author, cover: imageRef|null, links:[{id, store:'amazon'|'apple'|'bookshop', url}]}`; `apps` `{links:[{id, store:'appstore'|'googleplay', url}]}`; `map` `{name, address, googleId, appleId}`. New page-level keys of the document: `banner` `{id, visible, text, label, url}`; `utm` `{source, medium, campaign}`; `redirect` `{linkId}`; and on `profile`: `logo` (an image reference or null), `logoPlacement` ('beside' or 'instead', default 'beside'), `nameFont` (a font family from the allowlist or absent) and `nameSize` ('small', 'medium', 'large', 'xlarge', default 'medium'). New per-link keys on a link block: `utm` `{source, medium, campaign, off}` and `lock` (`{kind:'age'}` or `{kind:'code', salt, hash}`). Limits live in `LIMITS` (faq items 10, question 120, answer 600; contact name 60, phone 30, hours 160; discount code 32, description 100; book title 80, author 60, 3 links; apps 2 links; map name 60, address 160; banner text 100, label 30; utm value 40; code lock 4 to 32). Each feature spec owns its fields' rules; this one owns the plumbing below.

Unique ids: `requireUniqueIds` also checks the new ids (faq item ids, book and apps link ids, the map's `googleId` and `appleId`, the banner's `id`), so 'Ids must be unique within a page.' names the second holder; ids are made with `newBlockId`, follow the block id rule, and are never reused. Vitest table with a clash for each new id source, a clash between a map id and a link block id, and a duplicate between the banner and a block.

Click targets (`findLinkUrl`, pure, `src/lib/analytics/ingest/target.ts`): from the PUBLISHED document only, `findLinkUrl` resolves a discount block's id to its `url` (when non-empty), a book or apps link's id to its `url`, the banner's id to `banner.url`, the map's two ids to targets built by one pure function `mapTargets`: `https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query={encodeURIComponent(name + ' ' + address)}` and `https://maps.apple.com/?q={encodeURIComponent(name + ' ' + address)}` (fixed host, https, ASCII), and a `redirect` is never resolved by id (it is read by the page route, M9-31). Every target must still pass `isHttpUrl`. Vitest and Playwright: GET /r/<pageId>/<id> for each new id answers 302 with `Location` exactly the published URL (the map's exactly the built one), `Cache-Control: no-store`, no `Set-Cookie`, one `events` click row with `block_id` equal to the id; an id that exists only in the draft, in a hidden block, in another page or whose block type has no target (a faq item id, the contact block's id, a discount block with an empty `url`) answers 404 and inserts nothing; M4-22's open-redirect parameters never change `Location`.

Blocklist, save time: a new migration (db-change skill, `create or replace`, same signature, grants and security settings, no committed migration edited) makes `public.blocked_links_in` also read `links[]` of a block (the `url` of every `book` and `apps` link, reporting its id as `item_id`) and the document's top-level `banner.url` (reported with `block_id` 'banner' and `item_id` the banner id); a discount block's `url` is already read as a block `url`. The 600-URL scan cap, the 200-block cap and the 256 KB cap still bound the cost. pgTAP (extending the M5-03 and M6-29 files): for each new field a listed host fails the save with `blocked_link` (HL005, host in the detail, ids in the hint) and an unlisted host passes, the M5-03 spellings fixture holds for them, and a draft with 700 book links is refused or bounded within 2 seconds. `media_image_paths` needs no migration (it scans the whole document for image paths): pgTAP proves a book cover path and a logo path that only a draft names are kept by the cleanup (M5-14) and found when dropped.

Blocklist, application: the draft-side `urlFieldsOf` (used by `blockedFieldErrors` and `blockedPublishErrorHolds`) and the published-form `urlFieldsOf` in `blockedLinksInPublished` include the discount `url`, every book and apps link, the banner, and (as a defense) the map's two derived targets, with the same `blockId`, `itemId` and `field` shape, so Publish refuses a blocked link in any new field with `blocked_link` and one error per link naming its host, `pages.published` and `published_at` unchanged and `updateTag` never called; the admin impact count (`admin_blocked_domain_impact`, M7-12) counts pages whose published form links a domain through any new field (Vitest with a fixture holding all of them). The editor shows 'That site is blocked. Use a different link.' under the exact field (Shop link, a store's row, the banner link) and keeps Publish off while it stands (M5-03).

Analytics labels (`linkLabelsFromPublished`): 'Clicks by link' names a discount link 'Discount {code}', a book link '{title} on Amazon' (or 'Apple Books', 'Bookshop.org'), an apps link 'App Store' or 'Google Play', the map's links 'Map: Google Maps' and 'Map: Apple Maps', the banner link 'Banner: {label}', and a vCard save 'Save contact: {name}' (M9-18), each cut to 60 characters; a removed one reads 'Removed link' after a republish (M4-27). Vitest table over all of them.

Per-type tables are complete: a Vitest iterates `BLOCK_TYPES` and fails when any of these has no entry for a type: `BLOCK_TYPE_LABELS`, the add-block chips, `blockDefaults`, the `toPublishForm` case, `STYLE_SPECS` (the editor's style controls), the block row's summary (`summary.ts`), the analytics labels, `describeTemplate`'s plural words ('faqs', 'contacts', 'discounts', 'books', 'apps', 'maps'), and the renderer registry; `BLOCK_TYPES` is exactly the nine originals in their order followed by `faq, contact, discount, book, apps, map` in that order (the test checks the list is that list truncated to the types that exist so far, so each block feature can land alone).

Draft and share safety: the share page (M6-10) and the owner's preview never expose a lock's `salt` or `hash` (the function that builds the share payload strips them: Vitest with a fixture holding a lock) and never draw a locked link with an `href`; the draft cap of 256 KB (M2-04) still binds the whole document with all new fields; `publishedDocSchema` strips unknown keys, so a key this version does not know never reaches `pages.published`, and a stored document with a block type this version does not know still renders the rest of the page (M8-02).

Abuse cases through the publishable key and the owner's JWT, written as raw JSON: a `book` link with `store:'evil'`, a third `apps` link, a map with `googleId` equal to its `appleId`, a banner `url` of `javascript:alert(1)`, a `redirect.linkId` that names a hidden block, a card or nothing, a `utm` value with a line break or `&`, `nameSize:'huge'` and a `lock` with a 5,000-character `hash` are each refused or stripped at Publish with the field named, never reach `pages.published` and never render on http://mara.localhost:3000/; a hidden block holding bad new fields does not stop Publish.

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor with a page that holds one block of each new type and every page-level key: the editor, the preview and the share page open without an error, `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, and every button, input and standalone link is at least 44px tall (the controls themselves are specified by each feature).
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the same page opens without an error and the preview matches the live page after Publish (M2-31's parity pattern over the fifteen types).

Supersedes: M2-01 step 1's 'exactly nine types' (now the nine originals then faq, contact, discount, book, apps and map), M2-10 steps 1 and 6 ('nine chips in this order' and 'all nine chips fit in at most two rows': now fifteen chips in the order of `BLOCK_TYPES`, at most three rows at 1440x900, wrapping on a phone), M6-04's 'nine type chips in the order of M2-10' (the inline chooser shows the same fifteen), and M4-22's 'Location exactly the published URL' only for the map's built targets and, with M9-27, for a link that gets UTM tags. M2-12 and M6-05 'all nine block types' now run over every type in `BLOCK_TYPES`.

features.title: FAQ block: questions and answers that open without JavaScript, with FAQPage data
acceptance: Schema (the `faq` type of M9-15, the add-block-type checklist): `{type:'faq', id, visible, items:[{id, question, answer}], overrides?}` with 1 to 10 items. `question` is one line of at most 120 code points ('Add a question.' when empty at Publish), `answer` is at most 600 code points with line breaks kept ('Add an answer.'), both with the control-character and bidi rules of `text()`; 0 items fails with 'Add at least one question.' and an 11th with 'Use up to 10 questions.'. The draft is lenient, a hidden block is dropped at Publish, `toPublishForm` trims, turns CRLF into LF and drops unknown keys, and the new limits are in `LIMITS`. Vitest table: 0, 1, 10 and 11 items, a 121-character question, a 601-character answer, a control character in a question, an extra key such as `open` or `html` (stripped), and a missing item id.

Renderer (one component shared by the editor preview, the live page and the share page, `renderToStaticMarkup` parity in both modes): `
` holds one `
{question}

{answer}

` per item. All items start closed and every answer is in the HTML while closed. No JavaScript is involved: the native disclosure opens and closes on a tap, Enter or Space. The summary is at least 44px tall with its marker drawn by CSS from `--t-*` colors (no image, no icon font), a 2px `--t-accent` focus ring, and the answer uses `white-space: pre-line` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere`. Every piece of text is a React text node (escaped); the block reads only `--t-*` variables and `blockTokens(ctx.tokens, block.overrides)` on its root; no `--hl-*` and no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Answers carry no marks or links (plain text; a web address in an answer is not made a link).

No-JavaScript proof (Playwright with `javaScriptEnabled: false` at both viewports): the page shows every question; a tap, Enter and Space on a summary set `open` on that `<details>` and show its answer, a second one closes it, opening one leaves the others as they are, and nothing is requested (network log).

FAQPage data: the live document of a page with at least one visible FAQ block carries one `<script type='application/ld+json'>` in the head (page level, never one per block) holding `{'@context':'https://schema.org','@type':'FAQPage','mainEntity':[{'@type':'Question','name':question,'acceptedAnswer':{'@type':'Answer','text':answer}}, ...]}` for the visible FAQ blocks' items in page order, at most 50 questions. It is built by one pure function from the published document, serialized with `JSON.stringify` and then every `<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028 and U+2029 is written as `\u003c`, `\u003e`, `\u0026`, `\u2028`, `\u2029`, so no tenant string can close the element. It is written only in the live static document: not in the editor preview, not in the share page, not in the placeholder or any 404 or error page, not for hidden blocks and not for a draft-only item. features.title: Save contact: a vCard generated on the server from the published block
acceptance: Route: `GET /c/{pageId}/{blockId}` (and HEAD) is served on a page's own hosts (`{handle}.{root}` and its verified custom domains) and nowhere else: the proxy passes `/c/` through unrewritten on those hosts exactly like `/r/` (added next to `isTrackingPath`, pinned by `tests/unit/routing-proxy-matcher.test.ts`), and on the root, app and deployment hosts it is the plain 404 (the handler also checks the real Host header with `hostServesPage`, never `X-Forwarded-Host`). Ids are validated like /r (a UUID and 1 to 64 of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`); the route is `force-dynamic`, so an invented path makes no cache entry (the Wave J rule: Vitest scan and a burst of 50 random `/c/<uuid>/<id>` requests makes no `route-cache` file). Any method but GET and HEAD answers 405 with `Allow: GET, HEAD`.

What it serves: only for a block of type `contact`, visible, in the PUBLISHED document of a page whose owner is not suspended (M5-08), read through the same server-only published read the page uses. A draft-only block, a hidden one, an unknown id, an id of another block type, another page's block and an unpublished page all answer the notice page (HYDLNK style, 404, `no-store`) and insert nothing. The body comes from the stored fields and from nothing the request carries: `?name=`, `?download=`, a different Host header, Referer and cookies never change a byte of the body or the headers (Vitest and Playwright).

The file: 200 `Content-Type: text/vcard; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="{slug}.vcf"` where the slug is the name lower-cased and reduced to `[a-z0-9-]` (1 to 40 characters, 'contact' when nothing is left), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, no `Set-Cookie`. Body: vCard 3.0 with CRLF line endings and lines folded at 75 octets: `BEGIN:VCARD`, `VERSION:3.0`, `FN:{name}`, `N:{family};{given};;;` (the last word is the family name, the rest the given names; one word goes in the family slot), `TEL;TYPE=VOICE:{+digits}` when there is a phone, `EMAIL;TYPE=INTERNET:{email}` when there is an email, `URL:{the page's public address}` (the primary custom domain when one is verified, else the handle host, decided on the server by `getPrimaryDomain`), `NOTE:{hours}` when there are hours, `END:VCARD`. No photo, no other property.

Escaping, one pure function `vcardFor(contact, pageUrl)` (Vitest table): backslash, comma, semicolon and line breaks inside values are escaped as `\`, `\,`, `\;` and `
`; control characters and bidi controls are removed; a name of `Mara
TEL:+1999
END:VCARD
BEGIN:VCARD` and hours of `a;b,c\d` produce exactly one BEGIN and one END and only the property names above (the test splits the output into lines, unfolds them and checks every name against the allowlist); a 300-character hours value folds correctly and unfolds to the original; the filename slug never contains a quote, a semicolon, a space, a path separator or a non-ASCII character.

Counting and limits: a GET that is a navigation (`Sec-Fetch-Dest` absent, 'document' or 'empty' for a download) and not from a bot inserts one `events` row of type 'click' with `block_id` equal to the contact block's id after the response is sent (never for HEAD or bots, M4-23); 'Clicks by link' names it 'Save contact: {name}'. The route uses the click limiter family: more than 30 downloads in a minute from one client answers 429 with `Retry-After` and the notice page; a limiter failure lets the request through (a vCard is public data). A failing insert never reaches the visitor.

Playwright at 390x844 and 1440x900 on http://mara.localhost:3000/ with a published contact block: pressing 'Save contact' (also with JavaScript disabled) starts a download named `{slug}.vcf` whose content parses with the rules above and equals the stored fields; the anchor is a relative `/c/<pageId>/<blockId>` href with `download`; the live page's HTML contains no phone or email beyond the block's own anchors. On a verified custom host (the M4-09 fixture) the `URL:` line is the custom domain.
At 390x844 on the notice pages of /c/ (404 and 429): the message wraps, the 'Go to hydlnk.com' link is at least 44px tall, and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`.
At 1440x900 on the same notice pages: centered and at most 440px wide, as the existing /r notices.

Supersedes: M4-09 step 4's list of what lives on a page's own hosts ('nothing but the page, its image and the tracking routes') gains `/c/`; the proxy's tracking-path list in `.claude/rules/routing.md` gains it. Nothing else.

features.title: Support banner: a short message and link at the top of the page, dismissed without cookies
acceptance: Schema (page level, the `banner` key of M9-15): `{id, visible, text, label, url}`, absent on a page that never set one. When anything is filled in, `text` is required ('Add the message.', at most 100 code points, one line); `label` (at most 30) and `url` (the `url()` rule) are both set or both empty ('Add a label for the link.', 'Enter a full web address, like https://example.com.'), so a message alone is allowed; `visible` false drops the banner at Publish like a hidden block. The draft is lenient; `toPublishForm` trims and omits an empty or hidden banner, so a page that never used it publishes byte-identically to before. Vitest table: a message only, a message and a link, a link without a label, a 101-character message, a `javascript:` url, a control character, `visible:false`.

Renderer (shared, parity in both modes): the first child of `[data-page-root]`, before the profile, is `

{text}

{label} ×
`; the link element exists only when there is a link, and the destination is never in the markup (like every outbound link, M4-22). It is a bar across the page's width (the full viewport at 1440, the column at 390) with its content centered in at most 480px, not sticky, drawn with `--t-surface`, `--t-text`, `--t-border` and `--t-accent` (the link underlined) and no color literal. The text is a React text node. The dismiss anchor and the link are each at least 44px tall.

The fragment anchor is the one same-page anchor tenant pages may hold: the anchor scans of M2-22 and M4-22 (every anchor is `/r/...`, `mailto:`, `tel:`, `/c/...` or this fragment) pass.

The link: it goes through `/r/<pageId>/<banner id>`, is counted ('Clicks by link' reads 'Banner: {label}'), blocklist-checked at save and at Publish (the banner's url is read by `blocked_links_in` and `urlFieldsOf`, M9-15), and answers 404 once the banner is removed and the page republished. Hostile values (`https://good.example@blocked.example/`, a 4,000-character url, `//evil.example`) are refused with the field named.

Budget (M8-09 holds): a page without a banner is byte-identical to before; a page with one makes the same requests to its own host and none to a third party; the banner's CSS is in `<style>` only when the page has a banner (the M8-02 selector check); the layout-shift sum of a first visit is at most 0.05 (the bar is in the server HTML, so nothing moves after load).

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor the Banner card's controls are at least 44px tall and nothing scrolls sideways.

features.title: Branded QR code: colors, a center logo and a Scan me frame, as PNG and SVG
acceptance: Where: the QR card of the Share tab (M7-04, `qr-card.tsx`) gains a 'Style' group under the code, with every control starting at its default: 'Colors' (a segmented control 'Black and white' (default), 'Page colors', 'Custom'; 'Custom' shows the two color rows 'Code color' and 'Background', each the picker and hex field of M9-07), 'Logo' (a switch 'Add my logo in the center', disabled with the hint 'Add a logo or a photo to your page first.' when the page has neither; the picture is the page's logo, else its photo), 'Frame' (a switch 'Add a frame with text' and a 16px 'Frame text' field, default 'Scan me', at most 20 code points, one line, trimmed, empty means 'Scan me') and a 'Reset style' button. Nothing is stored: the style is view state and resets on reload (decision recorded in PROGRESS.md; no document field). Every control is at least 44px tall and keyboard reachable.

Defaults are M6-31, unchanged: with every control at its default the PNG (1024x1024, black modules on white, quiet zone 4, error correction M) and the SVG (one background `<rect>` and one `<path>`) are byte-identical to what the M6-31 generator writes (Vitest compares the bytes of both), the dialog-free card still encodes only `publicAddress` decided on the server, there is still no input that reaches the encoded string, GET /qr and /api/qr are still 404, and every step of M6-31 and M7-04 about the default code holds.

A pure function `qrColorsOk(code, background)` requires the modules to be darker than the background (inverted codes are refused) and a contrast ratio of at least 4 to 1; otherwise the card says 'These colors may not scan. Use a darker code color on a lighter background.' (`role='status'`) and 'Download PNG' and 'Download SVG' are `aria-disabled` until the colors pass, while the preview still shows them. Logo: with the logo on, the code is made at error correction level H, a plate of the background color covers a centered square of at most 20% of the module grid's side (at most 4% of its area, well under H's 30%), and the picture is drawn inside it with `object-fit: contain`, its aspect kept. The picture is fetched from the page's own media URL (`mediaUrl`, the root `/media` origin) with `crossOrigin='anonymous'`; `/media` already sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (`src/lib/media/serve.ts`), so the canvas is not tainted and `toBlob` returns a PNG (Playwright asserts both downloads work, not that a request was made on the way). The only network request the feature can make is that one image request, once, to the first-party media origin; no third-party request, no upload, nothing sent to the server (network log), and with the logo off the card makes no request at all (M6-31 step 6 holds).

Frame: with the frame on, the code sits inside a rounded border drawn in the code color with the frame text centered below it in bold at least 64px on the 1024px drawing (the PNG is 1024 wide and 1216 tall; the code keeps at least 80% of the width and its quiet zone of 4 modules of background color inside the frame); the text is drawn by the canvas for the PNG and as one SVG `<text>` (generic `sans-serif` family, bold, centered) for the SVG, XML-escaped from the field; the text field cannot grow the drawing (20 characters at most).

features.title: Export analytics as CSV: daily totals and clicks per link
acceptance: Route: `GET /analytics/export?kind=daily|links&range=7|30|90|365` on the app host (`src/app/(editor)/app/(screens)/analytics/export/route.ts`, `force-dynamic`), for the signed-in user's current page only (the same page rule and the same loader as the screen and `/analytics/stats`: the `hl-page` cookie is a preference among their own pages). The query string carries no page, owner or user id, and `?page=`, `?pageId=`, `?owner=` and `?user=` are ignored (a Playwright run as user B with user A's page id gets B's own data). Signed out is 401 JSON, never a redirect; any method but GET is 405; an unknown `kind` is 400; `range` goes through `parseRange` (anything else is 30). A Free account asking for 90 or 365 gets 403 `{ok:false,error:'plan_required'}` and no data, exactly like the stats route (the plan limit is enforced on the server by `analyticsHistoryDays`, never only in the UI); a Pro or Studio account gets every range. More than 20 exports a minute from one user answers 429 with `Retry-After` (the limiter failing lets it through).

Files: 200 with `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="{handle}-{kind}-{start}-to-{end}.csv"` (handle `[a-z0-9-]`, dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, UTC, the range's own start and end), `Cache-Control: no-store`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, no `Set-Cookie`. The body starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark, uses CRLF line endings, a header row and RFC 4180 quoting (a cell with a comma, quote, CR or LF is wrapped in quotes and its quotes are doubled). `kind=daily`: `date,views,clicks,uniques`, one row per UTC day of the range in ascending order, zero days included, from the same page-level `daily_stats` rows and the same freshness rule as the chart (the screen's numbers and the file agree). `kind=links`: `link_id,link,clicks`, one row per link with at least one click in the range, most clicks first (ties by label), labels from the same function as 'Clicks by link' (a removed link reads 'Removed link').

Agreement with the screen (Playwright, a fixture with recorded events at 7, 30 and 90 days): the sum of `views` and of `clicks` in the daily file equals the KPI strip's Views and Clicks for the same range, the number of rows equals the range's days, the daily `uniques` are that day's distinct visitors (not additive across days: the hint below says so), and the sum of `clicks` in the links file equals the table's total; a day with no events is a row of zeros.

Spreadsheet safety (Vitest table over the pure `csvCell`): a cell whose first character is `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return is written with a leading apostrophe, so a link label of `=HYPERLINK("http://evil.example","x")` and `@SUM(1+1)` and `+1-1` and `-2+3` open as text; control characters (U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F to U+009F) and bidi overrides are removed from labels; numbers are written bare; a label with a comma, a quote and a line break round-trips through a CSV parser to the original text. The file name and every header value come from the server (the handle is `[a-z0-9-]`), never from the request.

Screen: below the chart the Analytics screen shows an 'Export this range' row with two plain anchors styled as secondary buttons, 'Download daily totals (CSV)' and 'Download link clicks (CSV)' (`href` to the routes above for the selected range, `download` attribute, 44px; the hrefs follow the range control without a reload) and the hint 'Unique visitors are counted per day, so they do not add up across days.'. While the screen shows sample numbers, or the page is not published, the two controls are disabled `<button>`s with the hint 'Export is available once your page has real data.'; a Free account on 90d or 1y sees the locked state of M5-17 and no export row for those ranges. No menu component is used (no new Radix component). The anchors are keyboard activatable, announce their filename types to assistive technology through their names, and the download starts with a single click or Enter.

No new data exposure: the route reads with the signed-in user's own session or the same server-side loader the stats route uses (which checks ownership of the page before reading), RLS on `daily_stats` still decides what a user's JWT can read (the Free window of 30 UTC days), a user cannot export another user's page by any parameter, and the CSV holds no visitor hash, IP, referrer, device or country (the breakdowns are not exported in this wave).

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/analytics: the export row wraps with the two buttons stacked full width at least 44px tall, the hint wraps, a 60-character handle in a file name does not matter on screen, and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`; a download started with a tap names the file as above.
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the row sits under the chart inside the 720px column with the two buttons side by side, and the screen matches the commit before elsewhere.

features.title: UTM tags added to outgoing links at redirect time
acceptance: Schema (the `utm` keys of M9-15): a page-level `utm` `{source, medium, campaign}` and, on a link block only, `utm` `{source, medium, campaign, off}`. Each value is optional, trimmed, 1 to 40 code points of letters, digits, spaces, dots, hyphens, underscores and tildes ('Use letters, numbers, spaces, dots, dashes and underscores.'); `off` is a boolean; unknown keys are stripped; empty values and an all-empty object are omitted by `toPublishForm`, so a page that never sets one publishes byte-identically to before. The draft is lenient (any string up to 100 characters); Publish refuses a bad value with the field named. Vitest table: valid values, `a&utm_medium=x`, `a=b`, a value with a line break, tab, `#`, `?` or `%`, a 41-character value, an empty string, `off:'yes'`, and a `utm` on a card or a social icon (stripped).

The rule, one pure function `withUtm(target, pageUtm, linkUtm)` (Vitest table of at least 14 URL cases): only for an http or https target (anything else, and an unparseable value, comes back unchanged); for each of `utm_source`, `utm_medium` and `utm_campaign` the value is the link's own when it has one, else the page default; empty values add nothing; `off` on the link adds nothing at all; a parameter name the destination already carries is left as it is (the owner's own URL wins, and nothing is duplicated); the tags are appended with `URLSearchParams` (percent-encoded, never string concatenation), after the existing query in its original order and before the fragment, so `https://shop.example/p?id=1#top` with source 'hydlnk' becomes `https://shop.example/p?id=1&utm_source=hydlnk#top` and a URL with no query gets `?`; the host, path and fragment are never changed; when the result would be longer than 2048 characters no tag is added. Values are re-checked against the pattern at redirect time (a stored value that fails it is skipped), so a document that bypassed Publish still cannot inject a parameter or a header.

Where it applies: at the click redirect, `GET` and `HEAD /r/<pageId>/<id>` answer 302 with `Location` equal to `locationFor(withUtm(publishedUrl, ...))` for every link the owner typed (link, card, image link, grid cell, social icon, link inside text, discount shop link, book and app store links, the banner link, and the target of redirect mode); never for the map's built targets or the vCard, never for `mailto:` and `tel:` (those links do not pass through /r), and never when the page and the link set nothing (then `Location` is exactly the published URL, as in M4-22). The destination is read from the PUBLISHED document only, nothing from the request (query string, `?utm_source=`, Host, Referer) can change `Location`, the open-redirect parameters of M4-22 still do nothing, the response stays `Cache-Control: no-store` with no `Set-Cookie`, and the click row recorded is unchanged (no UTM value is stored or logged).

Playwright and Vitest end to end on http://mara.localhost:3000/ with a published fixture (page defaults source 'hydlnk', medium 'link-in-bio', campaign 'spring'; one link with its own source 'newsletter', one link with `off`, one link whose URL already has `utm_source=partner`, one social icon, one text link, one mailto icon): `curl -I` on each `/r/` path returns the expected `Location` (the first has the page's medium and campaign and its own source; the second none; the third keeps `utm_source=partner` and adds the other two; the icon and the text link get the page defaults); the mailto icon's href is unchanged; the links' hrefs in the HTML are still `/r/...` with no tag in the markup.

Analytics and blocklist unchanged: 'Clicks by link' is unaffected, the blocklist judges the published URL (a tag cannot change the host), and a page whose links all point at a blocked host still cannot be published (M5-03).

At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/: nothing visible changes (no tag appears in any anchor, `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, every anchor at least 44px tall) and a tap on a link lands on a destination whose query string holds the tags (a stub destination server records it).
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the same checks pass, and the same stub check passes on a verified custom host (the M4-09 fixture).

features.title: UTM controls: page defaults and a per-link override

features.title: Link lock on the server: an age check or a code, decided at /r
acceptance: Schema (the `lock` key of M9-15, on link blocks only): `{kind:'age'}` or `{kind:'code', salt, hash}`, where `salt` is 22 base64url characters (16 bytes) and `hash` 43 (32 bytes), checked by exact patterns; unknown keys are stripped; the draft is lenient (a `code` lock without a `hash` saves), Publish requires the hash ('Set a code for this lock.') and refuses a lock on any block type but a link (a hidden block is dropped as always). The plaintext code is never part of the document. The code is 4 to 32 characters with no whitespace, control or bidi characters ('Use 4 to 32 characters with no spaces.'), normalized (NFKC, trimmed, lower-cased) the same way when it is hashed and when it is checked, so the comparison ignores case.

Hashing, server only: a Server Action `hashLinkCode(code)` (signed-in users only, 20 calls a minute per user, the limiter failing closed through the `failClosed` option below) returns `{salt, hash}` using Node's `scrypt` with a random 16-byte salt (N 16384, r 8, p 1, 32 bytes, base64url); the code is never stored, logged, put in an error message, a Sentry event (M9-10's scrubber drops `code` fields) or an analytics row. Verification uses `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers. Vitest: the same code and salt give the same hash, different salts give different hashes, 'Spring2026' and 'spring2026 ' verify, a wrong code does not, a 33-character code and a code with a space are refused before hashing.

The gate lives in the /r handler (the tenant page's CSP, `form-action 'none'`, and the tenant script are unchanged and know nothing about locks): `GET` and `HEAD /r/<pageId>/<id>` for a locked link of the PUBLISHED document answer `200` with an interstitial HTML document, `no-store`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and a CSP of `default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; form-action 'self'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, in the HYDLNK notice-page style with no tenant text in it. An age lock says 'This link may contain sensitive content.' and 'Continue?' with a 'Continue' button and a 'Go back' link to `/`; a code lock says 'This link is locked.' and 'Enter the code to continue.' with a 'Code' field (`type='text'`, `autocomplete='off'`, `autocapitalize='off'`, `spellcheck='false'`, 16px, 44px) and 'Continue' and 'Go back'. HEAD returns the same status and headers with no body. No `Location` header, no destination and no destination host appears anywhere in the page HTML, in this interstitial, in any header or in any failure response (Playwright and Vitest search every response body and header of the flow for the destination's host).

Passing: `POST /r/<pageId>/<id>` (only `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, body at most 1 KB: 415 and 413 otherwise) with `confirm=1` for an age lock, or `code=...` for a code lock, answers `303` with `Location` exactly the published URL (with UTM tags, M9-27), `Cache-Control: no-store`, no `Set-Cookie` (no unlock is remembered: every visit asks again), and then records one `events` click row with `block_id` the link id (never for the interstitial, a wrong code, HEAD or a bot). A GET with `?code=` or `?confirm=1` is ignored (the interstitial is shown: a code is accepted from the POST body only, so it never lands in a URL, a log or the history). A POST for an unlocked link answers 405 `Allow: GET, HEAD`, for an unknown, draft-only, hidden or foreign id 404, and for a suspended owner's page 404 (M5-08).

Wrong or missing code: `403` with the same interstitial and 'That code didn’t match. Try again.' (a missing field is `400` with 'Enter the code.'), `no-store`, nothing recorded. Rate limits through the one limiter (`rateLimit`): 5 code attempts a minute per client per link and 20 per ten minutes per client in all (the client key as for clicks); beyond them `429` with `Retry-After` and 'Too many tries. Wait a minute and try again.', and the correct code is refused too while limited. `rateLimit` fails open by design (src/lib/rate-limit/index.ts) and every other caller keeps that; it gains one option, `failClosed: true`, used only by the lock check and `hashLinkCode`, under which a store error or a timeout returns `{ allowed: false, retryAfter: 1, failed: true }` instead of allowing the request (Vitest with a throwing store and with a store that never answers, for both options, and a scan that only these two callers pass it). For locks, when `failed` is true the answer is `503` with 'This link can’t be opened right now. Try again in a moment.' and no check is made. Playwright: 6 wrong attempts in a row end in 429; waiting out the window allows the correct code; 20 parallel wrong attempts evaluate at most 5.

Cross-site and abuse: a POST whose `Origin` header is present and not the request's own origin, or whose `Sec-Fetch-Site` is `cross-site`, answers `403` before any check (an attacker's page cannot make visitors' browsers guess codes); the `Host` header must pass `hostServesPage` (a victim's custom domain or another tenant's host gets the 404 notice); nothing from the request chooses the destination (the open-redirect parameters of M4-22 do nothing); a link preview bot or a prefetch that GETs a locked link sees only the interstitial and never the destination; the `salt` and `hash` appear in no response (the page HTML, the interstitial, the share page, the preview, the OG image), in no log line and in no analytics row (a Vitest scan of the published page HTML for a fixture's salt and hash finds nothing).

Draft and share safety: a locked link in the editor preview, the share page and thumbnails draws the lock marker and no `href` (so the private share link cannot be used to bypass the lock), the share payload strips every `lock` hash and salt, and `pages.published` holds a lock only after Publish. A lock on a link that is the target of redirect mode is refused there (M9-31).

At 390x844 on http://mara.localhost:3000/r/<pageId>/<id> (age and code interstitials, with and without an error): the card is centered, text wraps, the field, 'Continue' and 'Go back' are each at least 44px tall, `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`, and the on-screen keyboard does not hide 'Continue' (the card scrolls).
At 1440x900 on the same URL: the card is centered and at most 440px wide, like the existing /r notices.

Supersedes: M4-22 step 1's 'GET answers 302 to the link's URL' for a locked link (it answers the interstitial until the check passes) and its 'POST is not allowed' where it is stated (POST is allowed only for a locked link); M4-23's bot rule holds for the POST. Nothing else.

features.title: Lock a link in the editor, and the lock mark on the public page
acceptance: Editor control: the expanded panel of a link block gets a 'Lock this link' group (under 'Link tags') with a select 'Not locked', 'Age check' and 'Code' (16px, 44px). 'Age check' needs nothing else. 'Code' shows a 'Code' field (`type='text'`, 16px, 44px, placeholder 'Choose a code', counter '{n} / 32') and a 'Set code' button (secondary, 44px) that calls `hashLinkCode` (M9-29) and writes `{kind:'code', salt, hash}` into the draft; afterwards the group says 'A code is set. Enter a new one to change it.' (the code can never be shown again) with 'Remove lock' (44px). Errors: 'Use 4 to 32 characters with no spaces.' inline, 'Couldn’t set the code. Try again.' with Retry when the action fails, and a Publish error 'Set a code for this lock.' under the field with focus. The row gets a mono 11px chip 'Locked' (hidden below 760px like the other chips). Available on every plan.

The code stays out of everything but the one call: Playwright's network log shows the plaintext code only in the single Server Action request and in no draft PATCH, no undo state, no console message and no DOM attribute after the field is cleared; the autosave PATCH carries the salt and hash only; Undo and Redo move the lock like any field (one step per change, M6-07) without ever holding the plaintext; a draft written with a code lock and no hash saves and fails at Publish.

Public marker (the shared link renderer, parity in both modes): a locked link keeps its `href='/r/<pageId>/<id>'` on the live page and gains `data-locked='age'` or `data-locked='code'`, an outline lock glyph (inline `<svg>`, 16px, `aria-hidden`, `currentColor`, at the end edge of the button, not Lucide: the static pipeline ships no library client code) and visually hidden text ' (sensitive content)' or ' (locked)' so the accessible name is the label plus that text; the destination and the lock's salt and hash are never in the markup (Vitest scans the HTML of a fixture page). In the editor preview, the share page and thumbnails the same link has the marker and no `href` (inert). A page with no locked link is byte-identical to before (the CSS for the marker is in `<style>` only when a locked link exists).

Flow (Playwright at both viewports, the live page then /r): a visitor taps a locked link, sees the interstitial of M9-29, passes it and lands on the destination (a stub server); with JavaScript disabled the whole flow works (the interstitial is plain HTML with a form); the click is counted once, on success.

Escaping and abuse: a label of `` on a locked link renders as text next to the glyph; a `lock` written through the publishable key with a 5,000-character `hash`, `kind:'pin'` or on a card block is refused at Publish with the field named and never reaches `pages.published`; a stored lock whose hash fails the shape pattern is never treated as 'unlocked' by the handler (it answers the 503 notice rather than redirecting), so tampering cannot open a link.
Redirect mode interplay: the target picker of M9-32 does not list locked links, and the Publish gate refuses a locked target ('Pick a link that isn’t locked.').

At 390x844 on http://app.localhost:3000/editor: the group's select, field, 'Set code' and 'Remove lock' are at least 44px tall with 16px text, the status text wraps, `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`; on http://mara.localhost:3000/ a locked link with an 80-character label keeps its glyph at the end edge without overlapping the text and is at least 44px tall.
At 1440x900 on the same URLs: the group sits inside the expanded link block's 720px column, and the locked link stays within the 480px page column with its label centered in the space left.
